title: Start Here
text: A source-grounded guide to Mailloop, from first sign-in to the delivery boundary. The 30-second pitch Mailloop helps job seekers send personalized cold emails through their own Gmail account. A template and selected contacts become a campaign, with one separate message per recipient. The app adds contact management, PDF attachments, usage controls and Premium billing. This handbook documents a dated source snapshot. It does not establish observed production behavior, Google verification, customer outcomes, or interview mastery. Start with Architecture, trace Sending, then use Walkthroughs to rehearse an explanation. The two-minute pitch A signed-in user prepares contacts and a template in a Next.js interface. Server actions validate ownership, effective access and capacity, then atomically create campaign snapshots and usage reservations in PostgreSQL. After commit, the dispatcher publishes individual send events to Inngest. The worker prepares Gmail credentials and MIME outside database locks, then checks fresh controls and claims one delivery. Acceptance confirms usage. An ambiguous submission becomes UNCERTAIN, retains accounting and blocks automatic resend. Dodo webhooks and scheduled provider reconciliation maintain subscription observations; entitlements decide what the user can do now. Read the current limits With paid gating enabled, Free allows 3 recipients per campaign, 3 emails per UTC day and 15 per month. Premium allows 10 recipients per campaign, 20 per UTC day and 300 per allowance period. PAID is the internal enum; Premium is the public label. A 15-recipient request fails campaignSchema, whose array maximum is 10. A Free request containing 4 valid recipients passes that schema but fails the plan-specific campaign check. Do not describe a 15-message batch as current behavior. A deliberate reading path Learn the nouns first: User, Campaign, Send and UsageReservation. Then trace one successful delivery, one uncertain delivery and one paid upgrade. Finish by explaining what evidence cannot tell you. The source browser preserves source line positions, including visible redactions. Every excerpt is checked against an expected hash. New to the code: Start Here → Architecture → Database → Authentication. Working on sending: Sending → Inngest → Security/Reliability → Walkthroughs. Interview revision: Tradeoffs → Interview Prep → Cheat Sheet. Use the Function/API Reference and source browser to check details rather than memorizing file names.

Finish by explaining what evidence cannot tell you. The source browser preserves source line positions, including visible redactions. Every excerpt is checked against an expected hash.

title: Architecture
text: A modular Next.js application with durable database state and external providers. Runtime boundaries The application uses the App Router, server components, interactive client components, server actions and route handlers. Browser state presents drafts and progress; server code authenticates, validates and owns mutations. PostgreSQL stores durable delivery, usage, billing and recovery state. Inngest orchestrates work. Gmail accepts messages. Dodo provides hosted billing. Private Blob storage holds PDFs in production; development can use local storage. These services cannot participate in one shared transaction. Stack and responsibility Version declarations describe this checkout, not an endorsement of the newest library version. See the dependency ledger for declared and locally installed versions. A package confirms implementation use; it does not prove why its author chose it. Module map src/app contains pages and provider endpoints. src/components holds page-level interactions and reusable UI. src/lib contains policy and business operations. prisma/schema.prisma expresses the current models; migrations record evolution. tests and scripts capture failure contracts, disposable database verification and operator tasks. INFERRED tradeoff: keeping these concerns in one Next.js application reduces the number of deployable units to coordinate. Evidence is co-location and imports, not an architecture decision record promising lower cost. Durability over publication submitCampaign commits campaign and reservation rows before dispatching events. Publication failure is caught; the rows remain discoverable. Reconciliation repairs publication using the same delivery identity with a new dispatch generation. The durable outbox is a pattern: commit the intent locally, then recover publication to another system. It does not make publication and Gmail acceptance atomic.

title: Database
text: Models, constraints, accounting identities and the migration history. The relational core A User owns contacts, templates, campaigns, attachments and usage records. A Campaign selects a template and optionally an attachment; each Send represents one recipient snapshot and its delivery state. The contact relation remains, but recipient and rendered-message fields are stored on Send so later edits do not rewrite the queued message. Contact email uniqueness is per user. Campaign idempotency is scoped to userId. Send.mimeMessageId and UsageReservation.deliveryKey have uniqueness constraints. These constraints complement locking and policy checks. Accounting that survives history deletion UsagePeriod holds daily/monthly counters and period boundaries. UsageReservation holds stable delivery identity, two period references, a status, claim token and lease. Deleting a Send sets its reservation link to null; it does not erase the charge. UsageImportEvidence retains content-free historical evidence. DeliveryReceipt preserves minimal successful-delivery evidence after message-history removal. Its recipient address supports repeat-send checks. History deletion and account deletion are different retention operations. All models and all migrations The schema atlas below covers every model and migration in this snapshot. Read migration SQL before reasoning about old data: additive columns, data backfills and subsequent corrections matter beyond the final schema. Migrations that share a timestamp prefix are distinct directories and both belong to the history. The initialization of SystemControl and later billing binding guards are operationally significant. Local reset scripts intentionally preserve SystemControl and migration metadata. Transactions and owner locks withUsageTransaction serializes an owner’s usage changes with a PostgreSQL row lock. Reservation, claim, confirm and release operations run within that owner context. Period references include user identity to prevent linking a reservation to another tenant’s period. INFERRED tradeoff: per-owner serialization simplifies quota correctness under concurrent submissions but limits throughput for a single owner. The source supplies the locking design, not measured contention or capacity. Billing, administration and deletion records BillingSubscription and CheckoutAttempt can outlive their User relation through SetNull and owner snapshots. BillingWebhookEvent is an inbox keyed by unique webhookId. AdminAuditLog records actor and target snapshots, reason, request identity, and before/after state. AccountDeletionJob deliberately has no User foreign key: recovery must continue after User content is removed. Retained recovery and financial records need their own lifecycle; cascading everything would destroy recovery evidence.

title: Authentication
text: Google consent, manual persistence, JWT sessions and encrypted server credentials. OAuth and session identity OAuth delegates authorization to Google. The normal Google provider requests openid, email, profile and gmail.send with offline access and consent. The signIn callback requires a verified email and Google subject, and checks deletion tombstones. The app selects JWT sessions, meaning the session is backed by a signed/encrypted token managed by Auth.js rather than a session row in this schema. User persistence is manual inside the jwt callback. There is no Prisma adapter configuration in auth.ts. An unrelated existing email owner is never silently linked. What the callbacks persist The jwt callback finds users by googleId, locks an existing user, checks for deletion and rejects unrelated email collisions. It normalizes email, records granted scopes and send-only consent time, and computes gmailAuthorized from the scope plus refresh credential availability. A new refresh token is encrypted with the owner UUID before persistence. If Google omits a refresh token, the existing encrypted value can remain usable. The session callback rechecks User existence and deletion state before exposing a usable session user ID. Encryption and key rotation AES-256-GCM is authenticated encryption: ciphertext includes a tag that detects tampering. The v2 envelope contains version, key ID, random 12-byte IV, tag and ciphertext. Additional authenticated data binds the version, key ID, credential purpose and owner UUID. Copying v2 ciphertext to a different owner fails decryption. Legacy v1 decryption uses TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY; v2 resolves the identified key without falling back. rotateTokenPage scans User credentials and unexpired deletion credentials, defaults to read-only, and applies compare-and-swap updates so a concurrent reconnect wins. Retain old keys for backups until a restore exercise proves retirement safe. Authenticated mutations and fresh admin identity requireUser reads the current session and database owner; missing or deletion-pending users redirect home. Business operations still need entitlement and resource-ownership checks. A UUID alone is not authorization. Admin access uses a distinct Google provider and checks fresh reauthentication for mutations. The restricted admin connection verifies database privileges before allowing operations. Do not equate an isAdmin UI check with this complete boundary. Preparing Gmail without implicit replay gmailForUser decrypts the refresh token on the server, explicitly obtains an access token, then replaces OAuth credentials with that access token only. The returned object exposes only messages.send. This prevents token refresh from silently replaying a rejected send request. Send-only v1 cannot read a mailbox: canReadGmail returns false, and reply-check compatibility functions return disabled/no-op results. Repository files cannot establish Google verification status or provider approval for a production project.

title: Sending
text: From immutable campaign snapshots to a single Gmail submission. Campaign admission submitCampaign authenticates and consumes the campaign rate budget. createCampaign parses input, locks the owner through withUsageTransaction, checks an existing idempotency key, Gmail authorization, controls and plan limits. The transaction checks template ownership and availability, contacts and repeat-send evidence. Already pending or uncertain recipients are skipped; previously successful recipients need explicit resend selection. A duplicate idempotency key returns the existing campaign instead of creating another one. Current-limit batch behavior The schema caps recipientIds at 10 and rejects duplicates. With paidGatingEnabled true, createCampaign additionally enforces 3 recipients for Free or 10 for Premium. Free daily/monthly allowances are 3/15; Premium 20/300. Available capacity can be lower because other reservations already occupy it. With paid gating disabled, client entitlements expose 10 recipients, no monthly limit and the legacy rolling-24-hour cap of 200. The ledger still records state. Do not combine legacy rolling usage with UTC calendar counters as if they were equivalent. Personalization and MIME The allowed placeholders are {{name}}, {{company}} and {{role}}. The campaign stores rendered subject/body, recipient details, template name, message ID and attachment selection. A subject containing newlines after rendering is rejected. MIME is the email wire format. buildMime uses the gmail-mime package alias for Nodemailer MailComposer. It creates text and HTML parts, an explicit Message-ID, and an optional PDF attachment, then base64url-encodes the result. Each message has one To recipient; the code adds no CC or BCC. File and URL fetching are disabled in the composer. Prepare, claim, submit, settle deliverOne first reads current delivery state and performs preflight checks under a short owner lock. It prepares credentials, attachment bytes and MIME outside the lock. It then rechecks fresh controls and entitlement at the final claim; an intervening suspension or quota boundary can still stop delivery. claimUsage moves the reservation into an attempting state and returns a claim token. Only after the final claim commits does messages.send run, with SDK retries disabled. Success records Gmail IDs and confirms accounting. A lease is a temporary exclusive claim, not permission to resend after it expires. Definite failure versus uncertainty Preparation failures and definite provider rejections finish without an automatic sending retry and release appropriate reservations. Credential/domain failures pause the owner; rate limits pause owner or project work according to classification and provider deadlines. Other queued work can be deferred. A timeout, network failure, unknown provider outcome, lost acceptance persistence, or an expired attempting lease may mean Gmail accepted the message. Such work becomes UNCERTAIN, retains accounting and never automatically re-enters READY. A stable MIME Message-ID aids identity; it is not a provider guarantee of deduplication. Pacing and recovery Normal sends are spaced about five seconds apart, and the worker serializes per owner. Pacing waits happen before an attempt; they are not repeat submissions. Queues expire after 24 hours. Deferred publication and eligibility are revisited by hourly reconciliation. Read queue copy carefully: “retries” can mean publishing durable queued work, while the email worker has retries: 0 and never repeats an ambiguous send. Manual reply marking is not delivery reconciliation and does not search Sent mail.

title: Inngest
text: Eight registered functions, durable steps, concurrency and recovery. Registration is the authoritative list /api/inngest exports GET, POST and PUT from serve with exactly eight registered functions. Imports elsewhere do not create a ninth registration. Provider callbacks use the service signature boundary, not a user session. Actual deployed registration and signing configuration require operational verification. All eight functions Cron expressions below are the source schedules, described in UTC in the rollout documentation. Event-driven workers validate UUID data and serialize by user where configured. Steps are durable work boundaries sendEmail uses step.run for each pacing round and step.sleepUntil when it must wait. The function has automatic retries disabled and ends on done, uncertain or deferred. Deferred work is discoverable for future publication. Maintenance discovery pages users inside a step and emits batches of at most 100 owner events. Account maintenance rechecks deletion status, because events can arrive after account state changes. Reconciliation and maintenance Quota reconciliation pages owners, repairs accounting and publication, and turns abandoned claims into uncertainty. Attachment maintenance protects current PDFs and PDFs referenced by queued, attempting or uncertain sends. Physical deletion is marked separately so failure can be retried later. Billing maintenance sweeps lifecycle state, recovers inbox/checkout work every four hours and reconciles at UTC midnight. It skips Vercel previews; it must not be assumed to run merely because the function exists. Why background work exists CONFIRMED tradeoff: the billing schedule comment explicitly cites keeping baseline executions within Inngest Free’s monthly allowance as the reason for a four-hour cadence. That cadence allows recovery delay. It is not an observed service-level guarantee. INFERRED tradeoff: batching cleanup discovery reduces orchestration overhead relative to waking every account individually, while delays and backlog can increase. Measure step/run consumption and provider behavior before estimating capacity. Stale scheduling comments subscription-maintenance.ts still says scheduled maintenance runs each minute. The registered billingMaintenance caller actually invokes the sweep every four hours. Use the endpoint registration and the scheduler implementation for the current trigger; access is also checked at dispatch/final claim, so the periodic sweep is not the only enforcement point.

title: Payments
text: Hosted checkout, signed events, durable receipts and verified entitlement. Explicit test and live environments billingConfig accepts only explicit test_mode or live_mode, requires server credentials/product/business configuration, rejects custom base URL/header overrides, and validates a canonical origin. Live mode requires HTTPS. AGENTS.md and parts of older hardening/test guides describe test-only billing. Current config and docs/dodo-live-rollout.md support both environments. A database is bound to one environment and business; changing environment variables does not convert test objects into live ones. Rollout guards and hosted prices ensureBillingBinding locks SystemControl and binds only a clean unbound database. Existing provider records in an unbound database require review; a mode or business mismatch fails closed. Checkout has a separate billingCheckoutEnabled switch. Turning off new checkout must not stop management and recovery of existing subscriptions. verifyBillingProduct checks a monthly recurring catalog: USD 599 minor units, an India INR 29900 rule, tax inclusive, no trial/add-ons/discounts/PPP, and the expected long subscription term. Hosted quotes and final tax presentation remain provider-dependent and must be verified operationally. Signature verification before storage The webhook route limits the body to 256 KiB and requires webhook-id, webhook-signature and webhook-timestamp. Standard Webhooks verifies the exact raw body with timestamp tolerance before any payload is trusted. Missing/invalid signature returns 401; unavailable configuration returns 503. The route does not use a user session: a valid provider signature authenticates the callback. Never verify reserialized JSON or trust a client return URL as payment evidence. Durable inbox and reconciliation storeBillingEvent validates the business ID, normalizes supported data, hashes the raw payload and upserts by webhookId. Unsupported events can be IGNORED; recognized unusable data is QUARANTINED. Reusing a webhook ID with a different payload hash returns a conflict. After the inbox commits, after() attempts processing. A lost processing opportunity is recoverable from committed state and nextAttemptAt. Lifecycle processing and scheduled reconciliation use server-side provider observations rather than redirect parameters. Financial state is not simply the last browser event. Effective plan is a decision, not a badge getEffectivePlan considers deletion/suspension, active overrides, grandfathering and resolveSubscriptionLifecycle. A valid paid observation requires meaningful provider period boundaries. PAST_DUE grace extends the operational end of the same allowance; it does not mint another allowance. An unresolved active boundary pauses sending. Cancellation at period end can preserve access until the verified deadline. A later downgrade rechecks queued campaigns; whole eligible unsent remainders compete for Free capacity. Attempted and uncertain evidence is not refunded by downgrade. Maintenance and account deletion Recovery scans checkout attempts and webhook receipts; reconciliation refreshes provider observations. Billing maintenance runs every four hours and performs daily reconciliation at midnight UTC. Cancellation, portal and status routes remain authenticated and rate limited. Deletion recovery retains provider IDs and a deadline-limited revocation credential in an independent job so billing cancellation and credential cleanup can progress even after message content is gone. The handbook never performs real billing operations. Portal-host caveat in the current implementation Confirmed code limitation: createBillingPortal validates the returned HTTPS URL against test.customer.dodopayments.com without branching on the configured environment. Checkout URL validation, by comparison, explicitly selects test and live hosts. Externally dependent impact: if a live provider portal URL uses a different hostname, this implementation rejects it with INVALID_PORTAL_URL. The repository cannot prove which URL a live customer receives. Treat live portal verification as an unresolved rollout check; do not claim this snapshot has a verified working live portal.

title: Payments · Effective plan is a decision, not a badge
text: getEffectivePlan considers deletion/suspension, active overrides, grandfathering and resolveSubscriptionLifecycle. A valid paid observation requires meaningful provider period boundaries. PAST_DUE grace extends the operational end of the same allowance; it does not mint another allowance. An unresolved active boundary pauses sending. Cancellation at period end can preserve access until the verified deadline. A later downgrade rechecks queued campaigns; whole eligible unsent remainders compete for Free capacity. Attempted and uncertain evidence is not refunded by downgrade.

title: Payments · Maintenance and account deletion
text: Recovery scans checkout attempts and webhook receipts; reconciliation refreshes provider observations. Billing maintenance runs every four hours and performs daily reconciliation at midnight UTC. Cancellation, portal and status routes remain authenticated and rate limited. The handbook never performs real billing operations.

title: Tradeoffs
text: Separate decision evidence from plausible implementation consequences. Confirmed: conservative sending CONFIRMED: code comments and usage-ledger rollout guidance explicitly state that an expired lease never authorizes a resend and Gmail/database cannot guarantee atomic exactly-once acceptance. The policy retains ambiguous charges and asks the user to check Sent. Benefit: fewer duplicate submissions after unknown outcomes. Cost: a genuinely unsent message can remain unresolved and occupy allowance. Alternative: automatically retry uncertain sends, accepting duplicate risk. The source intentionally chooses the conservative policy. Confirmed: send-only Gmail CONFIRMED: canReadGmail is hardcoded false and the source labels v1 send-only. Restricting the exposed Gmail client to messages.send is explicit. Reply checks return disabled results. Benefit: runtime cannot inspect mailbox content through these paths. Cost: automatic reply/bounce detection and Sent reconciliation are unavailable. Manual reply status remains a user assertion, not observed mailbox evidence. Confirmed: schedule cost versus recovery time CONFIRMED: the billing schedule comment names Inngest Free’s execution allowance as a reason for the four-hour cadence. Daily provider reconciliation runs on the midnight invocation. Benefit: fewer baseline executions. Cost: delayed recovery of missed processing. Do not quote a measured monthly bill or user capacity without running representative traffic and checking provider plans. Inferred: PostgreSQL locking and Prisma INFERRED: relational constraints plus explicit row locks support per-owner correctness while Prisma supplies typed queries. Benefit: campaign and reservation changes can commit together. Cost: contention and transaction complexity. An in-memory counter would be simpler but would not survive multiple processes or restarts. The use of Prisma is confirmed by imports and configuration. The reason it was selected over another ORM is unknown; describe the demonstrated capabilities rather than claiming author motivation. Inferred: one application and hosted services INFERRED: keeping pages, actions, webhook ingress and worker registrations in one codebase makes cross-layer tracing and changes easier. Cost: changes in shared code can affect several execution paths and require coordinated deployment. INFERRED: hosted Dodo checkout avoids building payment collection UI, while adding provider availability, signed-event and reconciliation dependencies. Private Blob storage separates PDF bytes from database metadata, but cleanup becomes a distributed lifecycle. Design comparisons to rehearse Compare JWT sessions with database sessions: current identity tokens carry IDs but callbacks still check database deletion state. Compare queued orchestration with synchronous request sending: background work survives UI navigation but needs publication recovery. Compare snapshots with live template reads: snapshots preserve approved content but retain message data that deletion must explicitly handle.

title: Security / Reliability
text: Existing controls, confirmed limitations and deployment-dependent risks. Authentication is only one boundary Normal mutations authenticate the owner, validate input and scope resource queries by userId. Rate budgets are admitted before business parsing for protected operations. Webhooks authenticate with provider signatures; Blob completion verifies its service callback. Admin mutations add fresh identity, restricted SQL privileges and an audit record. These are implementation controls. They do not prove every deployment has correct secrets, least-privilege grants or provider settings. No penetration test or production audit is claimed here. Confirmed limitations Confirmed limitation: Gmail acceptance and database persistence are not atomic. Unknown outcomes cannot be resolved by mailbox reads because send-only v1 disables them. This can retain usage for a message that did not actually arrive. Confirmed operational gap: automatic operator alert delivery and monitoring jobs were removed in the documented hardening evolution. Safe logs and persisted recovery state remain; operators must arrange observation externally. Do not infer that an alert integration exists. PDF and content safeguards PDF validation enforces a 5 MiB size bound, MIME type and %PDF- prefix. Storage paths are restricted to the owner’s resume prefix, filenames strip control characters, and private Blob reads have timeouts. MailComposer cannot read arbitrary URLs or files. Possible risk: size/type/magic checks do not establish that a PDF is harmless; the shown validation is not a malware scanner. This is a possible content risk, not evidence of an exploit. The actual provider storage configuration is externally dependent. Credentials, logs and key recovery Refresh tokens are encrypted server-side with owner-bound v2 authenticated encryption. Safe logging accepts bounded codes and identifiers instead of raw provider errors, email bodies, addresses or credentials. A key rotation command covers retained deletion credentials too. Externally dependent: key provisioning, backup retention, restore exercises and secret access controls. Encryption does not protect against a fully compromised process that holds both database access and keys. The repository cannot establish actual backup readiness. Rate limits and predictable degradation The database-backed limiter uses rolling windows, row locks, bounded timestamp arrays and database time. Limiter/database failures block protected operations rather than silently admitting them. HTTP routes return 429 with Retry-After or 503; actions return structured failure codes. Provider throttling is separate from the app allowance. Reconnecting Gmail can clear a credential/policy pause but never restores cancelled sends, resets app usage or removes suspension. Test evidence has boundaries Tests cover token envelopes, MIME, usage claims, webhook signatures, deletion, privacy and database migrations. Browser suites exercise themes, plan gates, forms and status views. Test files are evidence of intended contracts; they are not proof those tests currently pass or that production behaves identically. This handbook runs its own static and browser checks without starting Mailloop, touching its database or using any provider credentials. Admin controls and non-recallable work The operator can change a timed plan override, suspend an account and toggle global sending. An override changes app access without mutating provider billing or clearing usage. A Free override requires acknowledgement that billing continues; default overrides expire after 30 days. Suspension cancels proven-unsubmitted READY work and preserves attempting/uncertain evidence. Unsuspension does not reconnect Gmail or restart cancelled sends. The global sending update takes an exclusive control lock that conflicts with final-claim shared locks: subsequent claims see the disable, but an earlier committed claim cannot be recalled. Admin changes require fresh identity, predefined reasons and stable UUID request IDs; successful identical replays return an acknowledgement, conflicting reuse fails. Current admission uses the general limiter before business parsing. Older admin-panel guidance describes a superseded ten-successful-mutations limit and rollback behavior; current code uses 20 admissions/minute and admission survives business rollback. Current request budgets These rolling-window request budgets are distinct from campaign size, email allowance and Gmail provider throttling. Authentication precedes admission; accepted admissions consume capacity even if later parsing or business work fails. Multiple admin/system budgets are checked atomically in a stable lock order.

title: Scaling
text: Bottlenecks, correctness constraints and measurement plans grounded in code. Current concurrency and cost drivers The send function limits concurrency to one per user and normal pacing is about five seconds. Gmail/provider limits, preparation latency, database transactions and scheduled recovery all affect throughput. A five-second interval is a policy constant, not a measured end-to-end rate. The platform may run many owners concurrently, but configured provider/account limits and Inngest capacity are external. Measure database lock waits, provider latency, event delays and uncertain-outcome rate before stating capacity. Database pressure and indexing Owner locks deliberately serialize competing usage operations. Schema indexes support status/availability/lease discovery and tenant queries. Reconciliation and maintenance page by stable IDs; rate-limit cleanup uses SKIP LOCKED with bounded batches. INFERRED tradeoff: more detailed accounting and indexes improve recoverability while increasing write work. Assess execution plans and realistic contention before changing indexes or widening parallelism. Removing owner serialization without a replacement can break quota invariants. Queue backlogs and lifecycle capacity Queues have original expiry deadlines; republishing must not extend them. Hourly recovery introduces visible delay after dispatch failure. Cleanup deletes at most ten obsolete PDFs per owner pass, so large backlogs take multiple passes. Billing recovery and account-deletion recovery have their own state and retry schedules. A useful scaling dashboard would expose oldest READY age, publication delay, expired leases, unresolved UNCERTAIN age, counter drift, cleanup backlog and billing inbox age. This is a proposed measurement plan, not an existing dashboard claim. Safe next steps A proposed load exercise uses disposable PostgreSQL, fake provider responses and representative multi-owner campaigns. Include concurrent submit, lost event publication, a token-preparation delay crossing a quota boundary and a lost acceptance write. Record latency distributions and invariant violations. Do not test production sending capacity by generating real cold email. Any architecture change must preserve stable delivery identity, tenant boundaries, accounting retention and uncertainty semantics. Sharding, partitioning or a dedicated queue are options to evaluate after measuring the actual constraint.

title: Sign in and reconnect Gmail
text: Trace Google identity through callbacks into a usable local owner. 1. Start Google consent The normal provider requests offline access and gmail.send. Identity scopes are separate from sending permission. 2. Validate the incoming profile Require verified email, subject and the expected provider; reject a deletion tombstone or pending deletion. 3. Persist the owner transactionally Resolve by googleId, lock an existing user and reject unrelated email collisions. Encrypt a new refresh token against the owner UUID. 4. Project a session Expose the owner ID only if User still exists and is not deletion-pending. Reauthentication evidence is distinct from normal Google sign-in. 5. Prepare credentials when sending requireUser authenticates business entrypoints. gmailForUser later checks authorization and refresh availability and prepares an access token. title: Deliver one message
text: Follow one queued Send across the non-atomic Gmail boundary. 1. Load state and refuse repeat submission Return immediately for terminal, DONE or UNCERTAIN states. An expired ATTEMPTING lease becomes uncertain rather than ready. 2. Perform preflight Under the owner lock read controls, pauses, expiry, access and accounting readiness. Pacing can wait and capacity can defer before an attempt. 3. Prepare outside the lock Obtain an access token, read the campaign-selected PDF and build MIME. Slow network preparation does not hold the owner lock. 4. Recheck and claim Use a fresh authorization time and controls. claimUsage supplies the token and lease that identify this specific submission. 5. Send exactly one request Call Gmail messages.send with retry false. One To recipient is encoded in the MIME message. This is one submission policy, not a guarantee of exactly-once provider acceptance. 6. Settle the evidence Persist success and confirmUsage; release definite rejection, or retain uncertain accounting. Failed settlement is warned and later reconciled. Supported failure cases Missing credentials or PDF can fail before submission and release the reservation. A definite Gmail rejection finishes without retry. A timeout after submission or acceptance with failed persistence is uncertain, keeps capacity and never auto-resends.

title: Upload and retain a PDF
text: Separate uploaded bytes, activation, campaign references and physical deletion. 1. Choose the storage branch Production uses private Blob storage; non-production without Blob can store local files with restrictive filesystem modes. The upload entrypoint authenticates the user. 2. Verify Blob callback boundaries The client-upload route authenticates token generation and relies on verified Blob completion for the provider callback. Do not apply a user-session requirement to the service completion branch. 3. Validate and activate activateResume reads bytes, validates size/type/header, locks the owner, checks availability and stores/selects attachment metadata. Rejected activation tries to discard the unactivated path. 4. Snapshot the selection createCampaign records the selected attachment ID; the worker reads that selection rather than the owner’s later replacement PDF. 5. Retire only unneeded files cleanupAttachments excludes current PDFs and references from queued, attempting or uncertain work. deletedAt and storageDeletedAt separate logical retirement from completed physical deletion. Supported failure cases An invalid owner path is rejected. Wrong MIME/prefix or oversized PDF fails validation. Suspension/deletion can race with completion and cause discard. Failed physical deletion remains pending; uncertain deliveries can intentionally retain their attachment.

title: Upgrade through hosted checkout
text: Separate a hosted return, a durable webhook and a verified paid entitlement. 1. Authenticate the checkout route The user endpoint validates session/origin and consumes a checkout rate budget before creating a hosted session. 2. Bind mode and verify product Require explicit config, a matching SystemControl business/environment binding, a valid catalog and the checkout enable flag. 3. Record attempt and call provider Checkout uses durable attempts and idempotency. Uncertain provider creation is recoverable; retrying with an unrelated identity can create duplicate commercial work. 4. Verify and commit webhook receipt Verify exact raw bytes, validate business, normalize data and upsert the payload hash by webhookId. Commit before asynchronous processing. 5. Process verified provider observations Lifecycle processing checks provider evidence and updates durable subscription state. Scheduled recovery and reconciliation cover missed processing. 6. Resolve present access The return page displays status; entitlement resolution considers effective plan, valid period, override, suspension and deletion. A redirect alone never grants Premium. Supported failure cases Config/mode binding or catalog mismatch blocks checkout. Invalid signature returns 401; oversized body returns 413. Duplicate identical receipts are idempotent; conflicting webhook ID/hash is 409. Processing outages leave durable recoverable receipts.

title: Delete an account with recovery
text: Understand why the cleanup job outlives User. 1. Confirm owner intent requestAccountDeletion locks the owner and requires the exact account email. The user-facing action authenticates before invoking it. 2. Commit unavailability and recovery state Mark deletionRequestedAt, disable Gmail authorization, increment billing version and create/update the deletion job in the same transaction. 3. Remove the normal credential copy The job retains a deadline-limited encrypted revocation credential; the User credential is cleared. Cancel only eligible queued work; attempted evidence needs draining. 4. Continue external cleanup runDeletionJob coordinates billing cancellation, credential revocation, content and storage cleanup with durable markers/leases. Exact ordering and drain deadlines are in the job source. 5. Discover unfinished jobs The daily sweep expires retained credentials, prepares legacy requests, and emits per-owner deletion events for jobs that are due. The job has no User foreign key so recovery survives content deletion. Supported failure cases Wrong confirmation email is rejected. External billing, storage or revocation failures leave recoverable state rather than pretending cleanup completed. Credential expiry can erase the credential before revocation succeeds; the job records incomplete revocation. Deletion tombstones block immediate Google identity recreation. Drain and independent cleanup stages The drain constant is 15 minutes. A newly requested deletion can attempt billing-only recovery immediately. After the drain, the full worker attempts content purge, storage deletion and Google revocation independently before its billing stage, so a billing outage does not indefinitely block content erasure. The credential retention deadline is 30 days from request, with the daily expiry sweep erasing one sweep interval early. Expired or missing revocation proof is recorded rather than fabricated. Completion requires content, storage, billing cancellation and Google revocation markers; unresolved revocation retains a visible tombstone.

title: What does Mailloop do?
text: It helps job seekers send personalized cold emails through their own Gmail. Contacts and templates become individual per-recipient messages; sending, usage and billing state are durable.

title: What are the current campaign limits?
text: Free: 3 recipients. Premium: 10 recipients. With gating enabled, daily caps are 3/20 and allowances are 15/300. Remaining reservations can reduce available capacity.

title: What happens to a 15-recipient request?
text: campaignSchema rejects it before plan enforcement. Its maximum is the Premium campaign limit of 10. A four-recipient Free request instead reaches the plan-specific check.

title: Is PAID a third product plan?
text: No. PAID is the internal enum for Premium. PLAN_LABELS maps the enum to public copy. Use this distinction when reading database records and UI text.

title: Where does durable truth live?
text: PostgreSQL stores campaigns, sends, usage and recovery state. Inngest events trigger work, but committed queue rows are the durable intent when publication fails.

title: Why not send all mail inside a server action?
text: The implementation commits durable work and dispatches background events. This allows recovery after UI navigation or publication interruption; it adds orchestration and reconciliation complexity.

title: What is the outbox pattern here?
text: Commit the queued intent before publishing an event. submitCampaign catches dispatch failure; later reconciliation repairs publication without replacing the delivery identity.

title: Does package presence explain architectural motivation?
text: No. It establishes implementation use. Label a reason CONFIRMED only when a comment or decision document actually states it; otherwise use INFERRED.

title: Why snapshot recipient and template fields on Send?
text: The queued message retains the approved values. Editing a contact or template later does not rewrite the campaign snapshot. This also creates explicit content-retention duties.

title: What prevents duplicate campaign creation?
text: An owner-scoped idempotency key and a unique constraint. The owner transaction first checks for a previous campaign. Replays return its identity rather than inserting another.

title: Why separate reservations from Send rows?
text: Accounting must survive history deletion. UsageReservation has a stable delivery key and nullable Send link with SetNull behavior, while period evidence remains durable.

title: Why does AccountDeletionJob lack a User foreign key?
text: Recovery must outlive removal of User content. The job retains cleanup markers, deadlines, provider identities and bounded credentials independently.

title: What is a composite ownership constraint?
text: A relation that includes tenant identity as part of its key. Reservation period references use period ID plus userId, preventing cross-owner period association at the schema level.

title: Is deleting history the same as deleting an account?
text: No. History removal preserves safeguards and accounting. Receipts and delivery identities may remain after history deletion; account deletion has a separate recovery lifecycle.

title: Which session strategy is configured?
text: JWT sessions. auth.ts configures strategy jwt and manually persists User rows in callbacks; it does not configure a Prisma adapter.

title: Why is verified email alone insufficient for automatic linking?
text: The app must not silently join unrelated existing accounts. The jwt callback resolves by Google subject and rejects an email owner whose ID differs from that identity.

title: Does login imply Gmail sending permission?
text: No. Scope and a usable refresh credential are checked separately. gmailAuthorized combines granted gmail.send permission with refresh-token availability, and send policy checks fresh state.

title: Where is the refresh token stored?
text: Encrypted server-side on User, with bounded retention on deletion jobs. The v2 envelope binds owner identity using authenticated encryption; plaintext is not projected into the session.

title: What happens when Google omits a new refresh token?
text: An existing encrypted credential can be retained. The callback updates encryptedRefreshToken only when account.refresh_token is present, while computing authorization from new scope evidence.

title: How does account deletion affect existing sessions?
text: The session callback removes a usable owner ID for missing or deletion-pending users. requireUser also queries current owner state; a still-present browser cookie does not restore account availability.

title: What are the delivery states?
text: READY, ATTEMPTING, UNCERTAIN and DONE. They complement the user-facing SendStatus. FAILED can coexist with UNCERTAIN and does not necessarily prove non-delivery.

title: When is network preparation performed?
text: After preflight and before the final database claim, outside owner locks. The worker prepares token, PDF bytes and MIME, then rechecks controls and usage at one fresh authorization time.

title: Why recheck after MIME preparation?
text: Policy or quota boundaries may change while preparation is slow. Suspension, pauses, period transitions and other owner activity can invalidate earlier permission; the final claim uses current state.

title: Can a timeout mean the email was sent?
text: Yes. A lost response does not prove rejection. The worker records uncertainty and retains usage rather than authorizing a duplicate submission.

title: Are Gmail requests automatically retried?
text: The current email worker disables automatic retries and the send call sets retry false. Pacing waits and publication repair occur before an attempt; they are different from repeating an ambiguous submission.

title: Does Message-ID guarantee provider deduplication?
text: No. It is a stable identity in the message, not a Gmail acceptance guarantee. Local uniqueness, state checks and claims prevent many duplicates, but the provider/database boundary remains non-atomic.

title: How does the app avoid CC/BCC batching?
text: buildMime constructs one To recipient for each Send. There is no CC/BCC population in the shown composer. Each recipient gets a separate rendered message.

title: Which template placeholders are supported?
text: {{name}}, {{company}} and {{role}}. Validation rejects unsupported or malformed tokens; campaign creation rechecks the rendered subject for newlines.

title: What happens after a definite provider rejection?
text: The appropriate reservation is released and the send finishes without automatic resubmission. Credential or throttle failures may pause other queued work; a definite rejection is not the same as an unknown send-time outcome.

title: What does normal pacing mean?
text: Sends are normally spaced about five seconds apart. Provider waits, preparation and orchestration add delay. The constant is not a measured end-to-end throughput claim.

title: How many Inngest functions are registered?
text: Eight in the source endpoint. They cover sending, quota reconciliation, attachment discovery/cleanup, deletion sweep/worker, billing maintenance and rate-limit cleanup.

title: How is per-user delivery concurrency limited?
text: sendEmail uses concurrency limit 1 keyed by event.data.userId. Database claims are still needed because orchestration configuration alone cannot provide atomic provider acceptance.

title: What does hourly reconciliation repair?
text: Accounting evidence, abandoned claims and interrupted publication. It must not turn an uncertain delivery into a fresh send. Deferred work is republished only when eligible.

title: Why is billing maintenance every four hours?
text: The source comment explicitly cites the Inngest Free execution allowance. This is confirmed decision evidence. Its recovery delay is a consequence, while actual provider pricing/capacity remains external.

title: Does this snapshot support live billing?
text: Yes, with an explicit live_mode configuration and rollout guards. Older test-only guidance is stale. This says nothing about whether a deployed account has live checkout enabled.

title: Can switching environment variables convert test customers into live ones?
text: No. The database binds to one Dodo environment and business. A mismatch fails closed; existing unbound provider data requires review. Product/customer/session identities do not cross modes.

title: Does a checkout return URL prove payment?
text: No. Access requires verified provider evidence. The return page displays state; signed events and server-side reconciliation maintain subscription observations.

title: What is verified by Standard Webhooks?
text: The exact raw body against the signature headers and timestamp tolerance. Verification precedes normalization/storage. Reserializing parsed JSON before verification would change the signed bytes.

title: How are duplicate billing callbacks handled?
text: A unique webhook ID and stored payload hash. Identical redelivery retains the first receipt; a different payload using the same ID raises a conflict.

title: Why commit the receipt before processing?
text: A processing interruption remains recoverable. after() attempts processing, while scheduled recovery can find committed RECEIVED/RETRY receipts later.

title: How can paid access remain after cancellation?
text: Verified cancellation at period end can preserve access until the deadline. Entitlement resolution uses lifecycle status and half-open period boundaries rather than simply testing a CANCELLED string.

title: What is grace-period usage?
text: An extension of the same allowance operational end. It must not create a second monthly allowance. Unresolved active provider boundaries pause sending rather than inventing dates.

title: Where are plan restrictions enforced?
text: Server actions, policy helpers and final worker checks. Client feature locks and allowance cards explain restrictions but cannot authorize a stale request.

title: What does a progress timer prove?
text: It presents an estimate or state projection, not provider delivery. Read committed send state and the provider evidence path; browser timing cannot determine acceptance.

title: How do page and component files divide work?
text: Server pages prepare data; focused client components handle interactions. Trace Compose through its page, component, submit action and business function to follow both rendering and mutation.

title: What binds v2 credentials to the owner?
text: AES-GCM additional authenticated data includes the owner UUID. The envelope also authenticates version, key ID and Gmail credential purpose; moving ciphertext to another owner fails.

title: How does rotation avoid overwriting reconnect credentials?
text: It updates only when the old ciphertext still matches. Compare-and-swap conditions include current deletion/expiry state. A concurrent reconnect or erasure wins.

title: Can old keys be removed immediately after rotation?
text: Not safely without checking retained credentials and backups. A restored backup may still hold v1 or older v2 envelopes. Repository instructions call for a restore/decrypt exercise.

title: Are PDF magic-byte checks malware scanning?
text: No. They check size, type and a PDF prefix. Treat harmful document content as a possible risk; do not claim the shown validation proves harmlessness.

title: What does fail closed mean here?
text: Unavailable controls or limiting infrastructure block protected operations. A missing SystemControl row or limiter error must not silently grant sending or expensive requests.

title: Are automatic operator alerts present?
text: The documented alert delivery/monitoring jobs were removed. Safe logs and persisted recovery remain. An external operational process must observe them; production monitoring is unknown.

title: Does reconnecting Gmail reset usage?
text: No. It can clear credential/domain-policy pause state. It does not erase app accounting, remove suspension or revive cancelled work.

title: What would you measure before scaling workers?
text: Queue age, publication delay, lock waits, provider latency and uncertainty rate. Per-owner serialization and provider limits are distinct constraints. A global worker increase may not improve one owner’s throughput.

title: Why not replace reservations with count-then-send?
text: Concurrent requests can each see capacity and over-admit. The owner transaction reserves the full batch and coordinates claim/settlement with durable identities.

title: What is the risk of removing owner locks?
text: Quota, cancellation and claim decisions can race. A replacement needs proven concurrency invariants, not just a higher parallelism setting.

title: Can the repository prove production capacity?
text: No. It provides constraints and test scenarios, not production measurements. Use disposable data and fake providers to measure representative workloads, then verify provider quotas separately.

title: Are all caller links exact?
text: No. Static call candidates are navigation evidence with explicit limits. Framework invocation, JSX references, aliases and dynamic properties can evade or confuse name-based caller matching.

title: What should a function explanation include?
text: Inputs, result, side effects, callers and failure behavior. Follow the exact source contract. Pure helpers, internal database primitives and authenticated actions have different assumptions.

title: Why disable normal credentials before cleanup completes?
text: Deletion immediately makes the account unavailable while recovery continues independently. The deletion job retains only deadline-limited revocation material and tracks incomplete external work.

title: What if billing cancellation fails during deletion?
text: The durable deletion workflow retains unfinished billing recovery. It should not falsely mark completion or depend on an already-deleted User relation.

title: Why retain an obsolete PDF for an uncertain send?
text: The unresolved campaign can still depend on that selected attachment. Cleanup protects current and queued/attempting/uncertain references; replacement is not permission to delete every previous file.

title: Why have both deletedAt and storageDeletedAt?
text: Logical retirement and physical deletion can fail independently. The remaining pending marker allows a later cleanup pass to retry external storage deletion without losing metadata.

title: OAuth
text: Delegated authorization: Google grants this app selected permissions without sharing the user password.

title: JWT
text: A token-based session representation managed by Auth.js; this app puts owner identity in its callbacks.

title: session
text: The authenticated application identity; distinct from the refresh credential needed to send Gmail.

title: refresh token
text: A server-held credential used to obtain an access token; persisted encrypted in this implementation.

title: access token
text: A temporary provider credential prepared explicitly before the final send claim.

title: scope
text: A named permission in the Google consent grant, such as gmail.send.

title: entitlement
text: A present-tense decision about whether an owner may use a feature, based on policy and current state.

title: idempotency
text: Repeated use of the same operation identity returns the same result or avoids repeating its effect.

title: idempotency key
text: An owner-scoped UUID used to identify one campaign submission or checkout operation.

title: snapshot
text: A stored copy of approved values, so later contact/template edits do not change a queued message.

title: MIME
text: The standard message format for text, HTML, headers and attachments; buildMime encodes it for Gmail.

title: base64url
text: A URL-safe base64 encoding used for the raw Gmail MIME message.

title: Message-ID
text: A stable message header identity; it is not proof of provider deduplication.

title: outbox
text: Durable local intent committed before publication to an external work system.

title: inbox
text: A durable provider-event receipt stored before asynchronous processing.

title: webhook
text: An HTTP callback from a provider. This app verifies Dodo signatures rather than requiring a user session.

title: reconciliation
text: Comparing/rebuilding local evidence and provider observations, including repairing interrupted publication.

title: lease
text: A time-bounded claim on active work. Expiry does not prove the external effect did not happen.

title: claim token
text: An unpredictable identity tying settlement to the exact claimed attempt.

title: reservation
text: Durable accounting capacity assigned to a delivery before external submission.

title: UTC
text: Coordinated Universal Time, used for daily usage boundaries and documented cron schedules.

title: half-open
text: A time range including its start and excluding its end, preventing overlap at boundaries.

title: grace period
text: A verified extension of paid operational access that retains the same allowance identity.

title: fail closed
text: Deny or defer protected work when required authorization/accounting controls are unavailable.

title: tenant
text: An owner whose data and operations must remain separate from other users.

title: row lock
text: A PostgreSQL transaction lock that serializes competing changes to the selected owner or budget.

title: transaction
text: A database unit whose local changes commit together or roll back together; external provider calls are outside it.

title: Prisma
text: The typed database client and schema/migration tooling used by this application.

title: App Router
text: The Next.js route organization used for layouts, pages, loading/error boundaries and handlers.

title: server action
text: A server-executed mutation entrypoint invoked by the UI; it still needs authentication and policy checks.

title: route handler
text: An HTTP endpoint implemented in an App Router route file.

title: server component
text: A React component rendered on the server; it can prepare data without making all UI code client-side.

title: client component
text: A React component opting into browser interactivity with use client.

title: Inngest
text: The event/workflow orchestration library registering the app’s eight background functions.

title: durable step
text: An orchestration work boundary recorded by Inngest; replay semantics differ from another Gmail request.

title: cron
text: A schedule expression used by periodic maintenance registrations.

title: AES-256-GCM
text: Authenticated encryption used for refresh-token envelopes, with a random IV and integrity tag.

title: AAD
text: Additional authenticated data binding a v2 credential to its version, key ID, purpose and owner UUID.

title: IV
text: The random initialization value used by encryption; v2 uses 12 bytes.

title: compare-and-swap
text: Update only if an observed old value still matches, preserving concurrent reconnect/erasure changes.

title: tombstone
text: A retained deletion marker that blocks unsafe recreation or activation while cleanup is pending.

title: Standard Webhooks
text: The signature/timestamp verification protocol used on the exact raw Dodo request body.

title: minor units
text: Integer currency subunits; configured examples include USD 599 and INR 29900.

title: rollout guard
text: A configuration or persisted control preventing activation before readiness is established.

title: rate limit
text: A request-frequency budget; separate from daily/monthly email allowance and Gmail provider limits.

title: UNCERTAIN

title: AGENTS.md
text:
# Mailloop

## Project

Mailloop is a web app that helps job seekers send personalized cold emails
through their own Gmail account.

## Stack

- Next.js App Router
- TypeScript
- Auth.js / NextAuth v5
- PostgreSQL
- Prisma
- Inngest
- Gmail API
- Tailwind CSS
- shadcn/ui
- Zod

## Development Rules

- Use TypeScript.
- Use the Next.js App Router.
- Use server-side code for secrets and Gmail API operations.
- Every user-facing server action and API route must authenticate the user.
- Auth.js entrypoints validate OAuth before a session exists. Inngest callbacks must verify service signatures; Blob completion callbacks must verify the Blob service.
- Dodo callbacks at `/api/webhooks/dodo` authenticate with verified Standard Webhooks signatures, not a user session. Billing supports test mode only.
- Always scope database queries by `userId`.
- Never log OAuth tokens.
- Never log email bodies.
- Never expose secrets to the client.
- Keep database IDs as UUIDs.
- PostgreSQL runs locally through Docker.
- The Next.js application runs directly on the host.
- Do not put the Next.js application inside Docker.

## Database

Use Prisma 7.10.0.

PostgreSQL is provided by docker-compose.yml.

For fresh local testing, use `npm run db:clear` to preview and
`npm run db:clear -- --apply` to clear records. Stop the app and workers first.
Preserve the complete `SystemControl` row and `_prisma_migrations`: they contain
required initialization, plan gating, test checkout and provider binding settings.
Never truncate all tables or reset migrations just to clear test data.

## Email

Every recipient must receive their own individual email.

Never use CC or BCC for batch sending.

## Development Style

Prefer simple, readable implementations.

Do not build unnecessary abstractions.

Build features incrementally and verify each step before moving on.

## Styling

- Use Tailwind utilities in TSX for ordinary component layout, spacing,
  typography, colors, and interaction states. Reuse the existing UI components
  and `cn` helper when composing variants with conflicting utilities.
- Use the existing semantic theme variables and Tailwind color mappings.
  Keep color literals in `src/app/theme-tokens.css`; run `npm run check:colors`.
- Keep complete utility strings in conditional branches or explicit maps so
  Tailwind can discover them. Do not build utility names from string fragments.
- Use `css-hover:` when migrating an unconditional CSS `:hover` rule. Tailwind's
  built-in `hover:` adds a pointer capability condition; existing Tailwind hover
  utilities should retain that condition.
- Keep custom CSS focused on theme variables, complex responsive compositions,
  motion, browser behavior, and scoped descendant rules that need to preserve
  the existing cascade. Do not replace stylesheets with large `@apply` blocks.
- Preserve selectors used by animation code and browser tests as stable hooks.
  Styling refactors must preserve appearance and behavior across both
  appearances, light/dark modes, and desktop/mobile layouts. Compare screenshots
  before accepting a migration; do not update snapshots to conceal differences.

- Run database-backed browser checks through `npm run test:e2e` or
  `scripts/test-usage-db.ts` so they use disposable databases and fake provider
  credentials. Fixtures restore the complete shared `SystemControl` row.
- See `docs/tailwind-styling.md` for retained CSS responsibilities and the
  screenshot/verification workflow. Keep established references fixed while
  migrating; document intentional functional/accessibility fixes separately.

## This is NOT the Next.js you know

This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (resolved from this file's directory; in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the repo root) before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices.

This block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean.
