UI “Daily allowance resets at 00:00 UTC (your time: …).” Follow-up days are elapsed 24-hour intervals, optional windows use user-selected IANA timezone; don't let timezone edits reset quotas.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

### Gmail retry/permanent-fail policy

Use Google HTTP status **and reason**; avoid assuming all 403 or 429 failures mean the same thing. Standard limits also include sends done directly in Gmail and other clients. [Google error handling](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/guides/handle-errors).

| Outcome                                                                                  | Retry/pause policy                                                                                                                                                                       | Reservation policy                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Local validation, attachment missing/oversize before Gmail                               | Permanent failure, show actionable reason                                                                                                                                                | Release; definitely not submitted.                                                                                                       |
| OAuth `invalid_grant` / revoked refresh token                                            | Pause owner's sending and read jobs; gmailAuthorized=false; reconnect required. Cancel unclaimed queue by default, retain approved sequence as paused only until expiry/user reapproval. | Release proven unsubmitted cancelled emails; keep attempting/uncertain until resolved.                                                   |
| 401                                                                                      | Try one bounded fresh credential refresh when safe; if repeated/invalid grant, reconnect pause                                                                                           | Do not reserve twice; failed rejected attempt can release on final cancellation.                                                         |
| 403 `rateLimitExceeded` / `userRateLimitExceeded`, explicit 429 throttle rejection       | Honor Retry-After; exponential backoff with jitter and shared owner cooldown; bounded attempts (e.g. 5) / 24-hour queue lifetime                                                         | Preserve while retrying, release only final proven rejection/expiry.                                                                     |
| 429 mail-sending daily limit / long provider retry time                                  | Pause owner until provider retry time, otherwise conservative hours-scale cooldown; show Gmail limit, not app quota                                                                      | Release if queue expires before safe retry and no submission was accepted. Do not reroute through other Google accounts to evade limits. |
| 403 `dailyLimitExceeded` / project quota exhaustion                                      | Global operational alert/cooldown, distinguish Google project from user allowance                                                                                                        | Keep unsubmitted reservations during bounded pause; cancel/release expired READY work.                                                   |
| 403 insufficientPermissions / domainPolicy                                               | Reconnect for missing consent, workspace-admin instructions for domain policy; no rapid retries                                                                                          | Release final explicit rejection; stop queued work with actionable pause.                                                                |
| Explicit 400 malformed MIME/invalid recipient, 404 invalid thread, rejected message size | Permanent; stop offending sequence/thread fallback needs user review                                                                                                                     | Release if provider explicitly rejected submission.                                                                                      |
| Network/5xx before any submission (token refresh/read/prepare)                           | Safe bounded retry; required reply read failure pauses auto-send                                                                                                                         | Preserve until retry/expiry; no outgoing ambiguity yet.                                                                                  |
| Network/timeout/5xx during/after send, or DB commit failure after accepted response      | UNCERTAIN, Sent reconcile if permitted; no blind retry                                                                                                                                   | Keep reserved/consume conservatively; no lease-based refund.                                                                             |
| Gmail API accepted, later hard bounce                                                    | Record evidence, suppress/cancel future outreach                                                                                                                                         | Confirmed slot remains consumed.                                                                                                         |

Use `sendingPauseReason` codes such as RECONNECT_REQUIRED, PROVIDER_RATE_LIMIT, PROVIDER_DAILY_LIMIT, DOMAIN_POLICY and SECURITY_SUSPENSION; only authorized reconnection clears credential pauses. Reconnection does not reactivate cancelled emails or increase quota. Read APIs can use safe transient retries; outgoing sends require stronger ambiguity handling than a generic SDK retry wrapper.

### Additional issues found during audit

- **One-off pass/annual quota:** do not conflate access expiry with quota month. A 30-day pass has one 300-email window; annual access needs 12 calendar/anchor monthly allowances. Add only when product decision is made.
- **Provider fees/minimums:** validate ₹299 in a real India-recurring quote with tax/FX/fees, and cost per retained paid customer. Do not implement discounted “pay what you want” as country validation.
- **Remote duplicate subscriptions:** local dedupe cannot fully eliminate unknown remote outcomes. Nightly reconcile all owned provider subscriptions; alert if more than one current recurring subscription, prevent another checkout, resolve billing rather than silently choosing one.
- **History erasure and scheduling:** clearing root history currently deletes follow-up reminders. Future cleanup must cancel approved sequences and erase follow-up bodies while preserving minimal usage/dedupe records. Never retain message bodies hidden behind a “delete history” operation.
- **Activity writes/pool pressure:** adding writes on every poll plus counter locks can overload the existing five-connection pool. Throttle lastActiveAt; bound page size/job fanout, keep locks short, and monitor queue latency before increasing connection counts.
- **Read permission retirement:** revocation can invalidate the sending token too; plan a deliberate reconnect flow. Disable read jobs before scope-policy claims, but don't assume an old token was downscoped merely because auth request text changed.
- **Support/admin accounting:** distinguish billed paid users from overrides and grandfathered accounts, record override expiry/reason, and show when access is denied but billing is still active. No staff access to Gmail or resumes to troubleshoot delivery.
- **Consent/change notice:** auto-send and payment terms require clear effective dates and user approval; existing reminder preferences cannot authorize new automatic mail. Store approval time/sequence snapshots and update privacy/terms before rollout.

The critical launch gates are reliable quota transactions, signed durable billing updates, truthful tracking/automation claims, revocable encrypted Google credentials, prompt subscription cancellation on deletion, and server-side suspension/admin controls. Everything else can be phased without sacrificing those guarantees.

### Dodo test billing completion (2026-10-20)

Implemented in `src/lib/billing/`: strict tax-inclusive USD 599/INR 29900 catalog verification, test-only configuration, directly pinned signature verification, durable ignored/quarantined receipts, period-end cancellation, atomic per-user request limits, bounded return polling, five-minute recovery and paginated midnight UTC reconciliation. Migration `20261020020000_dodo_billing_completion` defaults checkout off and retains existing billing/usage evidence. Checkout stays off until real hosted India/US/Germany quotes are checked. No live billing or deployment is part of this work. See `docs/dodo-test-billing.md` for local startup, signed fixtures, regression checks and rollback.

title: README.md
text:
# Mailloop

Personalized job outreach from your own Gmail. Production domain: **https://mailloop.in**.

Create templates, import contacts, preview emails for up to 10 recipients, attach a resume, track submissions, and mark replies manually. Every message has one recipient; Mailloop never batches through CC or BCC.

| Plan    | Recipients per campaign | Emails per UTC day | Emails per month |
| ------- | ----------------------: | -----------------: | ---------------: |
| Free    |                       3 |                  3 |               15 |
| Premium |                      10 |                 20 |              300 |

Daily allowances include sent and queued emails and reset at midnight UTC. Free monthly allowances follow the UTC calendar month; Premium follows the verified subscription billing period. When plan gating is disabled, the legacy allowance remains 200 emails per rolling 24 hours.

## Run locally

Requirements: Node.js 24 LTS, npm 11.19.0 (matching CI), Docker Compose, and a Google OAuth web client with Gmail API enabled.

1. Keep your existing `.env`, or copy `.env.example` to `.env` for a fresh checkout. For a new database, generate a local password with `openssl rand -hex 32`, set `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, and use the same password in `DATABASE_URL`. Fill in the remaining secrets; never commit `.env`.
2. Run `npm ci` (generates Prisma Client).
3. Run `docker compose up -d postgres`.
4. Run `npm run db:deploy` to apply checked-in migrations. No database reset is needed.
5. Run `npm run dev` on the host at **http://localhost:3000**.
6. In a second terminal, run `npm run inngest:dev`. Keep `INNGEST_DEV=1` locally so events go to the local Inngest dev server.
7. Sign in, save a template and contacts, optionally upload a PDF in Settings, and send from Compose.

Docker runs PostgreSQL only. The database is bound to **127.0.0.1:5433** to avoid the existing host listener at 5432 and restrict access to the local host. `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` must be set; Compose has no password fallback. The `mailloop_postgres_data` volume is preserved. Do not run `docker compose down -v` unless you intend to erase the database.

On an existing database, changing `.env` does not rotate the password stored in the volume. Rotate it through PostgreSQL's `\password mailloop` command in an authenticated administrative session, then update `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and `DATABASE_URL` to match. Recreate the PostgreSQL service with `docker compose up -d postgres` to apply the loopback binding without removing the volume.

The original scaffold, schema, generated-client path, and initial migration are retained. Prisma's configuration is now named `prisma.config.ts`. All three Prisma packages are pinned to **7.10.0**; do not upgrade them or use `prisma db push` to bypass migration history.

## Clear local test data

Stop Next.js, Inngest and subscription maintenance processes, then run:

```sh
npm run db:clear                 # Preview the reset; all changes roll back
npm run db:clear -- --apply      # Clear local app records
```

This deletes all local accounts, contacts, templates, attachments metadata,
campaigns, history, usage, billing records, deletion jobs and audit records.
It preserves the schema, migrations and the entire `SystemControl` record,
including plan limits, checkout enablement and Dodo test business binding.
Missing system settings cause the reset to fail rather than invent defaults.
The command accepts only the configured local Docker database on port 5433 and
rejects production mode. Restart the app and workers and sign in again afterward.
External Gmail messages, Blob files and Dodo test subscriptions are unaffected;
finish or cancel provider test subscriptions before clearing their local records.
Use this command instead of truncating every table or `prisma migrate reset`.

## Environment

| Variable                                            | Purpose                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DATABASE_URL`                                      | Local: `postgresql://mailloop:<your-password>@127.0.0.1:5433/mailloop`; production: managed PostgreSQL URL |
| `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `POSTGRES_DB` | Local Docker database configuration                                                                        |
| `AUTH_URL`                                          | `http://localhost:3000` locally; **`https://mailloop.in`** in production                                   |
| `AUTH_SECRET`                                       | Auth.js session encryption secret; generate with `openssl rand -base64 32`                                 |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`          | Google OAuth web client credentials                                                                        |
| `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`                              | Separate 32-byte AES-GCM key, encoded as 64 hexadecimal characters                                         |
| `INNGEST_DEV`                                       | `1` for local development only; unset in production                                                        |
| `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY`, `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY`          | Production Inngest event publishing and callback signature verification                                    |
| `BLOB_STORE_ID`, `BLOB_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_KEY`          | Provided by a **private** Vercel Blob store using OIDC in production                                       |
| `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`                             | Alternative credential for legacy private Blob stores                                                      |

Generate the token encryption key once:

```sh
node -e "console.log(require('node:crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))"
```

Keep this key backed up securely. Changing it makes existing refresh tokens unreadable; key rotation requires decrypting/re-encrypting existing tokens or reconnecting every account. It is independent of `AUTH_SECRET`.

Secrets are never sent as client props or returned by actions. Logs and Inngest events/step outputs contain no OAuth tokens, email bodies, or raw MIME messages.

## Google OAuth

Enable Gmail API and configure a **Web application** OAuth client. Add these exact authorized redirect URIs:

- Local: `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/google`
- Production: **`https://mailloop.in/api/auth/callback/google`**

Use `http://localhost:3000` and `https://mailloop.in` as the corresponding origins. Configure the consent screen and add your Gmail account as a test user during development. Request `openid`, `email`, `profile`, `gmail.send`.

Mailloop requests offline access and consent. Google returns a refresh token, which is encrypted before storing it. If a later login omits the token, the saved token remains intact. Settings offers reconnection for revoked/expired permission. Do not automatically link existing users based only on matching email addresses; users are bound to Google's stable account ID.

Mailloop requests sending permission only and never reads Gmail. Existing broad tokens cannot enable reads. Reconnecting does not revoke old grants: remove Mailloop in Google Manage Access and reconnect if broader permissions remain.

Sources: [Auth.js Google provider](https://authjs.dev/reference/core/providers/google), [Google Gmail scopes](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/auth/scopes), [Google OAuth token expiration](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2#expiration).

## Features and behavior

- **Templates:** Plain-text name, subject, and body, with a reference example and cursor insertion buttons. Supported placeholders are `{{name}}`, `{{company}}`, and `{{role}}`. Unknown/incomplete placeholders are rejected. Missing company values become empty text; every recipient needs a job role. Paste your portfolio, GitHub, LinkedIn, or other links directly into the message. You can include multiple links. Use full HTTP/HTTPS URLs to make them clickable. Delivery includes HTML and plain-text alternatives. The HTML uses natural width, left-aligned email typography, and preserves authored line breaks; typed HTML is escaped. Messages support `**bold**`, bullet lines starting with `- ` or `* `, and numbered lists starting with `1. `; these formats also appear in the live previews. The plain-text alternative keeps the authored symbols. Both template and Compose previews show the complete personalized message in a keyboard-accessible scrolling area capped at `min(440px, 55dvh)`, with controls, subject, and validation outside it. The message editor starts at `min(360px, 45dvh)` and can be resized vertically. Existing templates need no migration, and previously delivered messages remain unchanged. The complete example includes sample links and a signature to replace; attach the resume in Compose or remove the attachment sentence.
- **Contacts:** Both plans can save any job role without a custom-role quota. Settings supports up to 2 saved role shortcuts on Free or 8 on Premium, using any role text. Contacts shows only saved shortcuts, with no defaults when none are saved. Existing shortcuts above the limit can be retained or removed; adding or replacing requires fitting the current limit. Only Premium can override individual recipient roles in Compose; the preview updates automatically and saved contacts stay unchanged. Free uses the contact’s saved role, with server-side enforcement. Contacts require an editable name, email, and job role; company is optional. Email-derived names are suggestions and generic addresses need correction. Import comma/semicolon/newline email lists, CSV/TSV, or a CSV file with an `email` header. Optional columns are `name`, `company`, and `jobRole` (or `role`). Imports accept up to 1,000 rows / 1 MB, support quoted CSV, and provide editable, paginated previews and a bulk role selector. Correct unresolved names and roles before saving; duplicates are skipped. Emails are trimmed and lowercased; Gmail dot/plus aliases are not collapsed. Legacy Tag/Notes data remains in the database, and roles are backfilled from the latest nonempty campaign role when available.
- **Compose:** Select up to 3 recipients on Free or 10 on Premium and one template. Each recipient starts with their contact's job role, with batch-only overrides, saved shortcuts, filtering, and Apply Role to Selected. Preview each recipient separately. Contacts already sent/replied show local Last Sent timestamps and are skipped unless explicitly selected for resending. Queued and uncertain deliveries cannot be overridden.
- **Links and resume attachment:** Paste URLs directly into templates. Upload a resume PDF (up to 5 MiB) in Settings, then select “Attach Resume” in Compose; attachment defaults off. Mentioning a PDF in the message does not attach it. Both MIME type and PDF header are checked. Local uploads are stored under ignored `uploads/`; production uses private Blob with authenticated direct uploads, avoiding Vercel's function request-body limit. The server validates the uploaded file before activating it. Only the authenticated owner's current resume can be downloaded. Queued messages retain the chosen PDF and complete rendered message after later edits. Migration `20261008020000_inline_template_links` replaces every body `{{link}}` occurrence (including whitespace variants and archived templates) with the owner’s saved URL, then removes the saved-link column. Where no URL exists, the placeholder stays visible and preview/sending report “Replace {{link}} with a URL directly in your message.” Queued and historical snapshots remain unchanged.
- **History:** Sends redirect to `History?campaign=<id>` with queued, sent, failed, cancelled, and delivery-review counts. Progress refreshes every 5 seconds while visible and active. Approximate remaining ranges include all outstanding sends for that user and the persisted next-send delay; service delays can extend them. Completion comes from delivery states rather than a countdown. Recipient/company/role/template snapshots, filters, pagination, and automatic refresh are preserved. Sent Today uses a UTC calendar day; the quota uses the rolling last 24 hours.
- **Appearance:** Geist typography, restrained blue accents, matching light/dark tokens, and locally remembered Light/Dark/System choices. System is the default; the theme is applied before first paint. Explicit switches use brief opacity transitions and respect reduced motion. The account avatar menu contains account details, Settings, and Sign Out with keyboard and outside-click support.
- **Manual replies:** History offers Mark replied for sent messages and Undo for replied messages, including existing REPLIED rows. Both are available to all users. Marking a reply stops matching reminders; Undo restores eligibility. Mailloop does not read the inbox or detect replies. Add to shortlist prepares a follow-up for review in Compose. SENT means Gmail accepted submission, not confirmed recipient delivery. Legacy bounce records remain stored/exportable but have no effect on eligibility and are not displayed.
- **History deletion:** Settings permanently deletes eligible completed `Send` rows and reminders in a user-locked transaction. Successful sends become minimal `DeliveryReceipt` rows containing only a UUID, user ID, recipient address, original creation time, and successful-send time. Receipts remain until account deletion; quotas and yellow address warnings include both live sends and receipts. Queued, attempting, and uncertain sends remain. Empty campaigns retain idempotency keys while role and attachment references are cleared. Gmail emails remain unchanged.
- **Quota:** Up to 200 emails per rolling 24 hours, counting accepted submissions plus outstanding queue reservations and recent uncertain attempts. Capacity returns automatically as successful sends and uncertain attempts reach 24 hours old; READY queues and actively ATTEMPTING work remain reserved. The workspace refreshes usage every 60 seconds while visible and on return to the tab. Mailloop cannot reserve quota for emails you send outside the app; Gmail may impose additional account limits.
- **Cancellation:** Cancellation remains supported by the server for account deletion; History no longer displays cancellation buttons. The user-row lock serializes cancellation with delivery claims. Sent, actively sending, and uncertain messages cannot be stopped. Cancelled sends release quota reservations, finish campaign progress without claiming successful delivery, and release superseded PDFs once no remaining send needs them.
- **Export and account deletion:** Settings downloads a private, uncached JSON export from `/api/account/export`; credentials and storage locations are excluded. Typed-email confirmation disables access, cancels ready sends, and attempts billing cancellation immediately. The request is irreversible. The daily deletion sweep at 02:00 UTC / 07:30 IST processes requests after a minimum 15-minute drain, removing ordinary content and owned PDFs independently of billing/provider outages. Unfinished stages retry in later daily runs, with a 30-day target from the original request. A minimal recovery job and keyed Google identity hash prevent reactivation while deletion is pending. Retained revocation credentials are erased one daily interval before their original deadline. Signed Blob completion callbacks retain their separate drain protection and remove late uploads for disabled or missing accounts. Deleting Mailloop does not delete Gmail or recipient copies.
- **Follow-up reminders:** Default to 7 days; Settings also offers Off, 3, or 14 days. History computes a paginated due list on each load using the latest successful send, matching contact IDs and immutable recipient addresses. Replies, pending/uncertain deliveries, archived contacts, and an existing shortlist request suppress reminders. Rows use “No reply marked”; users record replies manually. Use Add to shortlist in History to prepare a follow-up; Compose is always the approval step.
- **Public policies:** `/privacy` and `/terms` are public and linked at sign-in, the landing footer, and Settings. The operator is Czar16; support is `[REDACTED_EMAIL]`. Review their wording and actual production provider/retention practices before launch.
- **Contact/template removal:** Contacts/templates are archived so queued emails and history survive. Resume replacement/removal affects new campaigns; queued messages retain their original version. Superseded files are deleted only when no queued/uncertain send requires them.

## How sending works

`src/lib/campaigns.ts` locks the user row in a short transaction, revalidates ownership/duplicates/quota, and snapshots each rendered message, recipient, template name, and attachment. An idempotency key makes repeated submission of the same campaign return its original result.

Each `Send` row acts as a durable outbox entry. `src/lib/inngest.ts` publishes one event per recipient using only `userId` and `sendId`. Campaign submission dispatches immediately; `quota-reconciliation` retries pending publishing and repairs accounting hourly (`0 * * * *`, UTC). Interrupted dispatches and deferred sends may wait up to one hour after becoming eligible. Event IDs and database delivery state protect against duplicate execution.

Daily maintenance (`0 3 * * *`, 03:00 UTC / 08:30 IST) uses one discovery step to paginate accounts and publishes per-account cleanup events in batches of 100 only for active accounts with unused attachments awaiting physical deletion. Idle accounts produce no cleanup events. Attachment cleanup processes at most ten files in a batch, preserves current attachments and those needed by queued, attempting, or uncertain sends, and records successful physical deletion while retaining historical metadata. Backlogs continue on later daily passes, so newly eligible cleanup may wait up to one day. Failed deletions remain pending for retry; local files already absent count as completed. Apply migration `20261013000000_attachment_storage_cleanup` and regenerate Prisma Client before running this version.

With no pending work, the current Inngest schedules use at least 56 executions/day (1,680 per 30 days): quota reconciliation hourly, daily deletion discovery (three steps), daily attachment maintenance, and daily rate-limit cleanup. Operator monitoring, alert delivery, and the 15-minute deletion-maintenance job are removed. Sending, additional pages, cleanup events/workers, pacing, and retries consume additional executions; previously consumed quota is unchanged.

The worker serializes active delivery steps per user. It checks `nextSendAt` in the database and uses `step.sleepUntil` instead of blocking a request. Sends are normally spaced about 5 seconds apart; Gmail limits may extend waits. The first send starts immediately if no persisted account wait exists. After each completed attempt the worker persists the shared `NORMAL_SEND_INTERVAL_SECONDS` delay (initially 5); separate campaigns share the same pacing. Existing persisted waits are retained, and the 60-second crash reservation remains. Inngest concurrency alone would not suffice because sleeping releases the execution slot.

`src/lib/gmail.ts` builds UTF-8 MIME with exactly one `To` address and an optional PDF, then sends the base64url-encoded message through Gmail API. The maintained MIME composer is installed as `gmail-mime`, separating it from Auth.js's unused optional Nodemailer provider dependency.

Delivery is **not exactly once** across Gmail and PostgreSQL. Ambiguous timeout/crash outcomes become FAILED/UNCERTAIN and immediately stop automatic processing. Check Gmail Sent yourself. History displays the uncertainty without a confirmation or resend button. Uncertain sends remain Needs review. Its quota consumption expires after 24 hours, but duplicate blocking persists. Each email gets one sending attempt, and the email worker has automatic retries disabled. Preparation failures and definite Gmail rejections finish without another automatic attempt and release reserved capacity. Rate-limit rejections retain account/project cooldowns for other queued messages. Legacy queued retries are finalized without another send.

Trade-offs: JWT sessions avoid additional Auth.js session tables; plain-text templates avoid a rich-text editor; private Blob avoids public URLs and ephemeral production disk; the MIME library handles Unicode and multipart encoding rather than handwritten MIME; authenticated routes use request-time rendering rather than caching user-specific data.

## Code map

| File                                               | Responsibility                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/auth.ts`                                      | Google OAuth, verified identity, JWT session callbacks                          |
| `src/lib/crypto.ts`                                | AES-256-GCM encryption with a fresh nonce and authentication tag                |
| `src/lib/db.ts`                                    | Shared Prisma 7 client with PostgreSQL driver adapter                           |
| `src/lib/session.ts`                               | Session + database user validation                                              |
| `src/lib/validation.ts`, `src/lib/imports.ts`      | Shared validation, placeholders, CSV parsing                                    |
| `src/lib/actions.ts`, `src/lib/campaigns.ts`       | Authenticated CRUD, imports, campaign snapshots, quota reservations             |
| `src/lib/inngest.ts`, `src/lib/gmail.ts`           | Durable dispatch, pacing, manual delivery review, Gmail sending/MIME            |
| `src/lib/storage.ts`, `src/lib/resume-actions.ts`  | Private PDFs, version retention, authenticated activation/removal               |
| `src/lib/account.ts`, `src/lib/launch-actions.ts`  | Explicit data export, deletion retention/cleanup, authenticated launch controls |
| `src/lib/cancellation.ts`, `src/lib/follow-ups.ts` | Serialized cancellation and paginated manual follow-up reminders                |
| `src/app/(app)`                                    | Protected Compose, Templates, Contacts, History, and Settings                   |
| `DESIGN.md`, `src/app/globals.css`                 | Design source of truth and Tailwind v4/shadcn-compatible tokens                 |

## Verify

```sh
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm test
npm run test:db
npm run test:e2e
npm run build
npx prisma migrate status
```

`npm run test:usage:db` creates a disposable Docker PostgreSQL database, applies migrations, runs usage and database tests, and removes only that test container and its storage. Use it to verify background-job changes without touching the development database.

Database/browser tests require the **local** database with checked-in migrations. Tests create and delete only UUID-scoped fixtures. Gmail calls are mocked in database tests. Browser tests use a separate server on port 3100, signed test-session cookies, fake refresh tokens, and an unreachable Inngest event endpoint; they never send real emails. Test artifacts are ignored.

Browser checks run desktop Chrome and mobile emulation with axe accessibility scans. Set `CHROME_PATH` when needed, or install Playwright's browser with `npx playwright install chromium`.

For a real smoke test, sign in with a user-controlled Google test account and send to another address you control. Verify the PDF, Gmail Sent message, manual reply marking and follow-up shortlisting, and reconnection. Real OAuth consent, Gmail delivery, and production Blob need valid external configuration and are not simulated by passing automated tests.

## Deploy to Vercel

Dodo subscription settlement rules, isolated verification, webhook setup and
deletion safeguards are documented in [Dodo test billing](docs/dodo-test-billing.md).
For production setup, use the [live billing rollout](docs/dodo-live-rollout.md).

1. Connect this repository and configure a managed PostgreSQL database. Keep local Docker out of production.
2. Set production environment variables, including **`AUTH_URL=https://mailloop.in`**, separate secrets, and a **private** Blob store token. Do not set `INNGEST_DEV` in production.
3. Back up the production database, then run `npm run db:deploy` against the production database as a controlled release step, then build with `npm run build`. Prisma Client is generated during installation; retain dev dependencies for the build/migration stage.
4. Connect Inngest to **`https://mailloop.in/api/inngest`** and configure the event/signing keys. Synchronize the registered functions. Verify `quota-reconciliation` uses `0 * * * *`, `maintenance` uses `0 3 * * *`, and `rate-limit-cleanup` uses `0 4 * * *` (UTC). Confirm `minimum-hardening-monitor`, `operator-alert-delivery`, `scheduled-replies`, and `refresh-replies` are absent. Auth.js entrypoints and service callbacks use provider verification; all user actions remain session-authenticated and user-scoped.
5. Add **mailloop.in** in Vercel Domains and configure the DNS records shown by Vercel. Complete Google production consent configuration using the callback above.
6. Review the public policies and confirm production hosting, PostgreSQL, private Blob, Inngest, and backup-retention practices. Configure Google consent with `https://mailloop.in/`, `https://mailloop.in/privacy`, `https://mailloop.in/terms`, and the production callback. Complete applicable Google OAuth verification/security assessment requirements for the requested Gmail scope before broad launch.
7. Verify sign-in, a controlled individual email with a PDF, private PDF access, signature-protected Inngest callbacks, manual reply marking and follow-up shortlisting, cancellation, export, reconnection, and deletion with accounts you control. Verify backups and monitor disabled accounts awaiting cleanup as well as failed sends, uncertain deliveries, and pending dispatch before inviting beta users. Do not log message contents or credentials.

The root layout includes Vercel Web Analytics, Speed Insights, and Google Analytics web stream `G-JMR4H98NTK`. Enable Web Analytics and Speed Insights in the Vercel project dashboard, then deploy and visit the site to begin collecting data. Google Analytics uses the stream's measurement ID directly; do not also publish a GA4 pageview tag for this stream through Google Tag Manager, as that would duplicate pageviews. Public URLs are listed in `/sitemap.xml`, with private app routes excluded from `/robots.txt` and marked `noindex` in their layouts.

Useful references: [Private Blob](https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage), [Blob client uploads](https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload), [Inngest concurrency](https://www.inngest.com/docs/durable-execution/flow-control/concurrency).

## Dependency audit

Prisma remains exactly 7.10.0 as required. The current `npm audit --omit=dev` reports four high-severity findings in Prisma CLI tooling and its `@prisma/config`, `deepmerge-ts`, and `mysql2` dependencies. The app uses PostgreSQL through `@prisma/adapter-pg`; it does not use the MySQL driver or accept user-provided Prisma configuration. Keep the CLI in the build/migration environment and track the upstream advisories. Do not run `npm audit fix --force`, which proposes changing the required Prisma version.

## Launch migration and cleanup operations

Keep full email history for launch and review database storage weekly using the [storage monitoring runbook](docs/storage-monitoring.md) and [read-only SQL report](ops/storage-report.sql). Review retention at 70% of the production plan's actual storage allowance, or when measured growth projects reaching that threshold within 30 days. This triggers review only; automatic retention is not enabled.

`20261010010000_launch_controls` adds `SendStatus.CANCELLED`, `Send.cancelledAt`, `User.deletionRequestedAt`, and `User.followUpDays` (default 7, constrained to 0/3/7/14). It is additive and preserves existing send history. Keep Prisma at 7.10.0 and apply migrations before deploying the new queries.

Register the updated Inngest functions after deployment. `account-deletion-jobs` runs daily at 02:00 UTC (`0 2 * * *`); remove the old `deletion-maintenance` registration. Billing cancellation is attempted inline when deletion is requested; daily workers retry unfinished stages. `maintenance` handles only active-account attachment cleanup at 03:00 UTC (`0 3 * * *`). A deletion request remains durable if Inngest is temporarily unavailable. Investigate unfinished jobs approaching their original 30-day target. Provider-managed backup/log retention must be established with the actual providers. Automated tests use mocked providers; production Blob cleanup and real OAuth still need controlled live checks.

`20261012000000_permanent_history` adds delivery receipts, backfills eligible soft-deleted successful history, and physically removes eligible soft-deleted sends atomically. Apply it before deploying the new queries. `historyDeletedAt` remains for compatibility with unresolved legacy rows. Selecting a yellow recipient in Compose authorizes their follow-up; deselecting removes authorization. Bulk selection continues to exclude previously emailed recipients.

Queue estimates are approximate: existing account wait + remaining 5-second gaps + a 5-second processing allowance per outstanding email. For 10 recipients, gaps total 45 seconds and the initial estimate is 95 seconds without an existing wait. Service latency can extend it; an expired timer shows “Sending” while work remains. “Sent” means Gmail accepted the send, not that it arrived in the recipient’s inbox.

Before general rollout, run a small campaign to controlled recipient addresses and review completion time, throttling, and uncertain outcomes without logging tokens or email bodies. If throttling increases, raise `NORMAL_SEND_INTERVAL_SECONDS` to 10.

Send-only deployment: apply `20261016000000_send_only_v1` and regenerate the pinned Prisma 7.10.0 client. Stop old workers before deploying. Synchronize Inngest and verify that `scheduled-replies` and `refresh-replies` are absent. Apply `20261016020000_remove_recipient_suppression` to remove unused suppression storage. Preserve applied migration history. Roll back cleanup or UI changes independently while retaining send-only OAuth, disabled reads, and uncertain-send protections. Test only against disposable local databases; verify real OAuth and individual sending with accounts you control.

Subscription deadlines use fresh checks at dispatch and claim. The production
Inngest app runs queued campaign cleanup and billing recovery every four hours,
and reconciliation daily. Billing webhooks process receipts directly;
monitor these [billing schedules](docs/dodo-test-billing.md#inngest-scheduling-for-vercel).
Account deletion uses a daily Inngest sweep at 02:00 UTC / 07:30 IST. Configure a stable
`DELETION_TOMBSTONE_HMAC_KEY` before enabling them. Deletion begins irreversible content cleanup on the next daily run after
a minimum 15-minute waiting period, targeting completion within 30 days, and cancellation recovery survives
User removal. See [lifecycle operations](docs/dodo-test-billing.md#lifecycle-and-deletion-operations)
for migration review, provider outages, key preservation, backup
restore fencing and rollback requirements. Automated verification uses disposable
Docker PostgreSQL and fake providers; these checks do not exercise real charges.

Before a payments launch, follow [Minimum hardening deployment and recovery](docs/minimum-hardening.md).
Keep checkout disabled through the production rollout. The runbook covers rolling limits, daily rate-limit cleanup,
Gmail provider pauses, credential key rotation, deployment checks and compatible rollback.

Operator monitoring and webhook alert delivery have been removed. After stopping
old workers, apply `20261021000000_remove_operator_alerts` to drop the unused alert
outbox and deletion-alert bookkeeping; financial, delivery and deletion-recovery
records remain. Synchronize Inngest and verify `minimum-hardening-monitor` and
`operator-alert-delivery` are absent. The replacement `rate-limit-cleanup` runs
daily at 04:00 UTC / 09:30 IST (`0 4 * * *`). It deletes up to 10,000 stale limiter
rows in batches of 500, skipping locked rows. Rows qualify only when `cleanupAt`
is more than one day old. Rate limits expire during requests independently of
cleanup. The idle cleanup costs two executions/day (about 60 per 30 days).
Automatic operator notifications and the minute heartbeat are no longer provided;
review safe logs and persisted recovery state manually.

Deletion credentials are erased when their deadline is within one day, reserving
one daily interval before the original day-30 deadline. A missed or delayed run can
still delay erasure. Daily deletion discovery prepares legacy requests and emits
only one worker event per due job. Attachment maintenance ignores deleting users,
and host billing recovery no longer independently schedules account deletion.

title: design/compose/README.md
text:
# Compose theme experiment

This records the original Compose experiment. The current implementation extends
it into selectable workspace appearances; see [Workspace appearances](../workspace-themes/README.md).

References generated with the built-in imagegen tool before implementation.

Prompt direction: a readable desktop Mailloop Compose workspace, Vercel-inspired
white / near-black surfaces, subtle 1px borders, system sans, 6px corners,
Inngest coral monospace section labels, blue links and focus, semantic status
colors. Compact Compose heading, horizontal navigation, message and shortlist
on the left, personal preview and send queue on the right. No purple, gradients,
or decorative illustration. Generate light and dark as separate images.

The implementation follows the references' palette, hierarchy, spacing, and
controls. Existing recipient role inputs, sending estimates, checklist, and
quota behavior take priority over invented controls in the generated references.
The existing estimate ring is retained to preserve its status information.

Compose content rules use `.compose-page`. Shell tokens follow the navigation
`data-compose-page` marker, because Next.js can retain inactive pages in hidden
Activity trees. Native dialogs inherit the tokens; Premium tooltips portal into
the scoped main element. The saved theme toggle and preference stay shared.

## Review artifacts

- [Light reference](reference-light.png) and [dark reference](reference-dark.png)
- [Exact generation prompts](prompts.md)
- [Light desktop](screenshots/compose-light-desktop.png), [laptop](screenshots/compose-light-laptop.png), [mobile](screenshots/compose-light-mobile.png)
- [Dark desktop](screenshots/compose-dark-desktop.png), [laptop](screenshots/compose-dark-laptop.png), [mobile](screenshots/compose-dark-mobile.png)
- [Light Premium dialog](screenshots/premium-light.png) and [dark Premium dialog](screenshots/premium-dark.png)

## Verification

Passed `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and all 5 tests in
`npm test -- tests/redesign.test.ts`.

All 24 targeted browser checks passed across desktop and mobile projects,
using the existing disposable PostgreSQL runner. Coverage includes sending
individual emails, templates, attachments, bulk selection, exhausted and stale
quotas, exact-capacity sends, and Premium dialogs in both themes. Compose was
captured at 1440×1100, 1280×800, and 390×844 in both themes. Accessibility scans,
viewport overflow, responsive columns, dialog dismissal and focus restoration,
and restoration of the existing shell after navigation passed.

The browser command was:

```sh
npx tsx scripts/test-usage-db.ts --e2e-only '--browser=app.spec.ts,feature-gates.spec.ts,--grep,compose theme|send-limit popup|send-limit boundary|individual campaign queue|attachment defaults|compose bulk selection'
```

No API or database implementation changes. No commit or push.

Only Usage content and its own portaled surfaces receive the supplied dark
palette in both light and dark modes. Shared header, navigation, header logo,
footer, help, Purple, and other routes keep their existing styles.

Existing text sizes, spacing, gauge dimensions (112px with 9px strokes), icon
tile size (60px), and bar height (8px) are retained per the implementation plan.
The supplied typography weights, letter spacing and corner values are applied;
the supplied larger typography/component sizes are deliberately not substituted.

## Files changed by this task

text:
# Vercel icon, History, help, and Pricing refinements

The final History treatment follows the two follow-up requests: role chips use
the same **blue highlight** as template placeholders, and recipient avatars have
a black background with white initials. Company/template chips and row hover
remain neutral. Purple retains its layout and icon styling; the later request
also brightens its light-mode amber. Purple dark yellow remains unchanged.

Compose has no blue feature tiles requiring a change. On Templates and Contacts,
only explicit icon markers and the subsequently requested semantic color
updates apply; their blue fields, selections, links, placeholders, and controls
keep their existing styling. Settings' ordinary icon tiles also receive the neutral treatment; warning/error icons remain semantic.
Shared help hints and walkthroughs receive the new styling on all workspace pages.

Usage changes from this task are limited to the subsequently requested semantic
green/amber colors. Separate concurrent work changed Usage's plan presentation
and the shared appearance controls during this task; that work was preserved.
Consequently, whole-page baseline screenshot differences may include those independent edits and changed header dimensions.

## Files changed by this task

- `src/app/globals.css`: brighter Purple light amber text/surfaces, with the
  existing Purple dark values retained.
- `src/components/usage/usage.module.css`,
  `src/components/settings/settings.module.css`,
  `src/components/ui/Tooltip.module.css`: semantic green/amber token updates only.
- `src/app/workspace-theme.css`: explicit icon tokens, History/portal neutral
  aliases, shared help styles, and consistent older History table selectors.
- `src/app/(app)/history/page.tsx`: History styling boundary class.
- `src/components/history/history.module.css`: role chip, tile outline, avatar.
- `src/components/history/HistoryStats.tsx`: neutral Send/Replies tile tints;
  queued remains amber.
- `src/components/history/StatCard.tsx`, `HistoryInfoRow.tsx`, `StatusBadge.tsx`,
  `RowActions.tsx`: History tooltip surface classes.
- `src/components/contacts/ImportContacts.tsx`, `ContactsEmptyState.tsx`:
  explicit icon tile classes, with no other component changes.
- `src/components/templates/TemplatesFreeView.tsx`: explicit empty-state glyph
  class, with no other component changes.
- `src/components/settings/SettingsPanel.tsx`, `ResumeUpload.tsx`: ordinary
  icon tile classes; Danger Zone retains its semantic treatment.
- `src/components/pricing/pricing.css`: Vercel-only light/dark Pricing styles
  and direct-load font registration using the existing bundled Inter file.
- `tests/browser/app.spec.ts`: refinement matrix, History avatars/chips/filter/
  hover/focus checks, every walkthrough step, Pricing and protected page checks.
  This file also contains concurrent appearance-selector test updates.
- `design/vercel-refinement/README.md` and selected screenshots: delivery record.

No API, database schema, billing logic, prices, or content changes.

## Tokens

| New token                   | Light     | Dark      |
| --------------------------- | --------- | --------- |
| `--workspace-icon-bg`       | `#EDEDED` | `#232323` |
| `--workspace-icon-ink`      | `#171717` | `#F2F2F2` |
| `--workspace-icon-border`   | `#D4D4D4` | `#333333` |

`--highlight-foreground`, and `--highlight-border`: `#EDEDED/#171717/#D4D4D4`
in light and `#232323/#F2F2F2/#333333` in dark. Links, progress and focus use
`--foreground` through local `--link`, `--ring`, `--progress-fill`, and

workspace boundary and follows the saved appearance.

## Verification

```sh
npm run typecheck
npm run lint

npx tsx scripts/test-usage-db.ts --e2e-only '--browser=app.spec.ts,pricing.spec.ts,--grep,Vercel refinement boundaries|public pricing,--output=/tmp/mailloop-vercel-refinement/final-results'
```

The browser matrix covers both appearances, both light/dark modes, desktop and
mobile. It checks all seven routes, all walkthrough steps, neutral icons, blue
History role chips, white-on-black initials, neutral company/template highlights,
row hover, keyboard tooltip focus, filters, overflow, direct Pricing loads,
localized price text, and automated axe accessibility/contrast checks.

Source comparisons confirm this task leaves Compose and the Templates/Contacts
stylesheet contents unchanged. Their existing blue link tokens are also asserted
in the browser. Baseline captures and raw run artifacts are isolated under
`/tmp/mailloop-vercel-refinement/` to avoid collisions with concurrent checks.

### Follow-up semantic colors

- Vercel green: `--success` / `--status-success-text` use `#176B3A` in light
  and deeper `#4FB87A` in dark. Pricing checks follow the same values. Usage's
  always-dark content uses `#4FB87A` in both modes.
- Vercel light amber: text `#946200`, visual queued fill `#D69B18`, warning
  background `#FFF3C4`, and recipient warning border `#E8C25A`. Dark amber stays
  unchanged.
- Purple light amber: text `#946200`, warning background `#FFF3C4`, premium
  notice border `#E8C25A`. Module-specific light warning labels now follow the
  shared status token. Purple dark values are explicitly preserved.
- Amber text contrast is at least 4.7:1 on the warm warning surface and 4.8:1
  on the light neutral surface. Deeper dark green is at least 6.7:1 on `#1E1E1E`.

The follow-up green also covers Vercel's Gmail connection dot and legacy sent
pills. Light-mode queue visuals and the connection dot use `#168A45`; the
light-mode queue amber uses `#C58A00`, while text keeps its accessible status color. History sent-badge backgrounds use `--appearance-sent-bg` with a Purple
fallback, so their tinted surface follows the deeper green.

Earlier shared changes were committed and pushed by a concurrent process
(`66b5d78` on `theme`, including earlier `97c9792`). The remaining refinements,
report, and screenshots are committed and pushed following the user's explicit
request. Those earlier commits are preserved.

## Review captures

- [History, dark desktop](screenshots/history-vercel-dark-desktop.png)
- [History, light desktop](screenshots/history-vercel-light-desktop.png)
- [History, dark mobile](screenshots/history-vercel-dark-mobile.png)
- [Pricing, dark desktop](screenshots/pricing-vercel-dark-desktop.png)

The full 10-case matrix passed. A separate six-case pass checks the follow-up

title: design/workspace-themes/README.md
text:
# Workspace appearances

The palette button between Gmail status and the light/dark control offers
**Purple** and **Vercel**. Appearance and color mode are independent. Purple is
the default; the browser remembers an explicit choice. Both appearances retain
the compact Compose heading, recipient summaries, role badges, and checklist.
The Vercel appearance uses the approved Compose references in `../compose` and
keeps the subsequently approved bright-yellow personalization highlights.

## Scope and behavior

Compose, Templates, Contacts, History, Usage, Settings, and billing use the
selected appearance. Public pages and admin retain their own existing styling.
The saved color mode continues to apply as before on public pages.

`mailloop-appearance` stores `purple` or `vercel`; the existing `mailloop-theme`
key still stores `light` or `dark`. Preferences synchronize across tabs. Blocked
storage falls back to in-memory choices for the document. No account setting,
API, or database changes are required.

The root pre-paint script initializes both choices. A single root-mounted
runtime tracks the active route and updates `data-workspace`, `data-appearance`,
and `data-theme` on the document. This avoids stale styling from Next.js's
retained, hidden route trees. Workspace-only Vercel tokens also reach native
dialogs and portaled menus/tooltips.

Page-local colors and decorative effects have appearance-aware overrides;
Purple retains its existing values. Vercel uses neutral surfaces, 6–8px controls
and panels, solid contrasting buttons, blue focus and links, coral section
labels, restrained glow, and semantic status feedback. Recipient rows and
status pills keep their deliberately rounded shapes.

## Review screenshots

- [Chooser](screenshots/appearance-chooser.png) and [mobile chooser](screenshots/appearance-chooser-mobile.png)
- Purple Compose: [light](screenshots/compose-purple-light.png), [dark](screenshots/compose-purple-dark.png)
- Vercel: [Contacts](screenshots/contacts-vercel-dark.png), [Templates](screenshots/templates-vercel-dark.png), [History](screenshots/history-vercel-dark.png), [Usage](screenshots/usage-vercel-light.png), [Settings](screenshots/settings-vercel-dark.png)
- Mobile Vercel: [Contacts](screenshots/contacts-vercel-dark-mobile.png), [Usage](screenshots/usage-vercel-light-mobile.png)

## Verification

Typecheck, lint, formatting checks, and 12 unit tests passed. The unit tests
exercise pre-paint initialization for every combination, route scoping, defaults,
invalid storage values, blocked storage, preview substitutions, and send estimates.

All 36 targeted browser configurations have been verified across desktop and
mobile, including all four appearance/mode combinations on the six main workspace
routes. Accessibility scans and viewport overflow checks passed. Tests cover
keyboard selection and dismissal, independent preferences, reload persistence,
cross-tab updates, blocked writes, public-page isolation, recipient selection,
templates, attachments, individual campaign sends, and quota/Premium dialogs.

The mobile outside-click test was corrected to tap the page edge rather than a
heading underneath the open chooser; the corrected selector test passed on both
projects. The relevant commands are:

```sh
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm test -- tests/appearance.test.ts tests/redesign.test.ts
npx tsx scripts/test-usage-db.ts --e2e-only '--browser=app.spec.ts,feature-gates.spec.ts,--grep,workspace appearance|compose theme|send-limit popup|send-limit boundary|individual campaign queue|attachment defaults|compose bulk selection'
npx tsx scripts/test-usage-db.ts --e2e-only '--browser=app.spec.ts,--grep,workspace appearance selector'
```

Work remains on `theme`, uncommitted and unpushed.

title: docs/admin-panel.md
text:
# Single-operator panel

The private `/admin` workspace provides users, access overrides, suspension,
read-only quota reporting, an immutable audit history, and the global sending
switch. It provides no impersonation, mailbox access, or billing-provider writes.
Dodo remains test-mode only.

## Deployment and recovery

1. Drain account-deletion workers. Older workers delete audit records and will
   fail after the new immutable-audit migration.
2. Apply migrations with `npm run db:deploy`; deploy this application and its
   updated workers together before resuming deletion work.
3. Set a new `ADMIN_DATABASE_URL` with the same database as `DATABASE_URL`, a
   **different, fresh login**, and a randomly generated password of at least
   24 characters. Never reuse the application owner connection. Run
   `npx tsx scripts/provision-admin-db.ts` explicitly using owner credentials.
   It creates the login and grants only enumerated columns and operations; it
   refuses an existing role rather than inheriting unknown grants. It prints
   only fixed result codes. Keep both URLs server-side and out of shell history.
4. Run the disposable test harness and verify forbidden-column access before
   provisioning the operator. `npm run test:usage:db -- --e2e --browser=admin,dodo-billing,feature-gates`
   creates its own temporary restricted credentials. PostgreSQL runs in Docker;
   Next.js runs on the host. No real provider calls occur in these tests.
5. Promote an existing account with its UUID and expected Google subject:
   `npx tsx scripts/bootstrap-admin.ts promote USER_UUID EXPECTED_GOOGLE_SUBJECT`.
   Use a trusted terminal; the subject is an identity identifier. The script
   serializes provisioning, refuses a second operator, and atomically audits
   promotion. Never bootstrap by email or by changing a role through the UI.
6. Configure the additional Google OAuth callback URI
   `https://YOUR_HOST/api/auth/callback/google-admin` (use the local origin in
   development). The normal Gmail callback remains `/api/auth/callback/google`.
7. Visit `/admin`, use **Verify Google identity**, and manually verify that a
   signed Google ID token supplies fresh `auth_time`. Mutation access fails
   closed if Google omits it. Mocked tests cannot certify Google's behavior.

Use an operator Google account protected by a passkey/security key and MFA;
restrict access to database owner credentials, the host, backups, and OAuth
configuration. Do not share operator sessions. Session refresh never renews the
15-minute mutation window. The identity-only provider requests `openid email
profile`, uses state/PKCE/nonce, binds the result to the existing session and a
five-minute encrypted challenge, verifies the ID token signature and Google
subject, and neither creates users nor updates Gmail credentials. Freshness
comes only from signed `auth_time`, never `iat`. See Google's
[OIDC claim reference](https://developers.google.com/identity/openid-connect/reference).

For recovery or rollback, revoke offline:
`npx tsx scripts/bootstrap-admin.ts revoke USER_UUID EXPECTED_GOOGLE_SUBJECT`.
Revocation is audited and effective on the next guarded request, including
already-issued sessions. Keep the migration, audit events, usage evidence,
cancellations, and sending-switch state. Deploy a fix rather than reversing the
migration or resetting quotas. Restore role credentials by provisioning another
fresh login and replacing `ADMIN_DATABASE_URL`, then remove obsolete grants
through the database operator's normal credential-rotation process.

## Behavior

- Every admin page, query, and action checks current role, suspension, and pending
  deletion through the restricted login. Mutations lock and recheck the actor.
  There is no fallback connection when admin configuration is missing.
- Reports use one repeatable-read, read-only transaction. Explicit DTOs exclude
  credentials, Google subjects, message content, contact data, resume paths,
  provider IDs, and arbitrary reasons. Legacy audit JSON is never returned.
- Usage is reconstructed from content-free ledger/import evidence, with the
  ledger's direct-assignment, overlapping-period, and deduplication rules.
  Confirmed/imported sends and reserved/attempting/uncertain consumption are
  separate. Remaining allowance never goes negative. Unresolved billing or
  unverified accounting displays unknown usage rather than fresh credit.
  Pending uncharged reservations remain conservatively reserved when normal
  lifecycle processing has not yet rebound them after an override boundary.
- Search is case-insensitive, bounded to 160 characters. Effective-plan filters
  run before the 50-row `(createdAt,id)` cursor. Applying filters drops cursors.
- All mutations require predefined reasons and a stable UUID request ID.
  Identical successful retries return the original safe acknowledgement;
  conflicting reuse is rejected. A maximum of 10 new successful mutations per
  operator per minute uses the durable billing-rate-limit table. Failed writes
  roll back both state, audit, and rate-limit consumption.
- Overrides expire after 30 days by default. A Free override requires explicit
  acknowledgement that billing continues. Overrides never change provider
  state or clear usage. Mutations re-evaluate accounting buckets under owner
  locks without reading campaign content. Existing worker/lifecycle checks
  enforce eligibility and rebind queued work before a new claim.
- Suspension cancels READY unattempted work and releases only proven
  unsubmitted reservations. It preserves attempted/uncertain evidence, existing
  resumes, billing cancellation, account export/deletion, and support. It cannot
  target the current operator. Unsuspension does not restart work or reconnect
  Gmail. Previously issued Blob tokens may upload until expiry; activation is
  denied and completion cleans up unactivated files.
- Global-control updates conflict with the shared lock held by final claims.
  After a disable commits, subsequent claims see disabled controls. A claim
  committed earlier cannot be recalled; no database lock spans a Gmail call.
- Audit UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE is blocked, even for the application connection.
  Only FK-triggered nulling on user removal is allowed. Immutable UUID snapshots
  and event data survive account deletion. New events have action-specific
  schemas, fixed reason codes, and a normalized request hash.
- `lastActiveAt` records visible application navigation through an authenticated
  same-origin endpoint, at most once every 15 minutes. Polling, workers, and
  admin inspection do not mark another user's activity. Missing history is
  shown as “Unknown.”

title: docs/custom-role-change-review.md
text:
# Custom-role change review

Free includes 1 custom role; Premium includes up to 5. Presets remain unchanged. Counts use normalized distinct titles across shortcuts and active contacts. Existing titles and approved queued snapshots remain usable. No dependencies, database columns, indexes, or migrations were added.

## Server enforcement

All new-title checks call `canUseRole` through the shared `roleLimitErrors` helper:

- `src/lib/actions.ts` — `savePreferences`: final shortcut set plus active contacts, preserving existing titles and atomic replacements.
- `src/lib/actions.ts` — `saveContact`: create, edit, email-based upsert, and restore; excludes the replaced active contact's former contribution.
- `src/lib/actions.ts` — `importContacts`: text and array input; CSV authorization still precedes parsing; distinct titles accumulate across valid rows; role failures return `fieldErrors["rows.<index>.jobRole"]` and write nothing.
- `src/lib/campaigns.ts` — `createCampaign`, reached by authenticated `submitCampaign`: validates each effective recipient role and accumulates new titles across the submitted batch without persisting overrides.

`src/lib/campaign-policy.ts` no longer cancels campaigns because of custom-role snapshots. Existing downgrade, dispatch, delivery, quota, template, and repeat-send checks remain. Snapshot eligibility survives downgrade and contact removal. Historical custom-role cancellation notices describe the former policy.

Counts and writes run under the existing owner-row transaction lock. The effective plan comes from the existing entitlement resolver; custom-role caps apply even with plan gating disabled.

## Exact pricing text changes

title: docs/design/free-templates/README.md
text:
# Free template layout references

Created with the built-in imagegen tool before implementation.

- [Active template, desktop dark](active-desktop-dark.png)
- [Retained templates, mobile light](retained-mobile-light.png)

## Design extraction

Use the app’s existing Plus Jakarta Sans typography and violet theme. Make the active template the primary panel: selection status, a prominent Edit action, readable subject and message, and quiet download/delete controls. Use one border around the message panel with internal dividers. Keep plan guidance in an open sidebar on desktop and stack it below on mobile. The active message remains visible independently of pagination; retained templates have a separate list and a clear switching action. Hide redundant selected buttons and single-page pagination. Preserve existing editing and plan enforcement.

Implementation uses 24px desktop padding, 20px narrow-screen padding, 16px corners, quiet neutral borders, and a 280px desktop sidebar. Long messages scroll inside a keyboard-focusable region rather than stretching the whole page. Existing application header/navigation and 34px page headings take precedence over illustrative reference chrome.

## Desktop prompt

Use case: ui-mockup. Create one high-fidelity desktop section reference for Mailloop's Templates page, improving Free-plan users' experience. Product uses Plus Jakarta Sans body, Space Grotesk numerals, dark background #0b0a14, card #15132a, foreground #ece9ff, body #b1adc9, restrained violet #a58aff, quiet neutral borders. Render a readable 1440x1000 style desktop UI, no browser chrome. Preserve a modest mailloop wordmark and horizontal nav Compose Templates Contacts History Usage Settings with Templates selected. Main heading 'Write once, personalise for everyone.' and subtitle 'Create, edit, and manage the messages you use in Compose.' Below, a 2-column layout: wide active template panel 70% and a narrow open plan explanation 30%. Active panel header shows a small check icon badge 'Active for Compose', template name 'First introduction' at 22px, prominent violet 'Edit template' button on right. Thin divider. Plain content with small 'Subject' label and 'Exploring {{role}} opportunities at {{company}}', another subtle divider then readable message: 'Hi {{name}},' blank line 'I’m interested in {{role}} opportunities at {{company}}. I’d love to share my experience and learn more about your team.' blank line 'Thanks,' newline 'Anoop'. Do not nest cards within the panel. Footer below a divider with secondary 'Download JSON' and quiet 'Delete' actions. Adjacent sidebar, no glowing container: 'Free plan' subtle violet label, heading 'One template. Every introduction.', short clear copy 'Your plan includes one reusable template. Edit it anytime and personalise it for every recipient.' A thin rule then 'Need more templates?' and 'Paid includes unlimited saved templates.', violet 'View Paid plan →' link and subdued 'Upgrades coming soon.' Under main panel a small sentence 'Placeholders fill in each recipient’s details when you compose an email.' Clean spacing, 24px padding, 16px corners, no disabled selected button, no large empty areas, no generic lock banners, no decorative graphics. Focus on this main section only, no other saved templates list.

## Mobile retained-template prompt

Use case: ui-mockup. Fresh standalone mobile UI reference for Mailloop Templates' 'Other saved templates' section, 430px phone width displayed large in 1024x1536 portrait format, no phone bezel or browser. Light theme #f6f5fb background, white flat cards, dark #17142b text, readable muted #6b6788, restrained violet #6d4aff accents. Plus Jakarta Sans. Large readable text and margins 24px. Section heading 'Other saved templates', small count '2 retained'. Supporting text 'Your existing templates are kept. Choose one to replace the template available on Free.' Two simple single-level cards, no nested boxes. First card title 'Follow-up', plain subject line 'Following up on my application', clear outlined button 'Use as Free template'. Thin divider at bottom and secondary actions 'View full template' disclosure, 'Download JSON', 'Delete' placed with comfortable touch spacing and sensible wrapping. Second card 'Referral request', subject 'A quick introduction', same clear selection button and secondary controls. Finish with a quiet inline text link 'Back to your active template ↑'. Keep layout concise and readable with quiet borders and 16px radii, no glow, no lock icons, no repeated Paid labels on each card. The purpose is making retained data accessible and template switching obvious without implying multiple active Free templates.

text:
# Landing footer reference

Generated with the built-in imagegen tool before implementation on 2026-11-06.
Reference: [landing-footer-reference.png](landing-footer-reference.png).

## Prompt

Use case: ui-mockup. Create a large readable standalone desktop website FOOTER design reference, wide landscape 1440 by 480 composition. Mailloop SaaS site, white background, clean Plus Jakarta Sans typography, charcoal primary text, muted gray secondary text, restrained lavender wordmark gradient. Top full-width clearly visible 2px gray dotted separator. Content centered within 1180px with 56px gutters. Three columns: equal narrow side columns flanking a spacious center. LEFT Product heading with Templates, Contacts, Send queue, Allowances stacked at 14.5px. CENTER large bold lowercase "mailloop" wordmark, around 135px text size, centered exactly in footer, with "Personalized outreach, made easy." beneath at 14.5px. RIGHT Support and Legal groups side by side: Support with Help center, FAQ, Contact us; Legal with Privacy, Terms. Vertically center navigation groups with central brand. Generous top and bottom space around primary row, no cards, no CTA or buttons, no separate small logo. Under row a 2px gray dotted separator and compact utility row: left "© 2026 mailloop", middle tiny green status dot and "All systems running", right "Made by Czarl6". Preserve exact labels. Design reference only for this footer, no other page sections.

## Extraction and implementation

The wordmark is the dominant element, surrounded by equal side columns. The
navigation stays smaller, with bold headings and muted links. The tagline sits
beneath the wordmark, centered; both separators frame a compact utility row.
There are no cards, shadows, buttons or extra brand icons. Implementation uses a
1:2:1 grid, 32px gaps and 48px vertical padding. It keeps the existing 1180px
container, responsive gutters, 14px navigation headings and 14.5px links.

The reference guides spacing and alignment; existing semantic colors and the
canvas animation remain the source for theme rendering. Follow-up user requests
set both separators to 1px at 60% of the landing page’s muted lavender color and
match the light-mode wordmark fade to dark mode: purple uses 60% top/6% bottom opacity,
and the alternate light appearance uses black at 50% top/4% bottom. These
refinements supersede both the reference image and the earlier stronger
light-mode gradient (90%/60% purple, 85%/55% black).

The system-status dot and “All systems running” label were subsequently removed
by request. The utility row retains copyright and creator credit.

Subsequent layout refinements align the Product, Support and Legal headings at
the top and remove the utility-row separator, retaining the outer dotted line.
The final centering correction supersedes top-aligned headings: each desktop
navigation group is centered vertically against the wordmark itself, with the
tagline in a separate row beneath it.

# Paid template library references

Created with the built-in imagegen tool before implementation.

- [Desktop dark library](library-desktop-dark.png)
- [Mobile light library](library-mobile-light.png)

## Design extraction

Preserve the app’s Plus Jakarta Sans typography, violet actions, existing header, and shared theme tokens. Use a single flat list with neutral dividers and 16px corners. Each desktop row has a two-line name/subject summary and trailing actions, with 44px touch targets. At narrow widths, move actions beneath the summary so names remain readable. Truncate long summaries; show the full text in the expandable preview. Keep only one preview open and limit its height to 320px with keyboard scrolling.

The library has a labeled server-side search across name and subject, 10 rows per page, result counts, pagination, and useful empty states. New/Edit opens the existing editor separately and preserves search/page context when returning. Free and ungated behavior stay intact. The loading skeleton follows the Paid library layout.

Each template also has a corner-arrow expand icon. It opens that individual message in a larger native dialog, with a readable subject, scrollable message, Edit and Download actions, and a Collapse control. Esc closes the view and returns focus to its expand icon. The underlying search, page, and inline preview stay in place.

The expand icon has an outlined 44px button and an “Expand” tooltip on hover or keyboard focus. Opening uses a 260ms eased fade and scale; closing uses a 180ms exit and waits before hiding the dialog or navigating to Edit. The backdrop fades with the dialog, interrupted opening starts closing from its current position, and repeated close clicks are ignored. Reduced-motion preferences disable these animations.

## Desktop prompt

Use case: ui-mockup. Generate a high fidelity desktop UI reference of Mailloop PAID user's Templates library. This is a compact library for many templates, NOT a full message per card. Existing visual language Plus Jakarta Sans, dark background #0b0a14, flat surface #15132a, foreground #ece9ff, readable muted #b1adc9, violet #a58aff. Header wordmark mailloop and navigation Compose Templates Contacts History Usage Settings; Templates active. Modest left heading 'Templates', subtitle 'Find the right message for your next introduction.' Primary violet 'New template' button at top right. Below one wide search field labeled 'Search templates', placeholder 'Search by name or subject', with Search button. Library toolbar 'Saved templates' and '24 templates'. A single bordered flat list, not separate cards. Show six compact rows about 68px tall. Each row left: small chevron and title on first line, muted subject on second line; right: Edit text link, download icon, Delete text button. Example rows 'First introduction' / 'Exploring {{role}} opportunities at {{company}}'; 'Follow-up' / 'Following up on my application'; 'Referral request' / 'A quick introduction'; 'Portfolio introduction'; 'Recruiter outreach'; 'Thank you'. One row 'Follow-up' expanded to show a short plain message in a shared open detail area immediately below its own row; all other message bodies hidden. Quiet neutral row dividers, 14px text, 16px panel corners, no nested cards, no huge panels, no extra plan upsell for Paid. Below list 'Page 1 of 3 · 24 results' and Previous/Next controls. Keep spacious gutters and readable content with efficient row density. Do not show the template editing form on this library view.

## Mobile prompt

Use case: ui-mockup. Fresh standalone mobile reference for Mailloop Paid Templates library, a compact searchable list to manage many email templates. 430px wide layout displayed at large readable size in 1024x1536 portrait, no phone or browser frame. LIGHT theme #f6f5fb background, white list surface, dark #17142b text, readable muted #6b6788, restrained violet #6d4aff. Plus Jakarta Sans. Header 'Templates' with subtitle 'Find the right message for your next introduction.' Clear 'New template' button beneath aligned left. Label 'Search templates' and search input with Search submit button. 'Saved templates' heading and '24 templates' count. One single flat bordered list with four compact entries, not separate cards. Each entry has a left disclosure chevron, a name and one muted subject line ellipsized, followed by a small action row with Edit, Download JSON icon button with clear icon, Delete. Titles First introduction, Follow-up, Referral request, Portfolio introduction. Message bodies are collapsed. Use thin quiet dividers and touch targets at least 44px high. Avoid huge card gaps, disabled controls, plan upgrade pitches, excessive icons, and showing full messages for every entry. At bottom show 'Page 1 of 3 · 24 results' and 'Next' button.
