title: docs/dodo-live-rollout.md
text:
# Dodo live billing rollout

Mailloop can run in either Dodo `test_mode` or `live_mode`, selected explicitly by
`DODO_PAYMENTS_ENVIRONMENT`. Local development remains in test mode. A database is
bound to one Dodo mode and business; changing its environment variables does not
convert test customers, checkouts, or subscriptions into live ones.

## Before deploying

1. Use a new managed PostgreSQL database for production. Never point Vercel at
   the local Docker database or a database already bound to a test Dodo business.
   Apply migrations with `npm run db:deploy` using the production `DATABASE_URL`.
   The `SystemControl` row is initialized with checkout disabled.
2. Verify the live Dodo product matches the catalog check in
   `src/lib/billing/store.ts`: monthly recurrence, 20-year subscription term,
   USD 599 minor units, one India rule of INR 29900 minor units, tax inclusive,
   no trial, add-ons, discount, or purchasing power parity. Checkout fails closed
   if the product differs.
3. Configure the other production services in `README.md`: Auth.js, Google OAuth,
   Inngest, private Vercel Blob, encryption keys, and billing recovery
   and reconciliation schedules from `docs/dodo-test-billing.md`. Do not set
   `INNGEST_DEV` in production.

## Deploy with checkout off

Set these **server-only** Vercel Production environment variables for the live
Dodo business. Use Vercel's secret settings, never `NEXT_PUBLIC_` or a committed
file:

```text
DODO_PAYMENTS_ENVIRONMENT=live_mode
DODO_PAYMENTS_API_KEY=[REDACTED_SECRET]
DODO_PAID_MONTHLY_PRODUCT_ID=<live product ID>
DODO_PAYMENTS_BUSINESS_ID=<live business ID>
DODO_PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_KEY=[REDACTED_SECRET]
AUTH_URL=https://mailloop.in
```

The live webhook endpoint must be registered in Dodo live mode as
`https://mailloop.in/api/webhooks/dodo` (replace the domain if production uses a
different canonical domain). The signing secret must come from that live endpoint.
Keep `SystemControl.billingCheckoutEnabled=false` during deployment and webhook
setup. A redirect back to Mailloop is not proof of payment; verified webhook
processing or provider reconciliation grants access.

## Verify and enable

1. Verify sign-in and the production domain, then confirm Dodo can deliver a
   signed live webhook. In Inngest Production, confirm `billing-maintenance` runs
   every four hours, including queued-send cleanup and billing recovery, with reconciliation daily.
   Investigate failed or missing runs before enabling checkout. This job depends
   on Inngest and the Vercel `/api/inngest` endpoint.
2. With a controlled account, verify hosted quotes for India (INR 29900), the US
   (USD 599), and Germany (provider-converted EUR), including the final tax
   presentation. The checkout URL must use `checkout.dodopayments.com` in live
   mode. No test key, product, or webhook secret can be reused.
3. Enable `SystemControl.billingCheckoutEnabled` only after the quote and service
   checks pass. Make one controlled real subscription purchase. Verify webhook
   settlement, paid access, renewal amount, portal access, and cancellation. A
   live test is a real charge. Review refunds and disputes operationally.
4. If checkout fails, disable `billingCheckoutEnabled` first. Keep webhook
   ingress, portal, cancellation, recovery, and reconciliation running to handle
   existing subscriptions and sessions.

The local `npm run db:clear -- --apply` command preserves `SystemControl`,
including the Dodo binding. It is not a way to convert a test database to live.

title: docs/dodo-test-billing.md
text:
# Dodo Payments test billing

Billing supports `test_mode` only. SDK `dodopayments` 2.55.0 and signature verifier
`standardwebhooks` 1.1.1 are directly pinned. Runtime billing code lives in
`src/lib/billing/` and stays server-only. Next.js runs on the host; PostgreSQL runs
in Docker. No live billing or deployment is included.

## Configuration and catalog

Configure server variables in an isolated local environment:

| Variable                                   | Required value                                  |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `DODO_PAYMENTS_ENVIRONMENT`                | Literal `test_mode`                             |
| `DODO_PAYMENTS_API_KEY`                    | Same test business's API key                    |
| `DODO_PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_KEY`                | Test webhook endpoint's signing secret          |
| `DODO_PAYMENTS_BUSINESS_ID`                | Expected test business ID                       |
| `DODO_PAID_MONTHLY_PRODUCT_ID`             | The single allowlisted test product             |
| `AUTH_URL`, `AUTH_SECRET`                  | Existing authentication configuration           |
| `APP_ORIGIN`                               | Optional canonical origin, otherwise `AUTH_URL` |
| `DATABASE_URL`                             | Separate local billing test database            |
| `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY`, `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY` | Existing service credentials as required        |
| `INNGEST_DEV=1`                            | Local development only                          |

No variable uses `NEXT_PUBLIC_`. Existing Google, encryption and Blob variables
remain required for their existing features. Origins must be HTTPS or loopback
HTTP, with no credentials, path, query or fragment. Custom Dodo base URLs and
custom headers are rejected. SDK logging and creation retries are disabled.

Configure one recurring **Mailloop Paid Monthly** product in the test dashboard:

- Base: USD **599 minor units (US$5.99)**, one payment every Month.
- Term: **20 Year**, separate from the monthly billing frequency.
- `pricing_mode: "by_country"`, exactly one active rule: country `IN`, currency
  `INR`, amount **29900 minor units (₹299)**.
- `tax_inclusive: true`: both prices **include applicable tax**.
- No trial, built-in discounts, PPP, add-ons or usage pricing.
- Three-day renewal grace, ending in `on_hold`. Only the signed deadline grants
  grace; the application never computes one from the current time.
- Portal period-end cancellation enabled; immediate cancellation and plan
  switching disabled. Scheduled cancellation may be revoked through the portal.

Checkout retrieves the product and `products.localizedPrices.list(productId)`
every time and rejects catalog drift. It omits `billing_currency`, leaves country
editing in hosted checkout, and disables manual currency selection/coupons.
Dodo derives currency from the billing country: India uses the fixed INR 29900
rule, the US uses the USD 599 base, and other countries may see the USD base
converted to their local currency through Adaptive Currency. Forcing USD instead
converts India's INR price back to dollars, so it must not be used as a fallback.
**Before enabling checkout, manually verify hosted quotes for India (INR 29900),
US (USD 599), and Germany (a provider-converted EUR quote), including applicable tax.**

This affects newly created sessions. Existing sessions retain their original
currency configuration and are deliberately reused until provider reconciliation
and expiry permit replacement. Do not mark an unpaid session expired locally
just to generate a replacement while the old hosted link is still payable.
Automated browser tests exercise the application flow with intercepted provider
navigation; they do not prove Dodo's actual country/currency precedence.

Keep `SystemControl.billingCheckoutEnabled=false` until those quotes pass. Enable
it only in the isolated test database after reviewing the hosted quotes. This is
a database switch, not a client or environment override. Portal, cancellation,
webhooks and reconciliation continue working while checkout is disabled and do
not depend on catalog availability. The database is bound to its test business;
a mismatch fails closed. Existing unbound billing data requires manual review.

## Migration and local startup

The additive migration is
`prisma/migrations/20261020020000_dodo_billing_completion/migration.sql`:

- Adds `SystemControl.billingCheckoutEnabled`, default **false**.
- Adds nullable `BillingSubscription.cancelRequestedAt`.
- Adds `BillingRateLimit` with a UUID identity, owner, operation, minute bucket
  and positive request counter. Its owner relation cascades on account deletion.

Existing billing receipts, subscriptions, checkout identities, usage, overrides
and earlier migrations are retained. Do not reset a database to apply this change.
Apply pending migrations **before** using the regenerated Prisma client:

```sh
npm ci
npm run db:deploy
npm run db:generate
npm run dev
```

Use only the intended local database for manual testing. Subscription processing
runs without Inngest. The webhook processes committed receipts using Next `after()`.
Run `npm run billing:recover`, `npm run billing:reconcile`, and
`npm run subscriptions:sweep` manually for local verification.

### Inngest scheduling for Vercel

The production `/api/inngest` endpoint registers one `billing-maintenance`
schedule every four hours at 00:00, 04:00, 08:00, 12:00, 16:00, and 20:00 UTC. Each run
sweeps queued sends, retries committed webhook receipts, and reconciles open
checkouts/subscriptions. At 00:00 UTC it additionally runs the
full daily reconciliation. Interrupted billing work may wait up to four hours
for scheduled recovery; verified webhooks still process immediately when received.
One run every four hours uses about 180 executions in a 30-day month, leaving
roughly 49,820 of Inngest Free's 50,000 monthly executions for email and other
functions. Monitor usage and upgrade or move scheduling before reaching the
allowance. Retries and other functions reduce the available margin.

After deployment, open Inngest **Production → Apps → mailloop → Functions** and
confirm `billing-maintenance` appears. Check **Runs** for successful invocations,
including a four-hour recovery run, before enabling checkout. Monitor failed and missing runs;
the recovery path now depends on both Inngest and the Vercel function. Preview
deployments must not run these schedules against the production database. Keep
checkout disabled if recovery is not operating.

### Host scheduling (alternative)

If operating a persistent host instead of Inngest, schedule these commands using cron. Example for a
checkout at `/srv/mailloop` (adjust the path and PATH for the host's Node installation):

```cron
SHELL=/bin/sh
PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
CRON_TZ=UTC
* * * * * cd /srv/mailloop && flock -n .subscription-sweep.lock npm run subscriptions:sweep >> subscription-maintenance.log 2>&1
*/5 * * * * cd /srv/mailloop && flock -n .billing-recovery.lock npm run billing:recover >> subscription-maintenance.log 2>&1
0 0 * * * cd /srv/mailloop && flock -n .billing-reconciliation.lock npm run billing:reconcile >> subscription-maintenance.log 2>&1
```

Use a cron implementation supporting `CRON_TZ`, or configure the scheduler host
for UTC. Run under the application service user, with the same environment and
installed dependencies as the app, including `tsx`. Commands load `.env` from the
working directory. Each `flock` prevents overlapping invocations of the same command;
a busy run skips its next invocation. Database owner locks protect concurrent
webhooks, recovery and reconciliation without blocking one schedule behind another.
Monitor nonzero exits and stale/missing successful runs, and rotate the log file.
Interrupted reconciliation safely starts over on the next invocation; five-minute
recovery keeps rotating through attached subscriptions in the meantime.

Do not run host cron and Inngest schedules together. If moving to a persistent
host, remove the three scheduled functions from the Inngest serve handler first,
deploy, and verify host cron runs before enabling checkout. The scripts remain
available for manual local verification.

The completion migration was also applied to the existing local Docker database
in response to the reported missing-column error. Existing row counts and
sending/gating/cutover/business-binding settings were checked before and after;
checkout remains disabled. Actual environment files and provider settings were
not changed.

## Request and access contract

All user-facing billing routes authenticate the session owner. POST routes also
require the configured Origin. Request limits use atomic owner/operation/minute
upserts: checkout 20/minute, portal 5/minute, cancel 5/minute, status 30/minute.
Limits return 429 with `Retry-After`; new checkouts additionally allow only five
attempts/hour. Minute counters are cleaned after one day.

Checkout accepts only `{plan:"paid_monthly",idempotencyKey:<UUID>}` and returns
only `{checkoutUrl}`. Customer, product, quantity, metadata and return URLs come
from the server. One unresolved attempt per owner, owner locks and stable customer
binding prevent duplicate creation. A lost response stays uncertain through the
24-hour provider validity window plus five minutes and provider reconciliation.
A processing/succeeded remote session or outstanding subscription blocks another
checkout even after the local expiry. Email alone never proves ownership.

Portal returns only `{portalUrl}` for the stored customer. The expiring bearer URL
is never persisted or logged. Cancel accepts only `{}` and returns pending state.
It records the marker before calling
`subscriptions.update(ownedId,{cancel_at_next_billing_date:true})`. Timeouts retain
the marker; recovery reads provider state before retrying the same flag. Verified
webhook processing or reconciliation clears the marker when confirmed. Paid time
is retained. Status exposes no provider IDs or secrets.

The workspace Usage page is `/usage`, including subscription controls, sending
allowances, reset times, and sending guidance. The public `/pricing` page compares
plans. Usage shows one advertised price: the saved billing country takes
precedence, otherwise it uses the same country-header localization as `/pricing`
(with a USD fallback). Stored subscription amounts keep their verified currency,
with terminal subscriptions shown in history. New checkout returns go to
`/usage/return`; checkout cancellation and portal returns go to `/usage`.
The authenticated legacy `/billing`, `/billing/return`, and
`/settings/billing/return` routes redirect to their Usage destinations without
forwarding query parameters. Stored amounts are before tax and are never inferred
from the user's location. Provider configuration outages do not hide persisted
subscription evidence. Suspension blocks upgrades, while management and
cancellation remain available.

Return query parameters grant nothing. The return page polls for at most two
minutes, then offers manual refresh. Settings display pending and confirmed
cancellation separately.

`subscription.active` alone cannot activate a paid period. Positive, signed
`payment.succeeded` coverage must match the stored customer/subscription and the
service period. Payment and subscription currencies may differ. Tax-added totals
are accepted; a client price or matching currency is not settlement proof.
Setup charges, zero payments and missing service periods do not grant access.
Payment failed/processing/cancelled events are observations and cannot downgrade
access or reset quota. Subscription lifecycle events retrieve current provider
state outside transactions, then commit history, access projection and processed
receipt together under the owner lock and billing version fence.

Signed grace is cycle-specific and survives GET responses that omit
`past_due_ends_at`. It extends the existing allowance, not its identity. Recovery
without a newly settled service period cannot mint another allowance. Sends during
grace count toward the later overlapping settled period. Hold/pause remove paid
access; terminal states end it at the verified boundary. Old subscription events
cannot replace or revoke an active replacement. Unsupported product changes are
quarantined and cannot reuse older settlement after switching back.

## Webhook inbox and reconciliation

The Node webhook route accepts at most 256 KiB, verifies the exact raw body with
`Webhook.verify()` and its default timestamp tolerance/secret encoding, then
checks the expected business. Test isolation comes from the endpoint, API client
and database binding; no payload environment field is invented.

Receipts commit before acknowledgement. Identical ID/hash duplicates return 200;
conflicting hashes return 409, preserving the original receipt and emitting only
a safe receipt-ID diagnostic. Database failures return retryable 503. Unsupported
signed events get minimal durable `IGNORED` receipts; recognized unusable data is
`QUARANTINED`. Normalization discards email, addresses, card details and arbitrary
metadata. Only owner/attempt correlation metadata is retained. Previously stored
normalized payment records without the new status field remain readable.

After commit, Next `after()` calls `processBillingEvent` with the receipt UUID.
Database owner locks/version checks fence concurrent callbacks, recovery and
nightly work; subscription processing has no Inngest dependency. Unresolved ownership retries with bounded
backoff, then quarantines after eight attempts. Deterministic ownership/product
conflicts quarantine immediately.

Five-minute recovery retries the inbox, unresolved checkouts, pending cancellation,
deletion safeguards and attached subscriptions. Nightly reconciliation pages all relevant
mapped subscriptions and open checkout attempts in bounded pages. An interrupted
command can safely restart; completed receipts remain recorded in the database. Safe
counts identify failures, missing settlement, quarantines, stale inbox work and
conflicting subscriptions; incomplete nightly runs fail visibly.

If settlement is missing, request **signed dashboard replay** of the payment
receipt. Subscription retrieval never substitutes for settlement. Inspect safe
`state`, `failureCode`, `attempts` and `nextAttemptAt` fields for retries; do not
log raw payloads. Review quarantines before any manual replay/reset.

Deletion disables access first, cancels queued sends, attempts immediate billing
cancellation, and retains uncertain checkout/subscription ownership until resolved.
The `account-deletion-jobs` Inngest function runs daily at 02:00 UTC (`0 2 * * *`).
Remove the old `deletion-maintenance` registration. Daily workers attempt Google
revocation and purge ordinary profile/content records and owned PDFs after the
minimum 15-minute drain. Database cleanup proceeds independently of billing or
storage availability. Recovery records retain minimal owner/provider identifiers
and a keyed Google identity hash; unresolved jobs survive removal of User.
The active-account attachment sweep and host billing recovery do not process
account deletion. Late signed events can add billing identifiers for the next
daily attempt without resurrecting an account.

## Verification

Automated checks use disposable Docker PostgreSQL and dummy provider clients,
never inherited application database credentials:

```sh
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm test -- --fileParallelism=false
npm run test:usage:db -- --billing-only
# Focused billing pages, deletion/maintenance, and desktop/mobile accessibility
npm run test:usage:db -- --billing-pages
npm run test:usage:db
npm run test:usage:db -- --e2e-only --browser=dodo-billing
MAILLOOP_E2E_ISOLATED=1 npm run build
```

For manual testing, use dashboard-signed events or
`dodo wh listen http://localhost:3000/api/webhooks/dodo`. `dodo wh trigger` produces
unsigned fixtures: do not weaken verification. Automated fixtures use
`Webhook.sign()` with fixture-only secrets.

Exercise India/US/Germany quotes, initial purchase, failed initial payment,
renewal, failed renewal, signed grace, sends across the boundary, hold/recovery,
period-end cancellation/revocation, delayed/replayed events and deletion. Stop
the recovery cron briefly to verify inbox recovery after it resumes. The controlled-clock database regression
checks allowance preservation, grace deadline exclusivity and usage attribution;
the replacement regression establishes A cancelled and B settled/active before
A's late cancellation/failure.

## Rollback

Disable `billingCheckoutEnabled` first. Keep webhook ingress, recovery,
reconciliation, portal, cancellation and signing secrets available while hosted
sessions/events drain. Existing sessions may remain usable for their validity
window. Roll back application behavior with checkout disabled; do not drop billing
tables, reverse historical migrations, reset quotas or delete idempotency records.
Restore captured dashboard settings if the operator changes them during testing.

## Official references

- [Localized pricing](https://docs.dodopayments.com/features/localized-pricing)
- [Checkout sessions](https://docs.dodopayments.com/developer-resources/checkout-session)
- [Subscription update](https://docs.dodopayments.com/api-reference/subscriptions/patch-subscriptions)
- [Subscriptions and signed grace](https://docs.dodopayments.com/features/subscription)
- [Webhooks](https://docs.dodopayments.com/developer-resources/webhooks)
- [CLI testing](https://docs.dodopayments.com/developer-resources/sdks/cli)

## Retention rollout

Before enabling the updated maintenance jobs in a deployment, review counts of
pending deletion requests at least 30 elapsed days old. The change applies to all
existing requests, and purged content cannot be recovered by reverting the code.
This implementation adds no schema migration, package, live billing, or new
financial retention deadline. If cleanup fails, disable only the new deletion
sweep while fixing it; preserve cancellation recovery and billing evidence. Do
not publish a 90-day retention policy as a rollback.

## Lifecycle and deletion operations

Billing remains test-mode-only. Run the additive `20261020030000_subscription_lifecycle`
migration before deploying the workers. Inspect the number and age of existing
`User.deletionRequestedAt` values first: the new worker starts irreversible content
purge on the next daily run after the original 15-minute drain, including old requests.
Do not apply this migration to an application database as part of automated tests.

Configure `DELETION_TOMBSTONE_HMAC_KEY` with an independently generated 32-byte hex
key before enabling the Inngest deletion workers. Operator webhook notifications
have been removed. Inspect safe logs and persisted recovery state manually.

The host command `npm run subscriptions:sweep` checks queued owners each minute
in pages. Dispatch and
claims also resolve access from the clock. Periods are half-open: verified
scheduled cancellation ends at `currentPeriodEnd`, signed failed-renewal grace
ends at `gracePeriodEnd`. Missing ordinary renewal evidence pauses sending. Grace
extends the same allowance. A Free downgrade counts same-month Paid attempts;
remaining allowance can be zero. Complete READY remainders compete oldest first
for both allowances. Cancelled work and its notice are never revived by renewal.

`account-deletion-jobs` runs daily at 02:00 UTC / 07:30 IST, including after User removal. The
independent `AccountDeletionJob` stores cancellation, storage and Google recovery.
Persisted leases protect concurrent workers. Billing attempts use read-before-write
and post-write retrieval, including duplicate subscriptions and late checkouts.
Billing cancellation is attempted immediately during the deletion request.
Persisted backoff remains a minimum eligibility delay; unfinished stages are
retried by the next daily sweep. Unresolved cancellation is never abandoned. Purge/revocation stages and deadline breaches remain visible in
the recovery records for manual review; no operator notifications are sent.
Inspect `failureCode`, `purgeFailureCode`, attempt counts, `nextAttemptAt`,
`nextBillingAttemptAt`, and stage timestamps. Never put provider exceptions or
customer data into those fields or logs.

On the next daily run after the 15-minute drain, database content and the tenant PDF prefix are erased
independently of billing and Google. The ordinary User is removed; content-free
notices, usage, contacts, templates, snapshots, receipts and unnecessary billing
rows are removed with it. Minimal UUID/provider cancellation evidence stays in the
job. Daily credential cleanup erases tokens when their original day-30 deadline
is within one day, including credentials retained by legacy User rows. This reserves
one daily interval before the deadline; scheduler outages can still delay erasure.
If Google is still unavailable, the credential is erased and
`googleRevocationIncomplete` stays visible for operator follow-up. Confirm external
revocation through Google/provider controls before recording its completion; do
not clear the tombstone without confirmation. Provider outages cannot guarantee
timely external deletion.

Dodo customer/support erasure is an operational process. Use the provider's
supported privacy/support channel and retain only legally necessary evidence.
There is no invented Dodo account-erasure API or automatic support contact here.
The operator must establish provider financial retention and backup windows; this
repository cannot certify those durations. Validate the privacy policy's section
11 backup practices with the actual backup operators before rollout.

Preserve the HMAC key alongside recovery data, outside the database. Do not rotate
it while unresolved hashes exist: the original Google subject is intentionally
unavailable for rehashing. Keep the old key until those jobs are resolved, or
implement and verify multi-key lookup before rotation. A restored backup must
remain unable to serve users, start checkout or dispatch sends until newer deletion
jobs/tombstones have been replayed, credentials past their deadlines erased, and
all already-deleted owners purged again. Restore the recovery ledger and matching
HMAC key before admitting traffic. Never let restoration recreate purged accounts.

Rollback keeps signed webhook ingress, deletion/cancellation workers, notices,
tombstones and ledger tables. Pause sending and disable checkout if necessary.
Only deploy code compatible with independent jobs; otherwise forward-fix. Retain
additive schema. Provider cancellations and content deletion cannot be undone;
rollback never queues cancelled campaigns again.

A successfully completed deletion job releases the Google identity block.
For already-deleted owners from an older deployment,
a late signed billing event transfers retained cancellation identifiers into a
job. Missing historical Google revocation proof remains flagged for operator
verification; it is never fabricated from the absence of a User row. After
confirming external revocation, an operator can record `googleRevokedAt`, clear
`googleRevocationIncomplete`, and make `nextAttemptAt` due for that exact owner.
Only the worker marks the entire job complete after all stages are confirmed.

title: docs/entitlement-foundation.md
text:
# Database and entitlement foundation

Billing/admin storage and server-only entitlement helpers now feed actions,
workers, quota reporting, preferences and UI. The sending control is enforced at
campaign creation, dispatch and both delivery checks. Paid gating remains off by
default; this implementation does not enable it.

Existing and future users default to Free, subscription status NONE, non-admin
and unsuspended. No subscriptions, overrides, grandfathering, activity or
billing dates are inferred. Free template eligibility uses the owned, active
selection or the oldest active template, breaking ties by ID. Legacy bounce storage stays unchanged. Recipient suppression storage was subsequently
removed by 20261016020000_remove_recipient_suppression. IDs remain application-generated UUID strings
in PostgreSQL TEXT columns; dates remain TIMESTAMP(3).

## Helper contract

Effective access uses [start, end) boundaries, including subscriptions scheduled
to cancel at period end. Precedence: deletion/suspension, active override,
grandfathering, verified subscription projection, Free. Free overrides take
precedence over grandfathering. PAST_DUE requires an explicit valid grace
deadline. Admin status grants no access or bypass.

requireEntitlement is an internal helper, not a Server Action. Entry points must
authenticate and obtain userId from the session; service jobs must verify their
service boundary. Reads use an explicit token-free selection, without caching.
An optional transaction keeps reads within the caller's transaction; callers
remain responsible for locks and resource-specific checks. Missing controls
deny access; database errors propagate.

Template checks grant baseline access only. Counts, selected-template ownership,
and active-template policy are enforced by template-policy under the User lock.
Sending checks do not reserve quota or replace Gmail preflight/OAuth ciphertext validation.

The client DTO explicitly allowlists fields and contains configured limits,
while quota snapshots supply remaining usage and reset timestamps. The workspace
provider refreshes both together; the flag-off quota API retains its legacy
shape. Basic tracking means Sent/Failed;
manual reply marking is a separate entitlement. Unlimited saved templates
serialize as null.

Gating off preserves legacy CSV, reminder and manual reply access. Custom-role caps apply independently of the gating switch.
Premium themes and preview highlight color customization also apply independently of the gating switch. Free previews use Cyan without overwriting a saved Premium color preference.
Priority support is new and still requires Paid. Account export/deletion,
cancellation and ordinary support remain outside paid
feature gates.

## Integration sites

| Existing site                                                                                                                        | Integration                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| src/lib/actions.ts:saveTemplate                                                                                                      | templateCreate/templateEdit; count and selected-template policy under user lock.                    |
| src/lib/actions.ts:archiveTemplate                                                                                                   | Maintain freeTemplateId when selected template is archived; retain archive access.                  |
| src/lib/actions.ts:importContacts                                                                                                    | csvImport before parsing or bulk lookup for string and array inputs; custom-role policy.            |
| src/lib/actions.ts:saveContact, savePreferences                                                                                      | canUseRole via roleLimitErrors for new distinct custom titles across shortcuts and active contacts. |
| src/lib/actions.ts:submitCampaign                                                                                                    | Entry checks; createCampaign remains authoritative.                                                 |
| src/lib/campaigns.ts:createCampaign                                                                                                  | send, templateUse, canUseRole via roleLimitErrors, plan recipient cap and atomic quotas.            |
| src/lib/inngest.ts:dispatchPending, deliverOne                                                                                       | Fresh sending/suspension/control checks before claim and Gmail submission.                          |
| src/lib/recipient-actions.ts:markReplied                                                                                             | Entitlement check inside existing transaction.                                                      |
| src/lib/recipient-actions.ts:undoReply                                                                                               | Require Paid for both reply editing actions; preserve readable reply history.                       |
| src/lib/capabilities.ts:canMarkReplied                                                                                               | Use the safe entitlement projection for advisory checks; actions reload access.                     |
| src/lib/launch-actions.ts:saveFollowUpDays                                                                                           | Gate enabling reminders; accept 3/7/14 and allow zero to disable.                                   |
| src/lib/follow-ups.ts:readFollowUps                                                                                                  | Suppress results if entitlement unavailable.                                                        |
| src/lib/resume-actions.ts:finalizeResume; src/lib/storage.ts:activateResume, storeLocalResume                                        | resumeUpload; recheck in activation transaction.                                                    |
| src/app/api/resume/upload/route.ts:POST                                                                                              | Authenticate and check upload eligibility.                                                          |
| src/app/api/resume/blob/route.ts:onBeforeGenerateToken                                                                               | Check eligibility before issuing upload token.                                                      |
| Same Blob route:onUploadCompleted                                                                                                    | Preserve service verification; recheck owner state for late uploads.                                |
| src/app/api/quota/route.ts:GET                                                                                                       | Safe authenticated quota DTO with fresh limits.                                                     |
| src/lib/campaign-progress-actions.ts:getCampaignProgress                                                                             | Preserve read-only status; safe plan context only if needed.                                        |
| src/app/(app)/layout.tsx                                                                                                             | Fresh snapshot; pass safe DTO only.                                                                 |
| src/app/(app)/compose/page.tsx; src/components/compose.tsx                                                                           | Recipient/template/custom-role controls and quota display.                                          |
| src/app/(app)/templates/page.tsx; src/components/forms.tsx:TemplateForm                                                              | Template count and edit eligibility.                                                                |
| src/app/(app)/contacts/page.tsx; src/components/contact-import.tsx                                                                   | CSV availability.                                                                                   |
| src/components/forms.tsx:ContactForm; src/components/preferences.tsx:Preferences, RoleChoices                                        | Custom-role availability.                                                                           |
| src/app/(app)/settings/page.tsx; src/components/launch-controls.tsx:AccountControls                                                  | Reminder eligibility and delays.                                                                    |
| src/app/(app)/history/page.tsx; src/components/recipient-controls.tsx                                                                | Mark replied and reminder visibility.                                                               |
| src/app/(app)/history/history-undo-reply.tsx                                                                                         | Lock Undo after downgrade; preserve existing reply labels.                                          |
| src/components/resume.tsx                                                                                                            | Upload availability; preserve download/removal.                                                     |
| src/components/workspace-quota.tsx, quota-explanation.tsx; src/lib/quota-usage.ts, delivery-usage.ts, email-limits.ts, validation.ts | Coordinated quota integration.                                                                      |

addContactToShortlist, saveContact and campaign resends use manualRepeatSend,
which is included in both Free and Premium. addToShortlist also requires
historyShortlist: the History shortcut is Premium-only when paid gating is enabled.
Free users can re-enter and save contact details to restore a repeat recipient
automatically; Premium users can use the History + shortcut. Durable delivery
receipts remain evidence after history removal. Re-saving updates or restores the
same contact and prepares a follow-up without sending. Compose requires individual
selection of previously emailed recipients; Select all skips them. Each repeat
email counts toward daily, monthly and campaign limits. checkContactEmail remains
available to show the same non-blocking warning on both plans.
Both markReplied and undoReply require Paid when gating is enabled. Existing reply
history remains readable and exportable. Reminder Off remains available to everyone.
Free includes 1 custom role; Premium includes up to 20. Saved role shortcuts have a separate limit of 5 on Free and 20 on Premium. Existing shortcuts survive a downgrade and may be retained or removed, while additions above the current plan limit are blocked. Count distinct normalized titles across shortcuts and active contacts. Existing custom titles remain usable even over the cap; only new titles are blocked. Replacements may use capacity freed by the same save. Compose overrides share remaining capacity within a batch without persisting titles. Approved queued role snapshots remain eligible after downgrade. Free users may switch their single eligible template; retained
extras remain viewable, exportable and archivable. Invalid campaigns lose their
READY remainder on downgrade, with only definitely unsubmitted capacity released.
Deleting completed history while a campaign is active hides and redacts message
content but retains original size/role evidence until the campaign is terminal,
so history deletion cannot make an invalid queued remainder eligible.

No integration is planned here with automatic reply stubs, suppression,
bounce marking or automatic follow-up workers. Usage models, follow-up
sequences, EntitlementGrant, sending-pause/cleanup fields, Gmail-read fields,
rollout/checkout flags and automatic tracking flags are excluded.

## Database invariants and deployment

SQL CHECK constraints are maintained in the migration; do not replace them
with db push. Related billing/override/suspension fields must be updated
atomically. Nullable periods support pending/failed records. Checkout and
webhook state fields remain open strings for future worker design.

SystemControl has at most one row with key global, seeded by the migration.
Missing-row handling denies access. Prisma generates UUIDs and updatedAt;
raw SQL writers supply IDs and updatedAt (the singleton seed uses PostgreSQL
gen_random_uuid). Webhooks and controls are service-owned. Provider IDs are
external strings.

Future verified billing handlers must maintain User projection and subscription
history transactionally. JSON writers must allowlist billing/audit metadata:
database JSON-object checks cannot enforce privacy. Audit snapshots survive
user deletion. Revisit billing/checkout cascade and financial retention policy
before billing launches.

Apply the additive migration before deploying code that queries the new fields;
generate Prisma Client explicitly. ALTER TABLE and ordinary index creation
acquire locks; schedule deployment with representative data in mind.

Verification uses disposable local databases ending in _test. New database tests
use unique schemas, clean them in finally/teardown (including setup failure),
and reject remote/non-test targets before writes. Run the entire database suite
serially using npm run test:db -- --no-file-parallelism. PostgreSQL stays in
Docker; tools and Next.js run on the host. Do not migrate the application
database as part of this verification.

For rollback, revert application code and leave additive schema and singleton
in place. The old application ignores them. Do not edit applied migrations,
reset the database or drop billing/audit evidence. Transactional migration
failure rolls back; correct before retry. Any schema removal needs a separate
reviewed migration.

## Verification

`npm run test:usage:db -- --e2e` applies existing migrations to a fresh,
loopback-only PostgreSQL container, runs database checks, then the feature-gate,
app, landing and policy browser suites before cleanup. The test application runs
on the host in `.next-e2e`, separately from the normal development server.
`--e2e-only --browser=feature-gates` repeats selected browser coverage with a new
disposable database. Neither mode uses the application database.

title: docs/minimum-hardening.md
text:
# Minimum hardening deployment and recovery

This release keeps Dodo in test mode and Gmail send-only. It adds no mailbox reads,
bounce detection, automated responses or resend of ambiguous submissions. It does
not enable real payments or provision backups.

## Deploy

1. Back up the database and preserve the existing legacy `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.
   Inventory backup/PITR and rollback retention; the actual retention policy
   is a deployment input.
2. Disable checkout and pause sending using existing operator controls. Drain and
   stop old workers before configuring v2 writes. Keep webhook reception and billing
   recovery running. All active processes must support v1/v2 decryption, including
   Auth.js, deletion workers and maintenance.
3. Run `npm run db:generate` and `npm run db:deploy`. The additive migration is
   `20261020050000_minimum_hardening`; do not remove historical billing buckets,
   reservations, pause state, receipts or financial records.
4. New operator roles use `scripts/provision-admin-db.ts`. For an existing role,
   run `npx tsx scripts/provision-admin-db.ts --upgrade-hardening` with the owner
   `DATABASE_URL` and restricted `ADMIN_DATABASE_URL`. This grants only SELECT,
   INSERT and UPDATE on the content-free `RateLimitBucket` table. Re-run restricted
   role privacy checks; never grant access to tokens, recipients or email content.
5. Configure the active key ID/key and prior-key map below.
6. Stop old workers and deploy the updated Inngest endpoint. Remove
   `minimum-hardening-monitor` and `operator-alert-delivery` registrations. Verify
   `rate-limit-cleanup` runs daily at 04:00 UTC (`0 4 * * *`). Preserve quota
   reconciliation and billing recovery. Verify `account-deletion-jobs` runs daily
   at 02:00 UTC (`0 2 * * *`), and `deletion-maintenance` is absent.
7. Apply `20261021000000_remove_operator_alerts` after stopping old code. This
   removes the alert outbox and deletion-alert bookkeeping. Preserve financial,
   delivery, pause and deletion-recovery records. The operator webhook environment
   variables are no longer used.
8. Check safe error logs and persisted retry/deletion state manually. Automatic
   operator notifications, scans and the minute heartbeat have been removed.
9. Complete the backup/key recovery exercise below before calling hardening ready.

## Limits and failure behavior

All limits are strict rolling windows using database time, per-budget row locks,
and bounded timestamp arrays. Authentication precedes admission. Admission commits
before parsing and business transactions; failed requests and idempotent replays
consume capacity. Database/limiter failure blocks the operation with 503 or action
code `UNAVAILABLE`. Denial returns HTTP 429 plus `Retry-After`, or action code
`RATE_LIMITED` and `retryAfter` seconds.

| Operation                           | Budget                                      |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Checkout                            | 5 / 10 minutes / owner                      |
| Portal + cancel combined            | 10 / minute / owner                         |
| Billing status                      | 30 / minute / owner                         |
| Campaign submission                 | 10 / minute / owner                         |
| CSV import                          | 5 / hour / owner                            |
| Account + template exports combined | 2 / hour / owner                            |
| Admin mutations                     | 20 / minute / actor                         |
| System controls, additionally       | 5 / minute / actor and 10 / minute globally |

Admin budgets are admitted atomically in stable lock order. Provider callbacks and
recovery jobs consume no user budget. Suspended users retain billing management.
Expired limiter rows are deleted daily in batches of 500, up to 10,000 per run,
without blocking active budgets. Only rows whose `cleanupAt` is more than one day
old qualify; excess or locked rows wait for a later pass. Request-time expiry is
independent of this cleanup.

Logs validate fixed event codes, UUIDs, timestamps,
bounded counts and outcome booleans. Raw provider payloads, nested errors, headers,
URLs, addresses, subjects, bodies and credentials are not accepted. Auth.js hooks,
SDK logging and Inngest step/function errors use the same safe boundary. Webhooks
correlate by internal receipt UUID, never by attacker/provider-supplied webhook IDs.

Gmail checks owner/project pauses at publication, preflight and final claim. Provider
calls hold no owner lock. Daily/project limits honor provider deadlines or default
to six hours. Retry-After >=1 hour is a long provider cooldown. Transient throttles pause other queued work for at least one minute.
Each email gets one sending attempt; definite Gmail rejections and preparation
failures finish immediately and release their reservations. The email worker has
automatic retries disabled. A definite 401 or revocation requires reconnection. Credential/domain pauses cancel and release only
READY work. Domain policy needs workspace-admin approval. Authorized reconnection
clears credential/policy pauses, preserves suspension and app quota, and never revives
cancelled work. Send-time network/timeout/5xx, unknown provider outcomes and failed
acceptance persistence remain UNCERTAIN, retain accounting and never auto-resend.

## Keys and rotation

Keep these server-only:

- `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`: the fixed legacy-v1 decrypt key.
- `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_ACTIVE_KEY_ID`: 1–64 letters, numbers, underscores or hyphens.
- `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_ACTIVE_KEY`: a new 32-byte key, encoded as 64 hex characters.
- `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_PREVIOUS_KEYS_JSON`: JSON object mapping prior v2 key IDs to
  their 64-character hex keys; exclude the active ID. The default is `{}`.

Provision keys with the secrets manager. New writes use
`v2.<keyId>.<iv>.<tag>.<ciphertext>` with AES-256-GCM. AAD authenticates the version,
key ID, Gmail credential purpose and owner UUID. A deletion job uses the same owner
and purpose when copying its owner's ciphertext. v2 never falls back to another key.
Malformed configuration, key loss, envelope tampering and owner mismatch fail closed
with constant safe errors.

To rotate A → B, retain A in the previous-key map and switch the active ID/key to B
on every process. Keep the legacy key too. Run:

```sh
npm run tokens:rotate
npm run tokens:rotate -- --apply
# Resume after the last successfully completed owner page:
npm run tokens:rotate -- --apply --after=OWNER_UUID
# Validate that every retained credential decrypts and needs no update:
npm run tokens:rotate
```

The default is genuinely read-only: SELECTs and crypto only, no row updates, leases
or checkpoints. Owner pages cover User credentials and unexpired retained deletion
revocation credentials, including jobs whose User no longer exists. Updates compare
ciphertext and current deletion/expiry state; a concurrent reconnect wins and erased
credentials cannot be restored. Logs contain counts and an owner cursor only. A
nonzero failure count stops the CLI; retain the previous successful cursor, fix key
configuration and resume. Re-run from the beginning after any conflicts; it is
idempotent. Dry run must show zero failures and zero eligible records after rotation.
Do not print plaintext, ciphertext, environment contents or key material.

Before retiring A or the v1 key, verify a restored staging backup can decrypt both
user and deletion-job tokens using the stored old keys. Exercise A → B, mixed
v1/A/B records, resumed rotation, concurrent reconnect/deletion and old-key recovery
with fixture credentials and mocked Google revocation. Record the recovery date,
backup identifier, required key IDs, recovery result and monitoring evidence in your
deployment record. Retain old keys **at least 90 days**, and longer while any backup,
PITR window, retained credential or rollback artifact requires them. Never retire a
key merely because the current live database has no matching rows.

## Rollback

Disable checkout and pause sending. Keep verified webhook reception and billing
recovery running. Roll back only to a release that reads both v1 and v2 and honors
persisted pauses and uncertain delivery. Keep the additive schema and financial,
reservation, delivery and encryption state. To roll back the writer, select the
previous active key and retain every required decrypt key. Never restore plaintext,
rewrite ciphertext back to v1, restore erased credentials or resend ambiguous work.

Repository checks do not certify the deployment's backup retention. Recovery
exercises require the operator's backup inputs before deployment readiness can
be declared.

title: docs/oauth-verification-v1.md
text:
# V1 Google OAuth verification resubmission

Project: `mailloop-510915` (number `842074495814`). Production: https://mailloop.in.

This guide concerns the send-only `main` release. Do not merge another branch to
prepare verification. Approval is Google's decision; a policy update alone does
not address the requested demo and reviewer access.

## Current implementation and remaining checks

- `src/auth.ts` requests only `openid email profile` and
  `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send`.
- Gmail operations send individual messages using `users.messages.send`.
  There is no inbox reading, Gmail deletion, or automatic reply detection.
- The public privacy policy names Vercel, Neon, Vercel Blob, Inngest, Google,
  and selected recipients, explains the data each handles, and describes
  HTTPS, AES-256-GCM refresh-token encryption, server-side credential handling,
  authenticated account access, private PDFs, and limited operational records.
- Sign-in uses Google only. V1 has no separate local password, app invitation,
  subscription purchase, or credit-card requirement. Keep authentication enabled.
- Verify the production OAuth client belongs to this project and the actual
  hosting/database/storage providers match the policy before resubmitting.
  The Cloud Console configuration cannot be inferred from repository code.

The privacy disclosures were already present on the live site when checked on
October 31, 2026. This follow-up adds direct section links. Deploy `main` if those
links are not yet present in production; no migration or new environment variable
is required for this follow-up.

## Cloud Console and live access

1. Select `mailloop-510915` in Google Auth Platform.
2. In Branding, check the app identity, support contact, verified domain,
   homepage `https://mailloop.in/`, and privacy URL
   `https://mailloop.in/privacy`.
3. In Data Access and the verification request, retain only identity permissions
   and `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send`. Remove any old read,
   modify, metadata, compose, or full-mailbox scopes from this submission.
   Explain the change if the previous submission included broader permissions.
4. Confirm the web OAuth client's authorized callback includes
   `https://mailloop.in/api/auth/callback/google`.
5. Check Audience/publishing status and any user-cap restriction. If access is
   limited to test users, obtain the reviewer's Google account address and add
   that exact address. Do not mistake the verification team's reply address for
   the account they will use to sign in. Resolve blocked access before replying.
6. Test the full flow below with a Google account and recipient addresses you
   control. Confirm live sending and the Inngest worker actually work.

If a reviewer needs credentials beyond Google sign-in, request their reviewer
account address for authorization or arrange a dedicated test account through
the verification thread. Never send personal account credentials or save any
test credentials in this repository. Do not add an authentication bypass.

## Recording the replacement demo

Use a real screen recording of the deployed app in English with readable text.
Keep the browser address bar visible, including the OAuth client ID during
authorization. Narration or captions should explain each step. Record all
scope-dependent user features, including personalized batch sends and an
explicitly selected resume attachment; do not substitute a promotional video.

Before recording, use a dedicated account you control and revoke its existing
Mailloop connection at https://myaccount.google.com/connections, then sign out
of Mailloop. This ensures old grants do not hide permissions or retain previous
mailbox-read access. Prepare a small, non-sensitive PDF and two controlled
recipient inboxes. Do not show passwords, tokens, or unrelated personal email.

1. Open the homepage, explain Mailloop's purpose, and show the public privacy
   policy, including the data-sharing and data-protection sections.
2. Click **Get started with Google**, choose the demo account, and show the
   complete Google sign-in and consent process. Expand **Show all services**
   and any permission details when offered. Leave every requested permission
   readable. Grant Gmail sending permission. If old read/modify permissions
   appear, stop and resolve the deployed client/scope mismatch first.
3. Show **Settings** with the signed-in address and Gmail sending enabled.
   Explain that identity permissions create the user's account and Gmail
   permission sends approved emails from that account. Click **Reconnect Gmail**
   and demonstrate that consent path too, expanding any permission details,
   then return to Settings.
4. Upload the demo PDF in **Settings**. In **Contacts**, add two addresses you
   control, with distinct names and a job role for each. Company is optional.
5. In **Templates**, save a named template with a unique subject, such as
   `Mailloop verification demo`, and body:

   ```text
   Hi {{name}},

   This is a controlled demonstration of Mailloop for the {{role}} role.
   Please find the selected demo PDF attached.
   ```

6. Open **Compose**, choose the saved template, select both recipients, confirm
   each role is filled, inspect each **Personal Preview**, and enable
   **Attach Resume**. Explain that each recipient gets a separate email.
7. Click **Send to 2 recipients** once. Show sending progress and **History**
   until both messages show **Sent**. Explain that this means Gmail accepted
   them, rather than proof of inbox delivery.
8. Open **Gmail → Sent** for the SAME sender account. Search the unique subject
   if necessary. Open both emails (expand the individual messages if Gmail
   groups them). Show sender, each single recipient, personalized body, and PDF
   attachment. Show there are no CC/BCC batch recipients. This is the required
   evidence of the change in the source Google account.
9. Explain that replies are checked in Gmail, and Mailloop does not read or
   delete mailbox messages. Deleting Mailloop history only deletes app records.
   No Gmail deletion demonstration is needed for this send-only release.

Upload the complete recording as an accessible unlisted YouTube video and test
the link while signed out. Keep the video available throughout review.

## Scope justification for the submission

> Mailloop is a standalone web app that sends user-approved, personalized job
> outreach emails from the user's own Gmail account. We use openid, email, and
> profile to authenticate the user and identify their account and sender name.
> We use https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send with Gmail
> users.messages.send to send a separate message to each selected recipient,
> including a resume PDF only when the user explicitly selects it. This is the
> narrowest Gmail scope supporting this sending feature in our standalone web

Reviewer access:

title: docs/storage-monitoring.md
text:
# Launch storage monitoring

Keep full email history for launch. Existing pagination, JSON export, manual history deletion, delivery receipts, and campaign submission keys remain in place. This report adds no automatic retention or deletion.

## Run the report

Run [ops/storage-report.sql](../ops/storage-report.sql) weekly against the migrated production Mailloop database. This is an operator-only report across all users, not a user-facing query or endpoint. Use an authorized database connection with `SELECT` access to `public."Send"` and permission to call `pg_database_size` (database `CONNECT` or the provider's appropriate monitoring role). The SQL uses a read-only transaction and rolls it back; it returns one row of aggregate counts and sizes, including zero counts/content bytes on an empty table.

From the repository root, use PostgreSQL's `psql` client:

```sh
psql -X --set=ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --dbname=service=mailloop-production --file=ops/storage-report.sql
```

Configure `mailloop-production` in your local PostgreSQL service file with the provider's host, database, user, port, and required TLS settings. Supply the password through a protected password file or your provider's secret tooling. Keep connection files outside the repository; do not put credentials into the command, report, or monitoring log. `-X` skips local psql startup customizations. Alternatively, run the SQL in the provider's authenticated SQL console.

For the local Docker database:

```sh
docker compose exec -T postgres sh -c 'psql -X --set=ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --username="$POSTGRES_USER" --dbname="$POSTGRES_DB"' < ops/storage-report.sql
```

| Column                  | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `database_bytes`        | Disk size of the connected database, including all its tables and indexes.                                                                                                                              |
| `send_total_bytes`      | Disk size of `public."Send"`, including its indexes and TOAST data. This is part of `database_bytes`, not an additional amount to add.                                                                  |
| `message_count`         | Exact count of all retained `Send` rows, across all delivery statuses (including queued and any unresolved legacy rows). Delivery receipts are separate and are not counted as messages.                |
| `message_content_bytes` | Combined logical byte length of all retained subjects and bodies, measured with `octet_length`. This is not disk usage: compression, row overhead, indexes, free space, and other columns are excluded. |

The size functions are documented in [PostgreSQL's database object size reference](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/functions-admin.html#FUNCTIONS-ADMIN-DBOBJECT). The exact count and content sum scan the table; schedule the weekly report during a quiet period as history grows. Sizes can change during concurrent activity, so treat them as an operational snapshot.

## Weekly review

Record the observation date in UTC, the four aggregate values, the production plan's actual storage allowance in bytes, and growth since the previous observation. Keep the record in a private operations log. Record only aggregate counts and sizes: no recipients, subjects, bodies, account identifiers, connection strings, or credentials.

Obtain the allowance from the actual production provider and plan; no allowance or cost estimate is assumed. Confirm whether the provider counts other databases, WAL, backups, or other storage toward that allowance. Compare `database_bytes` with the allowance and check the provider's own storage metric when its accounting differs. Private Blob attachments are outside PostgreSQL and are not covered by this report.

For database size `D`, allowance `A`, previous size `P`, and elapsed days `t`:

- Usage percentage: `100 * D / A`.
- Weekly growth in bytes: `(D - P) * 7 / t` (for positive `t`; a seven-day interval is simply `D - P`).
- Thirty-day projection: `D + max(0, (D - P) / t) * 30`.

Review retention when current usage reaches **70% of the allowance**, or the thirty-day projection reaches that threshold. Apply the same trigger to the provider's metric when it governs the allowance. The first observation establishes a baseline; record growth/projection as unavailable until there is a previous observation. A shrinking database does not imply future growth will stay zero.

This threshold triggers a review, never automatic deletion. Review the growth trend, provider accounting, and capacity options before changing retention.

## If retention becomes necessary

Prefer clearing subjects and bodies after **180 days**, while preserving history metadata, reply tracking, and follow-up functionality. Specify and disclose the exact policy before enabling it. This is a future direction, not an active policy. Preserve export, manual history deletion, delivery receipts, and campaign submission keys in any future implementation.

# Tailwind migration handoff

Updated 2026-11-03. **Completed.** The historical checkpoints below are retained
for traceability; their active-process and outstanding-work statements are stale.
See the final verification record at the end and `docs/tailwind-styling.md`.

## User intent and constraints

Finish the existing Tailwind migration and repair browser tests without redesigning
Mailloop. Preserve content, responsive layouts, interactions, and all pre-existing
working-tree changes. User wants implementation and verification, not another plan.
They requested faster execution and an account-switch handoff. Last rough estimate
was 2–3 hours remaining; this is uncertain and the full browser suite is not green.

Read AGENTS.md and the Tailwind skill at
`.agents/skills/tailwind-4-docs/SKILL.md`. Read relevant Next docs in
`node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before code changes. This session read CSS,
use-client and devIndicators guides. Tailwind snapshot is dated October 28.
Do not use subagents unless the user explicitly authorizes them.

Key constraints: no redesign, no API breaks or planned DB migration; authenticate
server actions and scope queries; no real Gmail/payment operations; Dodo test mode
only. DB/browser tests must use disposable databases through the runner. Never clear
the development DB. Preserve SystemControl initialization/settings and migrations.

Ordinary styling belongs in Tailwind on owning JSX. Keep justified CSS for themes,
motion, browser/native behavior, editor content, and complex responsive compositions.
Use semantic variables, color literals only in theme-tokens.css, `cn` for conflicts,
`css-hover:` for unconditional migrated CSS hover. Preserve exact inclusive
breakpoints and container boundaries 659/660/661, and test 320px.

## Working tree safety

The tree was already very dirty before this session (~130 files), including most
migration source files, AGENTS.md, scripts/test-usage-db.ts and
tests/history-allowance-pill.test.ts. Do NOT reset/revert wholesale. There are now
about 201 changed/untracked files. No commit has been created by this session.
A broad prettier run also formatted some previously clean, unrelated unit/DB test
files; review and remove only proven formatting-only incidental diffs if useful.
`docs/tailwind-styling.md` predated this session as an untracked prior-agent report:
its verification claims are stale and MUST be rewritten before finishing.

## Implemented so far

### Test infrastructure

- New `tests/helpers/system-control-browser.ts`: automatic per-test snapshot/restore
  of the complete SystemControl row. SQL `row_to_json` avoids timestamp timezone
  shifts; `json_populate_record` restores all columns except ID. Isolated DB guard.
  Baseline sending enabled, paid gating disabled; tests opt into gating explicitly.
  Browser DB fixtures now extend it. Callback named runFixture (not use).

  usage backfill/cutover fields. Shared settings restore even on test failures.
- `scripts/test-usage-db.ts` passes TZ=UTC to worker/server environment. Browser
  timezone is explicitly Asia/Kolkata in playwright.config.ts. Runner accepts
  --grep=, --grep-invert=, --project=, --reporter=, --output=, --config= and snapshots.
- `npm run test:e2e` uses the disposable runner, not bare Playwright.
- Isolated dev server hides Next development indicators. actionTimeout=10s.
- New compact browser-reporter.ts, screenshot.css (caret/dev indicator hiding),
  public-visual.spec.ts (desktop1440/mobile320 public routes/themes).

### Theme audit and screenshots

- Fixed populated audit ledger fixtures (valid reservation/evidence, fixed sentAt,

Expected height2195, actual2185 (Premium expected2205 actual2195). Diff inspected:

changed field borders and fills has been removed, keeping search focus on its
wrapper and preserving Contacts autofill paint. This is an intentional focus
behavior correction; resting controls retain their existing appearance.

Workspace access-refresh events request fresh server entitlements even when a
quota poll is pending or unavailable. Downgrades retain the saved theme preference
while falling back; restored Premium access reapplies that preference. Tooltips
reposition after ancestor entrance animations and hover transitions finish.

Browser matrices set preferences in storage before navigation, without accumulating
initialization scripts. Measurements wait for fonts, finite animations and actual
content; allowance bar ratios are polled until their animation reaches its target.
Assertions follow the current template editor navigation, appearance-specific
tutorial corners, layered Premium surfaces and scoped legacy allowances. Deletion
interception distinguishes confirmation submissions from status polling and checks
retryable errors, disabled pending controls and delayed sign-out. Background
sending-status polls authenticate without redirecting when access is revoked, so
they cannot interrupt the deletion confirmation delay or lose `/?deleted=1`. The
launch-controls test forces a poll during that delay. Tutorial close restores focus
after React commits the dialog removal and launcher visibility, avoiding a frame
callback that could run while the launcher was still hidden.

tolerances, accessibility rules and the serial worker configuration are unchanged.
