## Timer ring, Premium shine and allowance outlines (2026-11-12)

The landing timer's drop-shadow now belongs to a full-size HTML wrapper around
the SVG. Rotation remains on the SVG; the centered countdown stays outside the
shadow wrapper. The panel tilt, floating animation, reveal, progress and palette
are unchanged. The reported disappearance was not reproduced in headless Chrome
before this change, so a browser compositing cause remains unconfirmed.

Shared Premium button shines now use a six-second cycle: a two-second round trip
and four-second rest, retaining the three-second initial delay. Shared pricing
allowance boxes now have a subtle one-pixel outline using `--upgrade-border`,
including dark mode. These outlines intentionally change the pricing visuals
without changing box dimensions. Existing screenshot references remain fixed.

Verification: the disposable landing, rendered ring, public visual, primary-action
and Premium-upgrade suites passed 68 checks with eight viewport/hover skips.
Ring captures cover 1440px, 1100px and 768px, both direct theme loads, repeated
switching during sending, paused and completed states, reduced motion and the
View Transition fallback. Captures are in `/tmp/mailloop-ring-shine-after`;
all public references passed without update mode. TypeScript, changed-file lint,
formatting, color and whitespace checks passed. The runner cleaned up its
disposable database and server.

## Public visual references (2026-11-12)

The current compact public pricing cards and mobile landing layout were reviewed
against the previous references. The mobile landing page is shorter because the
pricing cards use the compact layout; the pricing page retains both plans,
comparison table, fine print and footer. Privacy and terms retain their content
and responsive layout. The user chose to keep this design, so the 28 public
visual references were regenerated with the disposable browser fixture and the
full public visual suite passed again without update mode.

Chalk queued indicators now use bright golden yellow instead of dark amber
(2026-11-10). This intentional palette change covers the batch ring, progress
bar, queued markers and their hover tint; status text retains its darker ink.
Usage allowance bars and queued legend dots share this yellow. Healthy allowance
rings retain Chalk's black ink, and warning text retains its darker amber.
Desktop and mobile progress-card checks passed using the disposable database
runner. Before/after captures are in `/tmp/mailloop-progress-before` and
`/tmp/mailloop-progress-after`; screenshot references were not updated.

Ordinary component layout, spacing, typography, colors, borders and interaction
states belong in Tailwind utilities beside their owning JSX. Reuse the existing UI
components and `cn`; use explicit component variants when shared controls need
different layouts. Keep React components and outgoing email HTML in their existing
roles.

## Rules

- Use the existing semantic variables and Tailwind color mappings. Keep color
  literals in `src/app/theme-tokens.css`; run `npm run check:colors`.
- Write complete utility strings in conditional branches or explicit maps. Never
  construct a utility name from fragments. Use `cn` for conflicting utilities,
  including arbitrary padding/font sizes and important variants.
- Preserve exact measurements, media/container query boundaries, native behavior,
  and reduced-motion behavior. A nearby default breakpoint can change the UI.
- Use `css-hover:` when moving an unconditional CSS `:hover` rule. Existing
  Tailwind `hover:` rules retain their pointer capability condition.
- Keep animation and test hooks stable. Class names generated by CSS Modules are
  implementation details; test semantic controls and visible behavior.
- Use important utilities only where an existing unlayered native/theme adapter
  must be overridden. Do not add global overrides to patch ordinary layout.
- Preserve runtime measurements through CSS variables/inline styles. Avoid large
  `@apply` blocks and long descendant utility chains where a child component can
  own its styles.

## Why CSS remains

The migration removes ordinary styling from JSX consumers rather than targeting a
stylesheet count. The following groups still have responsibilities that need CSS:

| Files                                                                | Responsibility                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `src/app/theme-tokens.css`                                           | Centralized palettes, color literals and appearance-specific theme values.                                                                                                     |
| `src/app/globals.css`                                                | Tailwind setup and semantic mappings, native element behavior, shared focus/autofill/dialog/table cascade, navigation container behavior, help/tutorial and completion motion. |
| `src/app/workspace-theme.css`, `compose-theme.css`                   | Workspace/Compose theme bindings, shared native controls, scoped state and illustration palettes.                                                                              |
| `src/app/preview-highlight.css`, `src/components/compose.module.css` | Scoped editor/preview marks, browser text decoration behavior, personalization and search motion.                                                                              |
| `src/app/appearance-control.css`                                     | Preview palettes, menu/theme view transitions and motion reset. Geometry and option states are utilities in the component.                                                     |
| `src/app/(app)/templates/template-editor.css`                        | Editor content/native input behavior, form-slot cascade, safe-area composition and motion.                                                                                     |
| `src/components/settings/settings.module.css`                        | Theme bindings, native disabled/focus/dialog behavior and responsive navigation marker pseudo-element.                                                                         |
| `src/components/contacts/contacts.module.css`                        | Contacts palettes, native controls/focus, and scoped shared form/import/action-slot adapters.                                                                                  |
| `src/components/history/history.module.css`                          | History palette bindings, responsive semantic-table/grid composition and shared action/status state cascade.                                                                   |
| `src/components/templates/templates.module.css`                      | Library palette bindings, native meter parts, focus/motion and shared control/theme adapters.                                                                                  |
| `src/components/usage/usage.module.css`                              | Usage palettes/font-face, portaled surfaces and native gauge motion.                                                                                                           |
| `src/components/limit-banner.module.css`                             | Decorative stripe, pip/detail/chevron motion and native focus.                                                                                                                 |
| `src/components/ui/Tooltip.module.css`                               | Portaled theme surfaces, arbitrary content links/focus and bubble motion.                                                                                                      |
| `src/components/PricingPage.module.css`                              | Arbitrary action-slot adapters, theme inheritance, native focus/table boundary and card motion.                                                                                |
| `src/components/pricing/pricing.css`                                 | Public theme/root scrollbars, safe-area/native focus and theme transitions.                                                                                                    |
| `src/components/landing/landing.css`                                 | Public palettes, hydration-independent theme painting, complex overlapping hero/illustration responsive compositions and motion.                                               |
| `src/components/landing/lower-sections.css`, `pricing-section.css`   | Section palettes, decorative pseudo-elements, native focus, hover/reduced-motion composition and gutter alignment.                                                             |

When changing a remaining group, identify its consumers and cascade before removing
it. Move ordinary child styles onto children where practical, and delete obsolete
rules/imports after verification.

## Browser fixtures and baselines

Run browsers through `npm run test:e2e` or the disposable runner:

```sh
npx tsx scripts/test-usage-db.ts --e2e-only --browser=public-visual,theme-audit
```

The runner creates and removes a disposable database, provisions the restricted
admin role, and starts its own host Next server with fake Gmail/billing credentials.
Never point these fixtures at the development database or an existing app server.
It accepts `--grep=`, `--grep-invert=`, `--project=`, `--reporter=`, `--output=`, and
`--config=` for focused checks. Only intentional baseline establishment uses
`--update-snapshots`.

The shared browser fixture snapshots and restores the complete initialized
`SystemControl` row after each test, including failed tests. Plan, Gmail, quota
ledger and billing states are explicit. Worker/server timestamps use UTC; browser
local display uses Asia/Kolkata. Free audits cover Lavender/Nightbloom; Premium
covers all four themes. Theme checks inspect required semantic values and variables
actually consumed by the page, including scoped/portaled surfaces.

Workspace baselines were refreshed against corrected fixtures before the styling
batches. Public baselines cover landing, pricing, privacy and terms. Fonts and
hydration settle, animations are controlled, development indicators are hidden and
reset dates/data are fixed. Keep these references fixed during migration; inspect
and repair differences rather than updating snapshots to make a refactor pass.

## Intentional bug-fix differences

- Public pricing cards use a shared heading/badge row and tighter card, allowance,
  and feature spacing on mobile (2026-11-11). Every feature remains visible.
  Before/after captures are in `/tmp/mailloop-pricing-before` and
  `/tmp/mailloop-pricing-after`; all eight desktop card captures are identical.
  Established screenshot references remain unchanged.
- Purple gradient action/ribbon ink and Chalk muted plan text have accessible
  contrast. Solid accent controls retain their separate ink mapping.
- A pricing header that overflowed by7px at320px uses a smaller logo below360px.
- Focused Contacts autofill retains its inset background paint and focus outline.
- The Usage upgrade action retains its intrinsic label width, wraps when needed,
  and uses smaller horizontal padding in the two-column card. The current-plan
  header stacks below a 320px container so Premium fits at 280px. Overflow checks
  cover 659/660/661px and 800/960/1200px without clipping.
- History locked shortlist tooltips retain in-shortlist, unavailable-contact and
  pending-delivery explanations alongside the Premium upgrade link.
- The editor tabpanel is a valid wrapper; the form ID used by Save is preserved.
- Admin retries can read the usage-reset field through the restricted role. The
  regression test requires rollback after failure, retained request IDs and one
  audit record after the successful retry.

## Verification status

Completed 2026-11-03. Final source passes color checks, Prettier, lint, TypeScript,
418 unit tests and the production build. Prior disposable database verification
passed 326 database tests plus the separate 101-test usage suite and backfill dry
run; this continuation made no database or provider changes.

The complete desktop/mobile browser run executed all 516 cases: 500 passed,
4 failed, and 12 retained their existing project-specific skips. The four failures
were the duplicate-warning palette-loading assertion, Free/Premium Usage visual
audits and plan-card overflow. Each was repaired and passed fresh targeted reruns.
Thus all 504 runnable browser cases have passing verification, with no unresolved
failures or new skips. This is a full run plus targeted reruns, not a claim that
one uninterrupted full invocation was green.

Final Free/Premium screenshot audits and both plan-card tests passed together
against unchanged references. Public landing/pricing/policy comparisons passed
on desktop and mobile in the complete run. Coverage includes 320px viewports,
659/660/661px containers, 280px Premium content, both appearances, light/dark,
menus/dialogs/tooltips, keyboard focus, hover/disabled controls, editor tabs,
previews, navigation and reduced motion. Skeleton/media assertions wait for
streamed styles, and mobile editor checks wait for the actual tab controls.
The touch palette check centers its swatch and verifies the hit target before
sending a touch event, avoiding the fixed help launcher.

Evidence:

- `/tmp/mailloop-browser-complete.log`: complete run, 500 passed / 4 failed /
  12 existing skipped; no mobile failures.
- `/tmp/mailloop-browser-final-retests.log`: duplicate-warning retest and Premium
  audit/plan-card passes; the intermediate Free screenshot failure was corrected.
- `/tmp/mailloop-browser-visual-final.log`: final Free/Premium audits and both
  plan-card tests, 4 passed / 0 failed.
- `/tmp/mailloop-pending-last-targets.log`: final desktop/mobile skeleton and
  tooltip lifecycle checks, 6 passed / 0 failed.
- `/tmp/mailloop-unit-verified.log`, `/tmp/mailloop-format-verified.log`,
  `/tmp/mailloop-lint-verified.log`, `/tmp/mailloop-types-verified.log`,
  `/tmp/mailloop-build-verified.log`: final static/unit/build checks.

All disposable browser databases and servers were cleaned up. No screenshot
references were updated during this completion continuation.

## Pricing card redesign (2026-11-03)

Landing pricing, `/pricing`, and the upgrade dialog now reuse
`src/components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx`. Caller-owned actions, authentication,
localized price resolution, monthly billing, allowances and all feature groups
are preserved. The card redesign intentionally changes rounded surfaces, corner
lighting, dot texture, decorative orbs, feature dividers and the inset Recommended
badge. The badge retains `data-recommended-ribbon` as a stable browser hook.
The Recommended label is 11.5px; Premium actions retain their original theme ink.
Decorative pointer lighting is disabled for reduced motion.

Established public screenshot baselines remain fixed. Their pricing comparisons

## Campaign status card hover (2026-11-10)

Campaign progress status cards reuse the shared 6px lift and 350ms transition,
with an 8% semantic status tint and softened matching glow. Sent uses success,
Queued uses queued, Failed uses error, and Cancelled uses muted body ink. The
neutral workspace hover suppression excludes only these cards. Reduced motion
removes their lift and transitions while retaining color feedback; touch taps
retain resting styles. Counts, labels, dimensions and layout are unchanged.

All eight desktop/mobile checks passed through the disposable database runner
for Lavender, Nightbloom, Chalk and Obsidian, including individual hover/return,
stationary siblings and parent, reduced motion, touch and overflow. Before/after
captures are in `/tmp/mailloop-progress-before` and
`/tmp/mailloop-progress-after`; all eight resting card captures are pixel-identical.
Hovered and reduced-motion captures were reviewed across all four palettes.
Color validation, TypeScript, scoped lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass.
Established screenshot references were not updated.

## Chalk and Obsidian interaction contrast (2026-11-10)

The shared interaction adapter now gives neutral primary actions a solid resting
paint and explicit hover/pressed paints: Chalk moves from near-black to charcoal;
Obsidian moves from off-white to light gray. Primary links and native buttons use
the same states. Outline and ghost controls use stronger neutral fills, and outline
borders strengthen on hover. Destructive actions retain their semantic red with
separate hover and pressed tones. Color transitions last 180ms; these neutral
controls retain their dimensions and position on hover and press. Keyboard
outlines, reduced-motion resets, touch hover suppression and unavailable/busy
state exclusions remain. Premium gradient and shine actions are excluded.

Required neutral control borders now use the existing accessible input-boundary
values, including Usage's scoped/portaled control palette and the shared search
wrappers in Templates, Contacts and History. Decorative card borders
remain separate. The review covers Compose, Templates, Contacts, History, Usage,
Settings, the Billing redirect to Settings' plan section, Pricing, help dialogs,
account menus and destructive confirmations. Muted text and semantic statuses
retain their existing palettes, including Chalk's yellow queue indicators.

These are intentional visual changes; established screenshot references were not
replaced. Desktop/mobile before and after captures and contrast records are under
`/tmp/mailloop-neutral-interactions-before` and
`/tmp/mailloop-neutral-interactions-after`. Primary/native/link/destructive state
captures are under `/tmp/mailloop-neutral-buttons-before` and
`/tmp/mailloop-neutral-buttons-after`; secondary/ghost captures use the existing
`/tmp/mailloop-buttons-before` and `/tmp/mailloop-buttons-after` directories.

The new palette review asserts numerical contrast corrections for the two neutral
themes and runs axe across all four. Its numeric report also records the existing
Lavender/Nightbloom primary gradient endpoint ratios (3.18/3.34:1 with white small
text); those palettes are outside this change's scope. This is not a claim that
all four palettes meet every numerical contrast threshold.

Final verification: the eight integrated Chalk/Obsidian desktop/mobile page and
primary/link/icon/destructive checks passed together, including held touch,
pressed/focus contrast, disabled/busy states and reduced motion. All eight routes
have zero measured contrast failures, unresolved required variables or axe
violations in these neutral captures. Outline/ghost checks passed for all four
palettes on desktop and mobile; Lavender/Nightbloom primary checks and page reviews
also passed, with the gradient endpoint findings above retained in the reports.
The help/account/destructive-dialog matrix passed on desktop (its existing mobile
skip remains). These results include targeted reruns after test hydration,
redirect and touch-release timing fixes; they are not one uninterrupted run.

Color validation, all 14 color tests, lint, TypeScript, formatting and whitespace
checks passed. Concurrent Settings danger colors were retained while their token
names were reconciled as semantic aliases, avoiding duplicate canonical
primitives. No screenshot references were replaced. Evidence includes
`/tmp/mailloop-neutral-integrated-final.log`,
`/tmp/mailloop-neutral-final.log`, `/tmp/mailloop-neutral-after.log` and
`/tmp/mailloop-neutral-unit-final.log`. Disposable databases and servers were
cleaned up by the runner.

## Mobile landing polish and shared Premium shine (2026-11-11)

Below 640px the landing batch illustration's complete wrapper is hidden, including
its decorative layers and layout space. Hero type, CTA sizing, vertical spacing
and section gutters are tighter; the Google button fits within the 320px gutters.
Feature cards now use one readable mobile column, two from 640px and three from
861px. Explicit pixel breakpoints avoid conflicting arbitrary media rules and
mixed-unit ordering. Tablet and desktop retain the batch illustration.

Premium upgrade buttons share `.upgrade-shine::before`: one narrow, automatic
left-to-right-and-back sweep lasting 1.5 seconds, then three seconds at rest.
The first sweep also waits three seconds; the effect stays beneath the text. The existing
`--upgrade-shine` palette keeps it visible in all four themes. Disabled,
`aria-disabled`, busy and reduced-motion states remove the effect. The dialog's
separate hover shine is removed; small Premium text links remain static. Existing
pricing-card edits and checkout/authentication behavior are preserved.

Intentional screenshot differences are the mobile illustration removal, tighter
spacing and aligned gutters, readable feature grid and restored spaces in the
hero highlights. Established screenshot references are unchanged. Before captures
are in `/tmp/mailloop-mobile-polish-before`; reviewed final captures are in
`/tmp/mailloop-mobile-polish-after`. Browser artifacts are also emitted by
`mobile-landing.spec.ts` into the Playwright output directory.

Validation: the disposable desktop/touch run passed 33 landing and feature
behavior checks. The timing clarification arrived during that run; focused
reruns passed the four remaining motion/link cases after updating the assertions
and waiting for streamed Settings content. Five existing viewport/hover matrix
skips remain. This is a full run plus passing targeted reruns, not one uninterrupted
green invocation. Forward/reverse travel, a 1.5-second round trip, the full
three-second rest, initial delay, disabled/busy/reduced-motion states and static
text links are covered. TypeScript, changed-source lint, formatting and color
checks passed. Disposable databases and servers were cleaned up.

title: docs/theme-audit/README.md
text:
# Four-theme audit

The application uses `src/app/theme-tokens.css` for color literals. Existing
semantic aliases and page scopes preserve the cascade. Chalk and Obsidian use
neutral highlights, links, focus rings and progress colors. Purple themes retain
their identity with corrections for measured contrast failures.

Color checking runs before tests and production builds. Exact exceptions for
standalone SVGs and browser metadata are documented in
[`scripts/color-exceptions.json`](../../scripts/color-exceptions.json).

## Verification and remaining findings

The original audit covered Compose, Templates, Contacts, Usage, History and
Settings in all four themes at 1440, 1024, 768 and 390 CSS pixels, using disposable
empty Free and populated Premium accounts. It captured 192 viewport screenshots
and established 48 [desktop regression baselines](../../tests/browser/theme-audit.spec.ts-snapshots).
No emails were sent and no payments were initiated.

The final verification measured **17,960 contrast pairs with zero failures**
(23 browser tests passed; 7 duplicate mobile cases were skipped). See the compact
[results](results.md), [summary](summary.json), [token changes](token-changes.json),
[style corrections](style-changes.json) and
[indicator measurements](indicator-contrast.json).

The audit is not an accessibility certification. These existing findings remain:

- Every theme: axe reports toast content outside a landmark
  (`.success-toast > p`, moderate `region` violation).
- Chalk Settings and Nightbloom History: fixed help/skip controls appear over
  printed content. Other print combinations may share this layout issue.
- Chalk and Obsidian Compose at 390px: the help launcher overlaps the shortlist
  header/count area.
- Actual 200% browser zoom and native Windows controls/print dialogs were not
  verified. Chromium forced-colors emulation and print-to-PDF were exercised.

[Manual findings](manual-findings.json) retain the affected pages and reasons.
The original change was restricted to presentation colors; semantic and layout
fixes remain separate work. Native saved-credential autofill, every tooltip and
payload, and all empty/populated × Free/Premium combinations are not certified.

## Run the checks

```sh
npm test -- --exclude 'tests/*.db.test.ts'
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm run test:themes
npm run audit:themes:report
MAILLOOP_E2E_ISOLATED=1 npm run build
```

`test:themes` owns a disposable Docker PostgreSQL database and a host-run Next.js
server on port 3100. It validates the local test database before creating UUID
fixtures. The dedicated audit cases are skipped by ordinary browser runs, which
may use a different database. Do not run the isolated build alongside this test
server: both use `.next-e2e`.

Screenshots, print PDFs and raw measurements are regenerated under ignored
`test-results/`. `audit:themes:report` writes its detailed CSV/JSON/Markdown to
`test-results/theme-audit/`; it does not modify tracked documentation. Those
large diagnostic files and duplicate review images are intentionally not kept
in Git. The compact documents above preserve the historical findings.

To intentionally replace reviewed baselines:
`npm run test:themes -- --update-snapshots`. Baselines are regression references,
not comparisons against screenshots of the original application. Measurements
composite transparency, include text opacity, and sample gradient stops and
interpolations; they are not per-glyph raster measurements. Thresholds are 4.5:1
for normal/placeholder/disabled text and 3:1 for large text and required controls,
progress and focus indicators.

title: docs/upgrade-modal.md
text:
# Premium upgrade modal

The modal follows the supplied “Mailloop – Upgrade modal pp.html” reference.
Only the comparison body scrolls. The header, feature chip, checkout action,
dismiss action, and pricing link remain visible. Premium appears first below
700px. Both cards reuse the existing `CardSpotlight` cursor tracking; their glow,
theme transitions, and button shine respect reduced motion.

## Audit and theme decisions

The previous modal used a native dialog and shared the public pricing cards.
The repo had no shadcn Dialog primitive or Radix Dialog dependency. The approved
implementation adds `@radix-ui/react-dialog` and a local shadcn-style primitive,
while leaving public pricing cards unchanged.

The modal reuses the existing font mappings, `--ring` for keyboard focus,
`--plan-card-spotlight` for the subtle cursor glow, and `--on-accent` for the
existing semantic backdrop treatment. The approved palette
choice uses dedicated modal colors rather than substituting the app's different
background, card, foreground, muted, and border values.

`src/app/theme-tokens.css` defines `--upgrade-app`, `--upgrade-surface`,
`--upgrade-surface2`, `--upgrade-text`, `--upgrade-muted`, `--upgrade-border`,
`--upgrade-grad`, `--upgrade-btn-fg`, `--upgrade-glow`, `--upgrade-ok`,
`--upgrade-okbg`, `--upgrade-dot`, `--upgrade-shine`, `--upgrade-check`, and the
checkmark mask. The selectors are, in cascade order:

1. `:root` (Lavender)
2. `html[data-theme="dark"]` (Nightbloom)
3. `html[data-theme="light"][data-appearance="vercel"]` (Chalk)
4. `html[data-theme="dark"][data-appearance="vercel"]` (Obsidian)

Only changed variables are overridden. `globals.css` maps colors and shadows
through `@theme inline`, and provides the gradient utility and scoped decorative
rules. No theme-switching or storage code was added.

The supplied purple gradients failed AA with white button text. Lavender uses
`#6f4ac5 → #9a45b3`; Nightbloom uses `#765ccc → #a54dbe`. Nightbloom's smaller
darkening also preserves contrast for the large gradient stat numbers on their
dark tiles. The shine stays at the button edges to preserve label contrast.
Prices continue using the caller's localized value, including ₹299 for India.

## Opening with feature context

Inside the existing provider:

```tsx
const openUpgrade = usePremiumUpgrade();
openUpgrade({ feature: "roles", trigger: event.currentTarget });
```

| Key              | Existing entry point / highlighted row                                                      |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `roles`          | Compose role control and Premium role lock / recipient role editing                         |
| `reminders`      | Reminder settings controls and Save / follow-up reminders                                   |
| `replied`        | History Mark replied / reply tracking                                                       |
| `csv`            | Contacts CSV import / CSV import                                                            |
| `templates`      | Extra or retained template editor, template locks, Compose picker / templates and shortcuts |
| `shortlist`      | History shortlist actions / History shortcut                                                |
| `themes`         | Locked Chalk/Obsidian options, including appearance-menu fallback / all four themes         |
| `role-shortcuts` | Outreach preferences at the Free shortcut limit / templates and shortcuts                   |
| `highlights`     | Locked preview color / preview highlight colors                                             |
| `repeat`         | Existing repeat-send gates / manual repeat sends                                            |

`trigger` is optional; the provider captures the active element when omitted.
`openUpgrade()` displays the roles chip with no highlighted row. An explicit key
highlights exactly one row. The direct component also accepts
`<PremiumUpgradeDialog feature="roles" onClose={close} />`.

Shared `FeatureLock` and `PremiumLock` components accept `upgradeFeature`
separately from their descriptive `feature` label. Existing allowance reasons,
details, gating, and fallback actions are retained. The checkout handler is
unchanged; this change does not alter billing or checkout behavior.

## Files changed by this redesign

- `package.json`, `package-lock.json`
- `src/app/theme-tokens.css`, `src/app/globals.css`
- `src/components/ui/dialog.tsx`
- `src/components/premium-upgrade-dialog.tsx`, `premium-upgrade-provider.tsx`
- `src/components/feature-lock.tsx`, `premium-lock.tsx`
- `src/components/compose.tsx`, `forms.tsx`, `appearance-control.tsx`, `preview-highlight.tsx`
- `src/components/contacts/ImportContacts.tsx`, `ContactShortlistAction.tsx`
- `src/components/history/RowActions.tsx`
- `src/components/settings/FollowUpReminders.tsx`, `OutreachPreferences.tsx`
- `src/app/(app)/templates/page.tsx`
- `tests/browser/premium-upgrade.spec.ts`, `feature-gates.spec.ts`, `appearance.spec.ts`
- `docs/upgrade-modal.md`

Existing screenshot references remain unchanged. Browser tests use disposable
databases and fake provider credentials through `scripts/test-usage-db.ts`.

## Verification

- TypeScript, ESLint, color-literal checks, formatting, and production build passed.
- All 418 runnable unit tests passed; database-only tests retain their existing skips.
- 35 distinct focused browser cases passed across the final run and targeted reruns.
  Five duplicate mobile cases are intentionally skipped because those tests own
  their viewport/theme matrices. The two initial light-theme failures came from
  the new contrast helper not expanding shorthand hex; both passed after fixing
  the helper. No visual baseline was updated.
- Coverage includes all four palettes, 320/360/390px widths, the 699/700px breakpoint,
  fixed header/footer, access to the last feature, focus containment/restoration,
  live changes through the existing switcher, cursor spotlight, reduced motion,
  feature contexts, localized pricing, and unchanged checkout retry requests.
- The embedded `startCheckout` handler was compared with its original source and
  remains byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Shared public card design (2026-11-04)

The modal and public pricing now share `pricing/plan-card.tsx`, including the
compact features, context metadata, configuration-derived stats, texture, border,
and cursor glow. The modal still owns its scrolling body and fixed checkout
footer. The public `PricingCards` wrapper adds bottom-aligned caller actions and
uses “Free plan” unless the signed-in user's current plan is Free. Premium's
badge also identifies the current plan when applicable. This supersedes the
historical note above that public cards were left unchanged.

title: docs/usage-ledger-rollout.md
text:
# Usage ledger rollout

Prisma remains pinned to 7.10.0. Campaign and worker integrations must deploy
as one runtime release. Schema migrations can deploy first. Neither migration
nor backfill enables paid gating.

## Verify on disposable PostgreSQL 16

```sh
npm run db:generate
npm run test:usage:db
npm test -- --fileParallelism=false
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
```

The runner creates a unique Docker Compose project with a random loopback port,
a random password, a `_test` database and tmpfs storage. It never connects to the
inherited development database. It runs the usage suites and the complete database
suite, then removes only that project's resources. Do not run database suites
against development data. Do not reset or drop production accounting tables.

## Cutover and backfill

1. Apply reviewed additive schema with `npm run db:deploy`. Generate the pinned
   Prisma client. Keep `paidGatingEnabled=false`.
2. Pause sending with `SystemControl.sendingEnabled=false` and stop old worker
   processes. Drain active Gmail requests before recording cutover; leases last
   two minutes, but a missing lease on an old worker requires an explicit drain.
   Do not convert attempting or uncertain work to READY. Install both runtime
   integrations while sending is paused.
3. Preview without committing any changes:

   ```sh
   npm run usage:backfill -- --dry-run
   ```

4. Apply only while sending remains paused and old workers are drained:

   ```sh
   npm run usage:backfill -- --apply
   ```

   The script records one `SystemControl.usageCutoverAt`. Every owner commits
   evidence, reservations, counters, validation, `usageCutoverAt`, and backfill
   version together. Failed owners roll back without a checkpoint; later owners
   continue. Resume with the same command. Completed owners are revalidated on
   rerun. Existing READY expiry is the original cutover plus 24 elapsed hours;
   neither reruns nor redispatch extend it. New queues expire after 24 hours.

5. Repeat the apply command to validate resumability. Require zero failed owners
   and no missing accounting before any activation. Restart the new workers and
   restore `sendingEnabled` when the cutover succeeds. A failed cutover remains
   paused until repaired.
6. Paid gating is a separate explicit operational change. The implementation,
   migrations, dry run, and apply command never flip that flag. Verify both flag
   states before activating it. Gated owners without validated accounting fail
   closed; genuinely empty new owners can initialize under their owner lock.

## Accounting and expected differences

Daily periods are UTC midnight to midnight. Free and complimentary Paid access
use UTC calendar months; actual paid subscriptions retain the exact provider
subscription ID and start/end timestamps. Grace extends that same allowance's
operational end; it does not grant a second allowance. An unresolved active
provider boundary pauses sending. A verified downgrade uses the Free calendar
month and includes paid attempts that occurred within that month. Unused capacity
does not roll over. No template, CSV, role, or reminder gating is added here.

Charges follow claim time, including an in-flight request crossing midnight.
Retained historical success uses `attemptedAt`, falling back to `sentAt` with
provenance recorded. Old receipts cannot recover a missing attempt time: their
`sentAt` fallback may approximate attribution near midnight. An unresolved legacy
attempt without an attempt timestamp is conservatively attributed to its creation
time and remains uncertain. Only known exact historical provider boundaries are
assigned directly; durable evidence seeds every subsequently created overlapping
allowance. Each charge is counted once per period, as a direct ledger reservation
or an imported baseline. Send deletion sets the ledger link to null; receipts keep
the stable delivery key and import evidence survives all history deletion.

The backfill independently reconstructs counters with SQL and validates retained
Send/Receipt identities. It also reports the unchanged legacy rolling-24-hour query.
Rolling totals and calendar totals are intentionally different: a previous UTC day's
success can remain in the rolling total, today's queued send may retain its original
reservation when deferring, and an uncertain attempt older than 24 hours stops counting
in legacy usage while still occupying its historical ledger allowance. Do not require
rolling and calendar totals to match or use their difference to issue refunds.

## Reconciliation and operational signals

The signed Inngest endpoint registers `quota-reconciliation` hourly
(`0 * * * *`, UTC), using one `reconcile-owners` step.
It pages owner IDs, settles durable acceptance, expires abandoned leases into
uncertainty, releases proven unsent terminal/expired work once, reconstructs counters,
and repairs publication after commit. A failed owner does not block others.
Publication repairs increment the dispatch generation/event ID, preserving both
the Send and delivery key. Deferrals use `availableAt`; quota waits do not create
long-running sleep loops. Definite rejections release reservations and finish
without another sending attempt. Legacy queued retries are finalized without
resubmission; their old counters remain only as evidence.

Campaign submission still dispatches immediately. Interrupted publication,
deferred sends, and accounting recovery can wait up to one hour after becoming
eligible; normal pacing still applies before the first sending attempt.
Already-sent and uncertain deliveries are never automatically resent.

`maintenance` runs daily at 03:00 UTC / 08:30 IST (`0 3 * * *`). Its single
discovery step paginates accounts internally and returns only IDs needing cleanup:
active accounts with unused attachments awaiting physical deletion. Account
deletion is owned by the separate daily deletion sweep. Current attachments and those
needed by queued, attempting, or uncertain sends remain protected. A prior
`deletedAt` marker does not exclude unfinished storage deletion. Events are sent
in batches of 100; an idle discovery emits none. The existing per-account worker
rechecks eligibility under its existing locks. Attachment backlogs beyond its
ten-file limit continue on later daily passes. Cleanup may wait up to one day
after becoming eligible, and provider failures can extend that delay.

With no pending work, the registered schedules now use at least 56 execution
units/day or 1,680 per 30 days. This includes the daily deletion-job sweep
(three steps), hourly quota reconciliation (at least one owner page),
daily attachment maintenance, and daily rate-limit
cleanup. Operator monitoring and alert delivery have been removed. Inngest counts
both function runs and steps ([execution limits](https://www.inngest.com/docs/durable-execution/limits)).
Sending, pacing, extra pages, account cleanup and retries add usage. Measure a
controlled campaign before estimating customer capacity.

After deployment, synchronize the current endpoint registrations. Verify
`account-deletion-jobs` uses `0 2 * * *` UTC,
`rate-limit-cleanup` uses `0 4 * * *` UTC, `quota-reconciliation` uses
`0 * * * *`, and `maintenance` uses `0 3 * * *`. Confirm
`minimum-hardening-monitor`, `operator-alert-delivery`, `scheduled-replies`, and
`refresh-replies`, and `deletion-maintenance` are absent. Deployment and production synchronization are
separate rollout steps.

Warnings contain only operational codes and owner/send UUIDs. Monitor
`UNCERTAINTY_OLDER_THAN_15_MINUTES`, `PUBLICATION_DELAY`, `COUNTER_DRIFT`,
`OUTSTANDING_ORPHAN`, `MISSING_ACCOUNTING`, `REPAIR_FAILED`, `PUBLICATION_FAILED`,
and `SETTLEMENT_FAILED`. Orphans are alerts, never automatic refunds. Gmail and the
database cannot guarantee atomic exactly-once acceptance. Ambiguous network failures
or lost acceptance persistence retain capacity and prevent automatic resend.
No Sent search or delivery-resolution controls are introduced. Mark replied and
Undo affect reply state only.

## Rollback

Disable paid gating to restore rolling-200 enforcement while retaining ledger
writes, claim leases, duplicate protection, and reconciliation. If accounting itself
fails, pause sending, drain workers, and repair forward. Preserve all added tables,
source identities, and uncertain attempts. Never refund an ambiguity or put it back
into READY. Do not run destructive down migrations.

BEGIN;

-- Inline each owner's saved URL, including archived templates. Use a callback-free
-- replacement escape so URL backslashes cannot be interpreted as regexp escapes.
UPDATE "Template" AS template
SET "body" = regexp_replace(
  template."body",
  '\{\{[[:space:]]*link[[:space:]]*\}\}',
  replace(owner."linkUrl", E'\\', E'\\\\'),
  'g'
)
FROM "User" AS owner
WHERE template."userId" = owner."id"
  AND owner."linkUrl" IS NOT NULL
  AND btrim(owner."linkUrl") <> ''
  AND template."body" ~ '\{\{[[:space:]]*link[[:space:]]*\}\}';

-- Queued and historical Send snapshots are deliberately untouched.
ALTER TABLE "User" DROP COLUMN "linkUrl";

COMMIT;

generator client {

model User {
  id                     String                @id @default(uuid())

  templates              Template[]
  contacts               Contact[]
  campaigns              Campaign[]
  attachments            Attachment[]
  deliveryReceipts       DeliveryReceipt[]
  usagePeriods           UsagePeriod[]
  usageReservations      UsageReservation[]
  usageImportEvidence    UsageImportEvidence[]
  usageBackfillVersion   Int                   @default(0)
  usageCutoverAt         DateTime?
  testingUsageResetAt    DateTime?

  plan                  Plan                  @default(FREE)
  subscriptionStatus    SubscriptionStatus    @default(NONE)
  currentPeriodStart    DateTime?
  currentPeriodEnd      DateTime?
  dodoCustomerId        String?               @unique
  dodoSubscriptionId    String?               @unique
  cancelAtPeriodEnd     Boolean               @default(false)
  gracePeriodEnd        DateTime?
  billingCountry        String?

  billingStateVersion   Int                   @default(0)
  lastBillingEventAt    DateTime?
  planOverride          Plan?
  planOverrideStartsAt  DateTime?
  planOverrideExpiresAt DateTime?
  planOverrideReason    String?
  grandfatheredUntil    DateTime?
  freeTemplateId        String?
  isAdmin               Boolean               @default(false)
  isSuspended           Boolean               @default(false)
  suspendedAt           DateTime?
  suspensionReason      String?
  lastActiveAt          DateTime?
  accountNotices        AccountNotice[]
  billingRateLimits     BillingRateLimit[]
  subscriptions         BillingSubscription[]
  checkoutAttempts      CheckoutAttempt[]
  adminActions          AdminAuditLog[]       @relation("AdminActor")
  adminTargetActions    AdminAuditLog[]       @relation("AdminTarget")

  @@index([plan, subscriptionStatus, createdAt, id])
  @@index([isSuspended, createdAt, id])
  @@index([currentPeriodEnd])
  @@index([gracePeriodEnd])
  @@index([lastActiveAt])
}

model Template {
  id         String     @id @default(uuid())
  userId     String
  name       String
  subject    String
  body       String
  archivedAt DateTime?
  createdAt  DateTime   @default(now())
  user       User       @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  campaigns  Campaign[]

  @@index([userId])
}

model Contact {
  id                  String    @id @default(uuid())
  userId              String
  name                String
  email               String
  company             String?
  jobRole             String?
  notes               String?
  tag                 String?
  archivedAt          DateTime?
  shortlistRemovedAt  DateTime?
  followUpRequestedAt DateTime?
  createdAt           DateTime  @default(now())
  user                User      @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  sends               Send[]

  @@unique([userId, email])
  @@index([userId])
}

model Campaign {
  id                     String      @id @default(uuid())
  userId                 String
  templateId             String
  status                 String
  role                   String      @default("")
  idempotencyKey         String?
  approvedRecipientCount Int         @default(0)
  usesCustomRole         Boolean     @default(false)
  usesRepeatSend         Boolean     @default(false)
  attachmentId           String?

  createdAt              DateTime    @default(now())
  user                   User        @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  template               Template    @relation(fields: [templateId], references: [id])
  sends                  Send[]

  @@unique([userId, idempotencyKey])
  @@index([userId])
}

// Content-free notices survive removal of campaign history.
model AccountNotice {
  id                 String    @id @default(uuid())
  userId             String
  deduplicationKey   String
  campaignIdSnapshot String
  reasonCode         String
  cancelledCount     Int
  createdAt          DateTime  @default(now())
  dismissedAt        DateTime?
  user               User      @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([userId, deduplicationKey])
  @@index([userId, dismissedAt, createdAt])
}

model AccountDeletionJob {
  id                         String    @id @default(uuid())
  userId                     String    @unique
  googleSubjectHash          String?   @unique
  requestedAt                DateTime
  credentialExpiresAt        DateTime
  encryptedRevocationToken   String?

  customerIds                String[]  @default([])
  subscriptionIds            String[]  @default([])
  checkoutRecovery           Json      @default("[]")
  billingRequired            Boolean   @default(false)
  billingRecoveryVersion     Int       @default(0)
  cancellationAttempts       Int       @default(0)
  cancellationFailures       Int       @default(0)
  nextBillingAttemptAt       DateTime  @default(now())
  nextAttemptAt              DateTime  @default(now())
  leaseToken                 String?
  leaseExpiresAt             DateTime?
  failureCode                String?
  purgeFailureCode           String?
  createdAt                  DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt                  DateTime  @updatedAt

  @@index([completedAt, nextAttemptAt, id])
}

model Send {
  historyDeletedAt        DateTime?
  createdAt               DateTime          @default(now())
  recipientEmail          String            @default("")
  recipientName           String            @default("")
  recipientRole           String            @default("")
  recipientCompany        String            @default("")
  templateName            String            @default("")
  subject                 String            @default("")
  body                    String            @default("")
  mimeMessageId           String?           @unique
  deliveryState           DeliveryState     @default(READY)
  attemptedAt             DateTime?
  availableAt             DateTime?
  queueExpiresAt          DateTime?
  claimToken              String?
  leaseExpiresAt          DateTime?
  dispatchGeneration      Int               @default(0)
  dispatchAttempts        Int               @default(0)
  preparationRetries      Int               @default(0)
  credentialRetries       Int               @default(0)
  throttleRetries         Int               @default(0)
  dispatchAttemptedAt     DateTime?
  usageReservation        UsageReservation?
  dispatchedAt            DateTime?
  lastCheckedAt           DateTime?
  replyMarkedAt           DateTime?
  bouncedAt               DateTime?
  sentConfirmedManuallyAt DateTime?

  id             String     @id @default(uuid())
  campaignId     String
  contactId      String
  status         SendStatus @default(QUEUED)
  cancelledAt    DateTime?
  sentAt         DateTime?
  gmailMessageId String?
  gmailThreadId  String?
  error          String?
  campaign       Campaign   @relation(fields: [campaignId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  contact        Contact    @relation(fields: [contactId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([campaignId])
  @@index([contactId])
  @@index([status, sentAt])
  @@index([status, deliveryState, availableAt])
  @@index([deliveryState, leaseExpiresAt])
  @@index([status, queueExpiresAt])
  @@index([deliveryState, attemptedAt, id])
  @@index([deliveryState, createdAt, id])
}

model Attachment {
  rejectedAt       DateTime?
  deletedAt        DateTime?
  storageDeletedAt DateTime?
  id               String     @id @default(uuid())
  userId           String
  fileName         String
  createdAt        DateTime   @default(now())
  campaigns        Campaign[]
  storagePath      String
  user             User       @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([userId])
  @@index([userId, storageDeletedAt, createdAt, id])
}

enum SendStatus {
  QUEUED
  CANCELLED
  SENT
  FAILED
  REPLIED
}

enum DeliveryState {
  READY
  ATTEMPTING
  UNCERTAIN
  DONE
}

// Minimal safeguards retained after permanent message-history deletion.
model DeliveryReceipt {
  deliveryKey    String?  @unique
  id             String   @id @default(uuid())
  userId         String
  recipientEmail String
  createdAt      DateTime
  sentAt         DateTime
  user           User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([userId, sentAt])
  @@index([userId, recipientEmail])
}

enum Plan {
  FREE
  PAID
}

enum SubscriptionStatus {
  NONE
  PENDING
  ACTIVE
  PAST_DUE
  ON_HOLD
  CANCELLED
  EXPIRED
  FAILED
  PAUSED
}

model BillingSubscription {
  id                   String             @id @default(uuid())
  userId               String?
  ownerIdSnapshot      String?
  dodoSubscriptionId   String             @unique
  dodoCustomerId       String
  productId            String
  status               SubscriptionStatus
  periodStart          DateTime?
  periodEnd            DateTime?
  gracePeriodEnd       DateTime?
  cancelAtPeriodEnd    Boolean            @default(false)
  cancelRequestedAt    DateTime?
  currency             String?
  billingCountry       String?
  recurringAmountMinor Int?
  lastEventAt          DateTime?
  settledPaymentId     String?
  paymentConfirmedAt   DateTime?
  createdAt            DateTime           @default(now())
  updatedAt            DateTime           @updatedAt
  user                 User?              @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)

  @@index([userId, createdAt])
  @@index([status, periodEnd])
}

model CheckoutAttempt {
  id              String   @id @default(uuid())
  userId          String?
  ownerIdSnapshot String?
  idempotencyKey  String
  productId       String
  billingCountry  String?
  billingCurrency String?
  dodoSessionId   String?  @unique
  checkoutUrl     String?
  failureCode     String?
  status          String   @default("CREATING")
  expiresAt       DateTime
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime @default(now()) @updatedAt
  user            User?    @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)

  @@unique([userId, idempotencyKey])
  @@index([userId, status, expiresAt])
}

model BillingWebhookEvent {
  id                String    @id @default(uuid())
  webhookId         String    @unique
  eventType         String
  businessId        String
  subscriptionId    String?
  customerId        String?
  paymentId         String?
  occurredAt        DateTime
  receivedAt        DateTime  @default(now())
  processedAt       DateTime?
  nextAttemptAt     DateTime?
  attempts          Int       @default(0)
  processingVersion Int       @default(1)
  state             String    @default("RECEIVED")
  normalizedData    Json
  payloadHash       String
  failureCode       String?

  @@index([state, nextAttemptAt, receivedAt])
  @@index([processedAt, receivedAt, id])
  @@index([subscriptionId, occurredAt])
  @@index([customerId, occurredAt])
}

model AdminAuditLog {
  id               String   @id @default(uuid())
  actorUserId      String?
  targetUserId     String?
  actorIdSnapshot  String
  targetIdSnapshot String?
  action           String
  requestId        String   @unique
  requestHash      String?
  reason           String
  before           Json
  after            Json
  createdAt        DateTime @default(now())
  actor            User?    @relation("AdminActor", fields: [actorUserId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  target           User?    @relation("AdminTarget", fields: [targetUserId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)

  @@index([targetUserId, createdAt])
  @@index([actorUserId, createdAt])
  @@index([action, createdAt])
}

model SystemControl {
  id                     String    @id @default(uuid())
  key                    String    @unique
  gmailProjectPauseUntil DateTime?
  sendingEnabled         Boolean   @default(true)
  paidGatingEnabled      Boolean   @default(false)
  usageCutoverAt         DateTime?
  billingCheckoutEnabled Boolean   @default(false)
  dodoEnvironment        String?
  dodoBusinessId         String?
  updatedAt              DateTime  @updatedAt
}

// Period identity is independent of the current plan's allowance. Daily buckets
// and calendar-month buckets are shared when the effective plan changes.
enum UsagePeriodKind {
  DAILY
  MONTHLY
}

enum ReservationStatus {
  RESERVED
  ATTEMPTING
  UNCERTAIN
  CONFIRMED
  RELEASED
}

model UsagePeriod {
  id                  String             @id @default(uuid())
  userId              String
  key                 String
  kind                UsagePeriodKind
  startsAt            DateTime
  endsAt              DateTime
  operationalEndsAt   DateTime
  sent                Int                @default(0)
  reserved            Int                @default(0)
  importedSent        Int                @default(0)
  importedReserved    Int                @default(0)
  createdAt           DateTime           @default(now())
  user                User               @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  dailyReservations   UsageReservation[] @relation("DailyUsage")
  monthlyReservations UsageReservation[] @relation("MonthlyUsage")

  @@unique([userId, key])
  @@unique([id, userId])
  @@index([userId, kind, startsAt, operationalEndsAt])
}

model UsageReservation {
  id              String            @id @default(uuid())
  userId          String
  deliveryKey     String            @unique
  sendId          String?           @unique
  dailyPeriodId   String
  monthlyPeriodId String
  status          ReservationStatus @default(RESERVED)
  chargedAt       DateTime?
  confirmedAt     DateTime?
  releasedAt      DateTime?
  claimToken      String?
  leaseExpiresAt  DateTime?
  createdAt       DateTime          @default(now())
  user            User              @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  send            Send?             @relation(fields: [sendId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  dailyPeriod     UsagePeriod       @relation("DailyUsage", fields: [dailyPeriodId, userId], references: [id, userId], onDelete: Restrict)
  monthlyPeriod   UsagePeriod       @relation("MonthlyUsage", fields: [monthlyPeriodId, userId], references: [id, userId], onDelete: Restrict)

  @@index([userId, status, chargedAt])
  @@index([userId, dailyPeriodId, status])
  @@index([userId, monthlyPeriodId, status])
  @@index([status, leaseExpiresAt])
}

// No addresses or message content. Stable identity survives Send/Receipt deletion.
model UsageImportEvidence {
  id              String   @id @default(uuid())
  userId          String
  sourceKey       String
  deliveryKey     String?  @unique
  chargedAt       DateTime
  timestampSource String
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  user            User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([userId, sourceKey])
  @@index([userId, chargedAt])
}

model BillingRateLimit {
  id           String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  userId       String
  operation    String
  minuteBucket DateTime
  requestCount Int      @default(1)
  user         User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([userId, operation, minuteBucket])
  @@index([minuteBucket])
}


enum GmailPauseReason {
  RECONNECT_REQUIRED
  OWNER_THROTTLE
  PROVIDER_DAILY_LIMIT
  DOMAIN_POLICY
}

model RateLimitBucket {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  scope         String
  operation     String
  admissions    DateTime[] @default([])
  cleanupAt     DateTime
  @@unique([scope, operation])
  @@index([cleanupAt])
}

Email support

For account, Gmail connection, sending, or billing questions, email{" "} {SUPPORT_EMAIL}. If the link does not open an email app, copy the address into your preferred email service.

Privacy and account requests

import Link from "next/link"; import { PolicyPage } from "@/components/policy-page"; export const metadata = { title: "Help center", description: "Get started with Mailloop and find answers about Gmail, sending, and your email queue.", alternates: { canonical: "/help" }, }; export default function HelpPage() { return (

Set up your outreach, check your queue, and find help when something needs attention. Need a hand? Contact us.

Your first email

  1. Sign in with Google, then check your Gmail connection in{" "} Settings.
  2. Add recipients in Contacts. You can enter a person individually or import a list and review it before saving.
  3. Create a message in Templates. Use{" "} {"{{name}}"}, {"{{company}}"}, and{" "} {"{{role}}"} to personalize it.
  4. In Compose, choose a template and recipients. Review each personal preview before approving the send. Every recipient gets a separate email from your Gmail account.
  5. Follow progress in History and check available sending capacity in Usage.

Common questions

How do I attach my resume?

Upload your PDF in Settings, then select Attach PDF in Compose. Mentioning a resume in your message does not attach it.

Why is Gmail disconnected?

Open Settings and reconnect Gmail, granting the requested sending permission. If your Google Workspace administrator blocks access, ask them for help. Reconnecting does not restart cancelled emails; review History before preparing another send.

What does Sent mean?

Sent means Gmail accepted the email. It does not confirm delivery to the recipient’s inbox. Failed entries in History explain what went wrong.

What should I do with Needs review?

Check your Gmail Sent folder yourself before deciding what to do next. The outcome is uncertain, and Mailloop never automatically resends these messages.

Why can’t I send more emails?

Usage shows your remaining allowance and reset times. Queued emails reserve capacity too. Google applies its own sending limits separately from Mailloop.

Does Mailloop read replies or send follow-ups automatically?

Mailloop does not read your inbox or detect replies. Premium users can mark replies manually in History and use follow-up reminders. Reminders do not send emails; you review and approve each message.

Still need help?

Contact support with the page you were using and the error you saw. For plan and billing details, see{" "} pricing and billing information .

); }

import { ALLOWANCE_RESETS, NO_ROLLOVER, PRICE_DESCRIPTION, PRICE_TAX_DESCRIPTION, REFUND_POLICY, } from "@/lib/pricing"; import { PLANS, ROLE_SHORTCUT_LIMITS } from "@/lib/plans"; import { PolicyPage } from "@/components/policy-page"; export const metadata = { title: "Privacy Policy", alternates: { canonical: "/privacy" }, }; export default function Privacy() { return (

Who we are

Mailloop helps job seekers send personalized, individual emails through their own Gmail account. Czar16 operates Mailloop. For privacy requests or support, contact{" "} [REDACTED_EMAIL].

Information we handle

Google sign-in supplies your Google account identifier, email address, and name. We store your account profile, preferred job roles, reminder preference, and an encrypted Google authorization refresh token. Session cookies keep you signed in. We do not receive your Google password.

We store the contacts you enter or import, templates, campaign history, recipient and message snapshots, delivery outcomes, Gmail message and thread identifiers, and manually recorded replies. Legacy manual evidence and address records are retained. Editing or archiving a contact or template does not erase historical message snapshots. Uploaded resume PDFs are kept in private storage and attached only when you choose to include them.

Website analytics

Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights collect page visits and browser performance measurements to help us understand site use and improve loading and responsiveness. Google Analytics collects page URLs and browser information for website analytics. We do not intentionally send Gmail message contents, recipients, OAuth credentials, or uploaded PDFs to these tools. Browser privacy controls or content blockers may prevent collection.

How Gmail access is used

We use Gmail sending permission to send each approved message individually from your account. Each email gets one sending attempt; failed preparation and rejected sends are not automatically sent again. Mailloop requests Gmail sending permission only and never reads your inbox, threads, or Sent folder. Premium users use Mark replied manually; this stops reminders for that contact. Mailloop does not detect replies. Gmail acceptance status reports that Gmail accepted an email, not guaranteed recipient delivery. Uncertain sends stay Needs review and are never automatically resent. Premium follow-up reminders use your choice of 3, 7, or 14 elapsed days since sending unless a reply is marked. You decide whom to follow up with and approve each message. Reminders never send automatically.

Mailloop’s use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adheres to the{" "} Google API Services User Data Policy {" "} and{" "} Google Workspace API user data policy , including their Limited Use requirements. Google user data is not sold, used for advertising, or used to train generalized AI or machine learning models. Human access is limited to circumstances allowed by those policies, such as your specific consent for support, security investigations, or legal requirements.

Sharing and disclosure of Google user data

Hosting and PostgreSQL database providers process application data to operate the service. Private Vercel Blob storage processes uploaded PDFs in production; local development uses local files. Inngest processes account and send identifiers and background job outcomes for delivery and maintenance. Google processes emails, recipients, and attachments when sent through Gmail. Recipients receive the message and any attached PDF. These providers process data under their applicable terms. We may disclose data when required by law or to address abuse and protect the service.

Dodo Payments is our payment processor and Merchant of Record. Optional subscriptions use its hosted checkout and customer portal. We send your account name, email, and internal billing identifiers to associate the transaction with your account. We retain customer and subscription identifiers, checkout identifiers and outcomes, billing country and currency, recurring amounts, verified billing dates, cancellation state, and minimal verified payment-event records for access checks, cancellation recovery, and reconciliation. Card details stay with the payment provider; Mailloop does not store them. Real charges are not enabled.

To enforce request limits and diagnose failures, we retain recent request timestamps, internal account and job identifiers, fixed error categories, provider status codes, counters, and operational timestamps. Operational logs exclude authorization tokens, recipient addresses, subjects, message bodies, and raw provider responses. Request-limit records expire and are cleaned up daily. Minimal recovery records may remain after account deletion until pending cleanup is resolved.

  • Vercel (application hosting): Our server code runs on Vercel and processes your Google account profile, authorization credentials, contacts, email content, and delivery results to authenticate you and send the emails you approve.
  • Neon (PostgreSQL database): Stores your Google account identifier, name, email address, encrypted Google refresh token, and Gmail message and thread identifiers, together with your contacts, templates, and campaign history, so your account and sending history remain available.
  • Vercel Blob (private file storage): Stores the resume PDFs you upload and their storage metadata. A PDF is sent through Gmail only when you choose to attach it.
  • Inngest (background job coordination): Processes internal account and send identifiers, job timing, and background job outcomes to coordinate sending and account maintenance. OAuth tokens, email bodies, and attachments are not included in Inngest event payloads or step results.
  • Google (Google sign-in and Gmail API): Processes authorization credentials to authenticate you and authorize sending. When you approve an email, we transfer the sender and recipient addresses, subject, message body, and any selected attachment to Gmail to send it from your account.
  • The recipients you select: Receive your sender name and email address, message subject and body, and any attachment you choose to include. Each email is sent individually.

Our infrastructure providers process data to operate Mailloop under their applicable service terms. We do not sell or rent Google user data, share it with advertising networks or data brokers, or transfer it for generalized AI or machine learning model training. Disclosure to authorities or other parties is limited to what is necessary to comply with applicable law or investigate security issues or abuse, consistent with Google’s Limited Use requirements.

How we protect sensitive data

We use the following safeguards to protect Google user data, authorization credentials, email content, and uploaded resumes against unauthorized access or disclosure:

  • Encryption in transit: The production website uses HTTPS, and communication with Google’s authorization and Gmail APIs uses HTTPS to protect data during transmission.
  • Encrypted stored credentials: Google refresh tokens are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before being stored in the database. The encryption key is held in server-side environment configuration, separately from the database records.
  • Server-side credential handling: Gmail API calls and token decryption run on the server. OAuth tokens and service secrets are not included in client-side application data or account exports. We never receive or store your Google password.
  • Account access controls: Access to account data requires authentication and is scoped to the signed-in user’s account. Background service callbacks use service authentication.
  • Private resume storage: Uploaded PDFs are stored in private Vercel Blob storage. Resume downloads require an authenticated owner, and the server checks account ownership before loading a file for sending.
  • Limited operational records: Application logs and background job event payloads and step results exclude OAuth tokens, email bodies, and raw email messages.

These safeguards reduce the risk of unauthorized access; no system can guarantee absolute security. Retention, account deletion, and Google access revocation are described below.

Your controls and retention

Settings lets you download a JSON export of your profile, preferences, contacts, templates, message history, manual evidence, legacy address records and reasons, minimal delivery receipts, and attachment metadata. It excludes credentials and private storage locations. Your current resume can be downloaded separately. You can revoke Mailloop’s Google access through{" "} Google account connections ; revocation does not delete your Mailloop data.

Delete history in Settings permanently removes completed message content and its follow-up reminders. Legacy address records and reasons survive contact and history deletion until account deletion; they do not block sending. Queued and unresolved deliveries remain, and Gmail emails are unchanged. We retain minimal delivery receipts containing your account ID, recipient address, original creation time, and successful-send time until account deletion. These preserve sending limits and warnings for previously emailed addresses. Empty campaign records retain submission keys to prevent duplicate sends. While a campaign has queued or unresolved deliveries, hidden completed rows retain recipient roles and original recipient counts to enforce plan eligibility; their message content is removed. A later history cleanup removes these rows once the campaign is terminal.

Account deletion disables access immediately and cancels emails that have not begun delivery. Already sending or uncertain deliveries cannot be recalled. The deletion request cannot be undone. You cannot sign in or create another Mailloop account with the same Google account while deletion is pending. Billing cancellation is attempted immediately. After a minimum 15-minute waiting period, the next daily cleanup run attempts Google authorization revocation and begins irreversible deletion of ordinary profile and content data and owned PDFs. The maximum target is 30 elapsed days from the original request, including requests already pending. Billing and storage outages do not hold up database content cleanup. An independent recovery record retains only original owner and provider identifiers, checkout/cancellation state, stage timestamps, and a keyed Google identity hash while cleanup remains unresolved. Any temporary encrypted revocation credential is scheduled for erasure one day before day 30, even if Google is unavailable. A missed or delayed daily run can delay erasure. Failed external cleanup remains retryable in daily runs; provider outages may delay completion. Minimal billing or legal evidence may remain where narrowly necessary for reconciliation or legal obligations. Outages may delay cleanup attempts; failures are retried in daily runs. Deleting Mailloop does not remove emails from Gmail or recipients’ inboxes. Provider-managed logs and backups follow the relevant provider’s retention practices; this policy does not promise a particular backup deletion deadline.

We retain account data while your account exists. Older PDFs can be removed once replaced or removed from Settings and no pending or uncertain delivery needs them. Historical attachment metadata may remain until account deletion. Contact us for access, correction, or privacy questions.

Plans and subscription controls

Premium costs {PRICE_DESCRIPTION}. {PRICE_TAX_DESCRIPTION} Billing country determines eligibility; checkout shows the final quote. Free includes {PLANS.FREE.monthlyEmails} emails/month and{" "} {PLANS.FREE.dailyEmails}/UTC day; Premium includes{" "} {PLANS.PAID.monthlyEmails}/month and {PLANS.PAID.dailyEmails}/UTC day.{" "} Contact job roles are unrestricted. Free includes{" "} {ROLE_SHORTCUT_LIMITS.free} saved role shortcuts and Premium includes{" "} {ROLE_SHORTCUT_LIMITS.premium}. Premium can override recipient roles in Compose. Compare all features and limits on{" "} Pricing. Your workspace shows the allowances enforced during rollout.

{ALLOWANCE_RESETS} Queued emails reserve capacity; manually sent follow-up emails consume allowances. {NO_ROLLOVER}

Premium renews monthly. Request period-end cancellation in{" "} Settings; cancellation remains pending until verified, and verified access continues through the current period. Failed renewals retain access only until a verified grace deadline shown in Settings. {REFUND_POLICY}

Abuse or security issues may lead to suspension. Suspension does not cancel billing; billing management, export, deletion, and support remain accessible. You are responsible for honoring recipients’ requests not to be contacted. Premium support emails at{" "} [REDACTED_EMAIL] are prioritized without a response-time or 24/7 promise.

Changes

We will update this page when our practices change. Material changes to Google data use require appropriate notice and consent before that new use.

); }

Using Mailloop

Mailloop is operated by Czar16. By using the service, you agree to these terms and acknowledge the Privacy Policy. Use a Google account you control and have authority to authorize. You are responsible for your recipients, message content, attachments, and compliance with applicable laws and Google’s policies. Contact{" "} [REDACTED_EMAIL] for help.

Acceptable outreach

Use Mailloop for lawful, relevant, personalized outreach. Do not send spam, deceptive messages, phishing, malware, harassment, or unlawful content. Do not impersonate others, misuse contact information, evade limits, or attempt unauthorized access. You are responsible for honoring recipients’ requests not to be contacted. You must have the rights and legal basis needed to use the contact information and content you provide. Access may be restricted or suspended for abuse or security reasons. Suspension does not automatically cancel a subscription; manage or cancel it in Settings.

Approval, limits, and delivery

You approve campaigns in Compose. Each recipient receives their own email; batches do not use CC or BCC. Your workspace shows your plan's daily and monthly sending allowances, including queued reservations. {ALLOWANCE_RESETS} {NO_ROLLOVER} Manually sent follow-up emails also consume allowances. Where plan limits are disabled, the legacy limit is {DAILY_EMAIL_LIMIT} emails per rolling 24 hours. {copy.description} {SEND_TIMING_DESCRIPTION} Google may deny delivery. Uncertain attempts retain their period's capacity and are never automatically sent again.

Google applies its own sending limits separately from your Mailloop allowance. Provider limits or service issues may pause queued work. Each email gets one sending attempt. Failed preparation or a definite Gmail rejection ends that email without another automatic attempt; confirmed non-delivery releases its reserved allowance. Revoked credentials or missing permission require you to reconnect Gmail; a workspace policy block may require your Google Workspace administrator’s help. Credential or policy pauses cancel remaining emails that have not begun delivery. Reconnecting does not restore cancelled emails, increase your allowance, or remove an account suspension. Request limits also apply to checkout, subscription management, campaign submission, imports, and exports.

Queued emails can be cancelled only before delivery begins. Actively sending and uncertain deliveries cannot be stopped or recalled. A successful Gmail API response does not guarantee arrival, inbox placement, a reply, or a job opportunity. Timings are estimates. Premium users use the Mark replied button manually; marking a reply stops reminders for that contact. Mailloop does not read your inbox or detect replies. SENT means Gmail accepted submission, not confirmed recipient delivery. Uncertain delivery stays Needs review. You can check Gmail Sent yourself; Mailloop offers no confirmation or resend control for uncertain sends. Premium follow-up reminders use 3, 7, or 14 elapsed days since sending unless you mark a reply. You decide whom to follow up with and approve each message. Reminders never automatically send messages.

Plans, payment, and cancellation

Premium costs {PRICE_DESCRIPTION}. {PRICE_TAX_DESCRIPTION} Billing country determines eligibility; Dodo checkout shows the final quote. Dodo Payments is the payment processor and Merchant of Record. Checkout is available only when enabled. A live checkout charges real money and renews according to the subscription terms.

Free includes Lavender (light) and Nightbloom (dark) themes. Premium also includes exclusive Chalk (light) and Obsidian (dark) themes, independently of email allowance rollout. When Premium access ends, the active theme returns to Lavender or Nightbloom in the same light or dark mode; your saved Chalk or Obsidian preference is retained.

Premium renews monthly. Request cancellation at period end in{" "} Settings; the request remains pending until verified. Verified Premium access continues to the end of the current period. A failed renewal retains access only through a verified grace deadline shown in Settings; otherwise Premium access ends. Suspension does not cancel billing.

{REFUND_POLICY}

Premium email support requests at{" "} [REDACTED_EMAIL] are prioritized, without a guaranteed response time or 24/7 support promise.

Service limitations

The service depends on Google, hosting, storage, database, and background processing providers. It may be unavailable, delayed, changed, or discontinued. To the extent allowed by applicable law, it is provided as available without warranties of uninterrupted operation or guaranteed results. Czar16 is not responsible for indirect losses or missed opportunities arising from use of the service, to the extent permitted by law. These terms do not limit rights or liabilities that applicable law does not allow us to exclude.

Your data and ending use

You retain rights to your content and authorize the processing needed to provide the features you request. You can export your data, revoke Google access, or request account deletion in Settings. The request immediately disables access and cancels emails that have not begun delivery. Billing cancellation is attempted immediately. After a minimum 15-minute waiting period, the next daily cleanup run attempts Google authorization revocation and begins irreversible deletion of ordinary profile and content data and owned PDFs. The maximum target is 30 elapsed days from the original request, including requests already pending. Billing recovery does not delay ordinary-data cleanup. Database content cleanup proceeds even if storage deletion fails; remaining storage work is retried. Only identity and billing records narrowly necessary for cancellation recovery, preventing reactivation, reconciliation, or legal obligations may remain. Minimal recovery records remain until unfinished cleanup is resolved. Outages may delay a cleanup attempt; failures are retried in daily runs. The request cannot be undone, and you cannot sign in or create another Mailloop account with the same Google account while deletion is pending. Account deletion does not delete emails from Gmail or recipients’ inboxes. Download any data you need before requesting deletion.

Updates and questions

We may update these terms as the service changes and will identify the effective date on this page. For questions or to raise a concern, email [REDACTED_EMAIL].
